GV-PM-003 — Policy Acknowledgment & Staff Attestation

1. Policy Header

2. Purpose

This policy establishes the requirements for documented acknowledgment and attestation by all workforce members upon the issuance, revision, or assignment of agency policies. Acknowledgment ensures that all individuals subject to a policy have received, read, and understood their obligations under that policy. This policy supports the agency's compliance with CMS Conditions of Participation, OIG Compliance Program Guidance, and California state employment and licensing requirements by creating an auditable record of workforce policy awareness and accountability.

3. Scope

This policy applies to:

All employees of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. (full-time, part-time, and per diem)

All contracted clinical and non-clinical staff performing services on behalf of the agency

All members of the Governing Body

All students, interns, and volunteers functioning within the agency

All agency leadership, including the Administrator, Director of Nursing, and Compliance Officer

This policy does not apply to external vendors or business associates who are not directly performing services under agency supervision, except where a specific policy expressly requires their acknowledgment.

4. Policy Statement

4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall require documented acknowledgment of all agency policies by all individuals within scope of each policy, as a condition of employment, contract, and Governing Body membership.

4.2 Policy acknowledgment shall occur:

Within 14 calendar days of initial hire or new appointment for all policies applicable to the individual's role

Within 14 calendar days of the effective date of any new policy applicable to the individual's role

Within 14 calendar days of the effective date of any substantive revision to an existing applicable policy

Within 14 calendar days of any role change that expands the scope of policies applicable to the individual

4.3 Acknowledgment shall be documented using the standardized Policy Acknowledgment Form (see Appendix A of the applicable policy, or the general acknowledgment form in Appendix A of this policy). Electronic acknowledgment through the agency's designated platform is an acceptable alternative to paper forms, provided the system captures the individual's identity, date, and a confirmation of receipt and understanding.

4.4 The Administrator shall maintain a centralized policy acknowledgment tracking log for all agency policies and all individuals within scope. This log shall be current at all times and available for CMS survey review.

4.5 Non-compliance with acknowledgment requirements shall be escalated per Section 6.4 of this policy. Failure to acknowledge assigned policies within required timeframes may result in corrective action, up to and including suspension from patient care duties pending completion.

4.6 Acknowledgment of a policy does not substitute for training. Where a policy requires training in addition to acknowledgment, both requirements must be independently satisfied and documented.

4.7 Governing Body members and senior leadership shall acknowledge all REQUIRED-tier and Tier 4 — Privileged policies within 14 calendar days of appointment and within 14 calendar days of any revision.

5. Definitions

6. Procedures

6.1 Policy Assignment and Acknowledgment Trigger Events

6.2 Acknowledgment Completion

6.3 Acknowledgment Tracking and Reporting

6.4 Non-Compliance and Escalation

6.5 Acknowledgment During Leaves of Absence

7. Documentation Requirements

8. Compliance & Audit Considerations

8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

8.2 What Surveyors and Auditors Will Look For

CMS surveyors and OIG auditors will specifically examine:

Evidence that workforce members have acknowledged the policies governing their scope of practice and compliance obligations, particularly REQUIRED-tier clinical, compliance, and patient safety policies.

Evidence that the Governing Body has acknowledged all REQUIRED-tier governance policies, including this policy.

Currency and completeness of the Acknowledgment Tracking Log.

Evidence that non-compliance with acknowledgment requirements is tracked and acted upon.

Consistency between the agency's stated acknowledgment requirements (in individual policy documents) and the tracking system maintained by the Administrator.

8.3 Common Failure Points

9. References

9.1 Federal Regulations

9.2 OIG Guidance

9.3 Cross-Referenced Agency Policies

10. Training & Acknowledgment Requirements

10.1 All individuals within the scope of this policy shall receive orientation to the acknowledgment process as part of new employee orientation or Governing Body onboarding, conducted by the Administrator or designee.

10.2 All individuals within scope shall acknowledge this policy (GV-PM-003) within 14 calendar days of their effective date of hire, appointment, or this policy's effective date.

10.3 Annual refresher on acknowledgment obligations shall be incorporated into the agency's annual mandatory training program per policy HR-TD-001.

11. Version Control

11.1 This policy is maintained under the agency's enterprise policy lifecycle management system per policy EN-LC-001.

11.2 Only the most current approved version of this policy is valid for any operational, compliance, or regulatory purpose.

11.3 Any substantive revision requires Governing Body approval (documented in meeting minutes), re-acknowledgment by all personnel within scope within 14 calendar days, and update to the enterprise policy index per EN-TG-001.

11.4 Non-substantive revisions may be approved by the Administrator with notification to the Governing Body at the next regular meeting and do not require re-acknowledgment.

GV-PM-004 — Communication & Notification Standards

1. Policy Header

2. Purpose

This policy establishes the standards governing internal and external communication and notification at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. Effective communication is essential to patient safety, regulatory compliance, operational continuity, and workforce accountability. This policy defines timeliness requirements, acceptable communication channels, escalation protocols, and documentation obligations for all categories of organizational communication, ensuring that critical information reaches the appropriate individuals in a reliable, accurate, and auditable manner.

3. Scope

This policy applies to:

All employees of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. at all levels

All contracted clinical and non-clinical personnel performing services on behalf of the agency

The Administrator, Director of Nursing, Compliance Officer, and all department leads

The Governing Body, with respect to notifications directed to or from the Governing Body

All communications involving patients, families, referral sources, payers, and regulatory bodies

This policy does not govern clinical documentation standards (see CL-CD-001) or HIPAA-specific privacy and security requirements for PHI communications (see CO-HP-001, CO-HP-002), which are addressed in their respective policies but must be read in conjunction with this policy.

4. Policy Statement

4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall maintain clear, timely, and documented communication channels at all organizational levels to support patient safety, compliance, and operational effectiveness.

4.2 All communications that require action, document a material decision, or affect patient care or regulatory compliance shall be documented in writing (paper or electronic) and retained per the agency's record retention requirements in policy CO-HP-007.

4.3 Verbal communications regarding patient care, compliance concerns, or operational decisions shall be confirmed in writing within the timeframes specified in Section 6 of this policy.

4.4 All communications involving PHI shall comply with HIPAA privacy and security requirements per policies CO-HP-001 and CO-HP-002. PHI shall not be transmitted via unsecured channels, including personal email or unencrypted text messaging, without explicit patient authorization or a documented operational emergency.

4.5 The agency shall maintain an escalation protocol ensuring that urgent clinical, compliance, and regulatory matters are communicated to the appropriate leadership level without delay. No individual shall impede or delay the escalation of a patient safety or compliance concern.

4.6 Regulatory agencies, accrediting bodies, and government authorities shall receive all required notifications within the timeframes mandated by applicable law or regulation, and responses shall be coordinated through the Administrator with oversight from the Compliance Officer.

4.7 All staff are obligated to communicate concerns about patient safety, compliance, or operational risk through established channels and are protected from retaliation for doing so per policy CO-CP-005.

6. Procedures

6.1.1 — Routine Internal Communication

6.1.2 — Urgent and Critical Internal Notifications

6.1.3 — Policy and Operational Notification

6.2 External Communication Standards

6.2.3 — Payer and Revenue Cycle Communication

10.2 Annual refresher training shall be incorporated into the agency's mandatory training program per policy HR-TD-001.

10.3 All individuals within the scope of this policy shall acknowledge this policy within 14 calendar days of hire, appointment, or the policy's effective date per policy GV-PM-003.

GV-PM-005 — Stakeholder Grievance & Feedback Management

1. Policy Header

2. Purpose

This policy establishes the process for receiving, documenting, investigating, resolving, and trending grievances and feedback from patients, families, staff, referral sources, and other stakeholders of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. A robust grievance and feedback management program supports patient rights, workforce engagement, quality improvement, and regulatory compliance. This policy integrates with the agency's QAPI program and patient rights framework to ensure that all concerns are treated seriously, addressed promptly, and used to drive continuous improvement.

3. Scope

This policy applies to:

All patients receiving services from Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc.

All family members, legal representatives, and caregivers acting on behalf of patients

All agency employees and contracted staff

Referral sources, physicians, discharge planners, and care coordination partners

Community members or organizations with concerns about agency practices

All agency leadership, including the Administrator, Director of Nursing, and Compliance Officer

This policy applies to all types of grievances and feedback, including those received in person, by telephone, in writing, electronically, or through third parties (e.g., regulatory hotlines, ombudsman offices).

4. Policy Statement

4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall maintain an accessible, non-retaliatory, and responsive grievance and feedback management process that ensures all concerns from patients, families, staff, and other stakeholders are received, documented, investigated, and resolved in a timely and respectful manner.

4.2 Patients and families shall be informed of their right to file a grievance and the process for doing so at the time of admission, per policy CL-PR-001 (Patient Rights & Responsibilities), and shall not be subject to retaliation, discrimination, or changes in care as a result of filing a grievance.

4.3 All grievances shall be acknowledged within 5 business days of receipt and resolved or formally responded to within 30 calendar days of receipt, unless the nature of the grievance requires a longer investigation, in which case interim status updates shall be provided every 14 calendar days.

4.4 Staff grievances and complaints shall be received through the process defined in this policy and in policy HR-ER-003 (Employee Grievance & Complaint Process). Staff shall not be subject to retaliation for filing a good-faith grievance, per policy CO-CP-005.

4.5 All grievances and feedback shall be logged in the agency's Grievance and Feedback Register and trended quarterly as part of the QAPI program (policy QA-PG-001) to identify systemic issues and opportunities for improvement.

4.6 Grievances alleging abuse, neglect, exploitation, or HIPAA violations shall be immediately escalated to the Compliance Officer and handled per their respective specialized policies (CL-PR-006, CO-HP-003).

4.7 The Administrator shall report grievance volume, resolution rates, and trend data to the Governing Body at each quarterly meeting as part of the operational oversight report.

5. Definitions

6. Procedures

6.1 Receiving and Logging Grievances

6.2 Triage and Escalation

6.3 Investigation and Resolution

6.4 Staff Grievances

6.5 Trending, Reporting, and QAPI Integration

10.2 Clinical staff shall receive specific training on informing patients and families of their right to file a grievance and providing contact information for the Grievance Coordinator.

10.3 Annual refresher training on grievance handling shall be included in the agency's mandatory training program per policy HR-TD-001.

10.4 All individuals within scope shall acknowledge this policy within 14 calendar days of hire or appointment, and within 14 calendar days of any substantive revision, per policy GV-PM-003.

GV-EA-001 — Interagency Agreements & Contracts

1. Policy Header

2. Purpose

This policy establishes the requirements for initiating, reviewing, approving, executing, monitoring, and renewing contracts and interagency agreements between Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. and third-party service providers, subcontractors, referral entities, staffing agencies, vendors, and other external organizations. Effective contract governance protects the agency from legal and regulatory risk, ensures that contracted parties meet applicable compliance standards, and supports the agency's obligations under 42 CFR Part 484 and applicable California state law. This policy ensures that no third-party arrangement compromises patient safety, regulatory compliance, or the agency's legal accountability.

3. Scope

This policy applies to:

All contracts for services provided to or on behalf of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. by third parties, including but not limited to: clinical staffing agencies, therapy contractors, DME suppliers, billing companies, laboratory services, social work contractors, and IT vendors

All interagency service agreements with hospitals, skilled nursing facilities, physician practices, and community organizations

All Business Associate Agreements (BAAs) as defined under HIPAA (governed jointly with CO-HP-005)

All managed care and payer contracts

The Administrator, Compliance Officer, and any department lead with authority to negotiate or recommend contracts

The Governing Body, with respect to its approval authority over material contracts

This policy does not govern employment contracts for direct employees (see HR domain policies), patient care plans, or physician orders.

4. Policy Statement

4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall not enter into any contract or interagency agreement for services affecting the agency's operations, patient care, or compliance obligations without written documentation reviewed and approved by the Administrator and, where required by Section 6.2, the Governing Body.

4.2 All contracts shall be reviewed for compliance with applicable federal and state laws prior to execution, including Anti-Kickback Statute requirements (42 U.S.C. § 1320a-7b), Stark Law (42 U.S.C. § 1395nn), HIPAA, and CMS Conditions of Participation.

4.3 All contractors and contracted entities performing services that directly affect patient care or that access PHI shall be screened against the OIG List of Excluded Individuals/Entities (LEIE) and SAM exclusion database prior to engagement and monthly thereafter, per policy HR-TA-003.

4.4 All contracts with entities accessing PHI shall include a valid Business Associate Agreement per policy CO-HP-005.

4.5 All contracts shall include provisions establishing: (a) the scope of services; (b) quality and performance standards; (c) compliance obligations and audit rights; (d) confidentiality and data protection requirements; (e) indemnification and liability allocation; (f) termination rights; and (g) record retention requirements consistent with policy CO-HP-007.

4.6 No individual staff member shall independently execute a contract on behalf of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. without written authorization from the Administrator.

4.7 All active contracts shall be maintained in the agency's Contract Register and reviewed no less than annually to assess performance, compliance, and renewal terms.

GV-EA-002 — Community Liaison & Public Relations

1. Policy Header

2. Purpose

This policy defines the approach of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. to community engagement, referral source relationship management, and public communications. Effective community liaison and public relations activities support the agency's mission by building trust within the communities it serves, developing ethical referral relationships, and maintaining a positive public reputation consistent with the agency's compliance obligations. This policy ensures that all community and public relations activities comply with the Anti-Kickback Statute, Stark Law, CMS marketing guidelines, and applicable California state advertising standards.

3. Scope

This policy applies to:

The Administrator and all staff engaged in external marketing, community outreach, or referral development activities

Clinical staff who interact with referral sources, discharge planners, or community partners in their professional capacity

Contracted marketing personnel or agencies retained by Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc.

All Governing Body members engaged in public representation of the agency

Any communications, events, materials, or activities conducted in the name of or on behalf of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc.

4. Policy Statement

4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall engage with the community, referral sources, and the public in a manner that is truthful, ethical, compliant with applicable law, and consistent with the agency's mission of providing high-quality home health services.

4.2 All marketing materials, public communications, and community outreach activities representing the agency shall be reviewed and approved by the Administrator prior to distribution or publication. Materials shall not contain false, misleading, or unsubstantiated claims about the agency's services, quality outcomes, or credentials.

4.3 No remuneration — including gifts, meals, entertainment, payments, or any item of value — shall be provided to referral sources, physicians, discharge planners, or their staff in exchange for, or to induce or reward, referrals to the agency. All interactions with referral sources shall comply with the Anti-Kickback Statute (42 U.S.C. § 1320a-7b) and Stark Law (42 U.S.C. § 1395nn), as governed by policy CO-FA-001.

4.4 The agency may provide nominal educational materials, agency informational materials, or de minimis items of no more than $15 in value per instance and $75 per year per source (consistent with OIG guidance), provided these are not conditioned on referrals and are offered uniformly.

4.5 The Administrator is the sole authorized spokesperson for Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. in communications with media, regulatory bodies, and the general public, unless the Administrator expressly delegates this authority in writing per policy GV-PM-004.

4.6 All social media activities conducted in the name of the agency shall comply with policy IT-UP-003. Staff shall not make public statements about the agency's operations, clinical outcomes, or patients on personal or professional social media accounts in a manner that could identify patients, disclose PHI, or misrepresent the agency.

4.7 The agency shall participate in community health initiatives, local coalitions, and professional associations in a manner that advances patient access, health literacy, and the visibility of home health services, without compromising the agency's compliance obligations.

GV-EA-003 — Legal Counsel Engagement & Oversight

1. Policy Header

2. Purpose

This policy establishes the requirements and standards for engaging, managing, and overseeing legal counsel retained by Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. Legal counsel plays a critical role in protecting the agency's legal interests, ensuring regulatory compliance, managing litigation risk, and supporting governance decision-making. This policy ensures that legal resources are engaged appropriately, that attorney-client privilege is preserved, that legal expenditures are authorized, and that the Governing Body receives timely notification of material legal matters.

3. Scope

This policy applies to:

The Administrator and all senior leadership who may identify needs for legal counsel

The Compliance Officer, with respect to legal matters arising from compliance investigations

The Governing Body, with respect to Tier 4 — Privileged legal matters requiring board-level oversight

All external legal counsel retained by the agency

All agency staff who may be contacted by legal counsel or asked to provide information in connection with legal matters

This policy applies to all types of legal matters, including regulatory compliance, contract review, employment law, litigation, government investigations, HIPAA matters, and corporate governance.

4. Policy Statement

4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall retain qualified legal counsel with expertise in healthcare regulatory law, home health agency operations, and California state law to advise the agency on legal matters, as needed.

4.2 The Administrator is the primary point of contact for engaging and directing external legal counsel, except in matters where the Governing Body exercises direct legal oversight (Tier 4 matters). The Compliance Officer shall be involved in all legal matters with compliance implications.

4.3 No staff member shall engage legal counsel on behalf of the agency, execute a legal retainer agreement, or authorize legal fees without written authorization from the Administrator.

4.4 Attorney-client privilege attaches to communications between the agency's authorized representatives and legal counsel made for the purpose of obtaining or providing legal advice. All personnel shall take steps to protect the confidentiality of privileged communications and shall not disclose them without authorization from the Administrator or Legal Counsel.

4.5 The Governing Body shall be notified of any material legal matter, defined as any matter that could result in a financial exposure exceeding $10,000, regulatory action, exclusion from Medicare or Medicaid, or reputational harm to the agency. Notification shall occur at the earliest practicable time, not to exceed 5 business days from the Administrator's awareness.

4.6 All legal matters and associated costs shall be documented and tracked in the agency's Legal Matter Register. The Administrator shall report legal matter status and associated costs to the Governing Body at each quarterly meeting.

4.7 Legal counsel retained for compliance investigations operates under direction of the Compliance Officer, with the Administrator's authorization, to preserve privilege and independence.

GV-EA-004 — Agency Licensure & Certification Maintenance

1. Policy Header

2. Purpose

This policy establishes the requirements for maintaining continuous, uninterrupted licensure, Medicare certification, Medicaid enrollment, and any applicable accreditation credentials for Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. The agency's legal authority to operate and to receive reimbursement from federal and state healthcare programs depends entirely on the currency and validity of these credentials. A lapse in any required license or certification — even for a single day — may result in termination of the agency's Medicare provider agreement, loss of reimbursement, state enforcement action, inability to admit new patients, and potential Condition-level deficiency under 42 CFR § 484.100. This policy ensures that all required credentials are tracked, renewed timely, and maintained in a state of continuous validity, and that the Governing Body exercises its oversight responsibility to confirm the agency's credential status at each quarterly meeting as required by policy GV-GB-001, Section 6.2.1.2.

3. Scope

This policy applies to:

The Governing Body of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. (oversight and quarterly verification)

The Agency Administrator (primary accountability for credential maintenance)

The Compliance Officer (regulatory monitoring and compliance verification)

The Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager (clinical certification and accreditation support)

Any administrative staff assigned responsibility for license renewal processing, application submission, or credential file maintenance

This policy governs the following agency-level credentials:

California Home Health Agency License issued by the California Department of Health Care Access and Information (HCAI) — License No. 406412878

Medicare Certification (CMS Certification Number / CCN) issued by the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services

Medicaid (Medi-Cal) Provider Enrollment, if applicable

National accreditation, if applicable (e.g., ACHC, CHAP, Joint Commission)

Any additional state or local permits, registrations, or authorizations required for the agency to operate lawfully within its defined service area

This policy does not govern individual employee licensure or certification (see HR-TA-004) or physician credentialing. It applies exclusively to agency-level credentials.

4. Policy Statement

4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall maintain current, valid, and uninterrupted licensure, certification, and enrollment with all applicable federal, state, and local regulatory authorities at all times as a condition of its legal authority to operate and to participate in federal and state healthcare programs.

4.2 The Administrator is directly accountable to the Governing Body for the maintenance and timely renewal of all agency credentials. No credential shall be allowed to lapse, expire, or become inactive without immediate corrective action and Governing Body notification.

4.3 The Administrator shall maintain a centralized Agency Credential Register (Appendix A) that documents every required agency-level credential, including the issuing authority, credential number, effective date, expiration date, renewal deadline, and current status.

4.4 Renewal applications for all credentials shall be submitted no later than 90 calendar days before the expiration date of each credential, unless the issuing authority specifies a different renewal window, in which case the issuing authority's timeline shall be followed.

4.5 The Administrator shall verify the agency's credential status at each quarterly Governing Body meeting and present documented confirmation that all credentials are current and valid, per policy GV-GB-001, Section 6.2.1.2.

4.6 The Compliance Officer shall independently monitor regulatory changes, licensing requirements, and certification standards that may affect the agency's credential obligations and shall notify the Administrator within 7 calendar days of identifying any new or changed requirement.

4.7 Any communication from a licensing, certification, or accreditation body — including routine correspondence, deficiency notifications, survey announcements, enforcement actions, or requests for information — shall be immediately forwarded to the Administrator and Compliance Officer and responded to within the timeframes specified by the issuing authority.

4.8 The Governing Body shall be notified immediately — within 24 hours — of any event that threatens the continuity of any agency credential, including but not limited to: (a) a credential approaching expiration without a submitted renewal; (b) a denial of renewal application; (c) a regulatory enforcement action threatening suspension or revocation; (d) a change in regulatory requirements affecting eligibility; (e) a state survey resulting in an Immediate Jeopardy finding.

4.9 All credential documents, renewal applications, correspondence with regulatory bodies, and survey-related records shall be maintained in the agency's credential file and retained for a minimum of 7 years per policy CO-HP-007.

4.10 Only the most current approved version of this policy shall be considered valid. Any revision requires re-acknowledgment by all personnel within scope within 14 calendar days of the revised effective date.

5. Definitions

6. Procedures

6.1 Agency Credential Register Establishment and Maintenance

6.2 California Home Health Agency License Maintenance

6.3 Medicare Certification Maintenance

6.4 Medi-Cal Provider Enrollment Maintenance

6.5 Accreditation Maintenance (If Applicable)

6.6 Renewal Application Quality Control

6.7 Credential Display and Accessibility

6.8 Escalation and Exception Handling

7. Documentation Requirements

8. Compliance & Audit Considerations

8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

8.2 What Surveyors and Auditors Will Look For

CMS surveyors conducting a standard survey under the State Operations Manual (SOM) Appendix B will specifically verify:

Evidence that the agency holds a current, valid state license. Surveyors will request a copy of the current California home health agency license and verify it is not expired. They will also verify that the license is displayed in the agency's principal office. An expired or suspended license is a threshold finding that may terminate the survey process and trigger immediate CMS notification.

Evidence that the agency's Medicare certification is in good standing. Surveyors will verify the CCN and cross-reference the agency's PECOS enrollment status. Any discrepancy between the agency's reported certification status and CMS records is a critical finding.

Evidence that the agency responds to survey findings. Surveyors will review prior survey history and verify that Plans of Correction were submitted timely and that corrective actions were implemented and sustained.

Evidence that the Governing Body monitors the agency's credential status. Surveyors will review Governing Body minutes for documented credential verification. Minutes that do not reference licensure or certification status reviews may result in a finding of inadequate governance oversight.

Evidence that the agency reports required changes to CMS and the state. Surveyors will verify that changes in address, ownership, administrator, or services were reported as required. Unreported changes are a common deficiency.

Evidence of accreditation currency (if the agency holds accreditation). If the agency relies on accreditation for deemed status, surveyors will verify that accreditation is current and that the accrediting organization's most recent survey results are on file.

8.3 Common Failure Points

9. References

9.1 Federal Regulations

9.2 CMS Guidance

9.3 State Requirements

9.4 Cross-Referenced Agency Policies

10. Training & Acknowledgment Requirements

10.1 The Administrator and all administrative staff responsible for credential maintenance shall receive training on this policy within 14 calendar days of assuming credential-related responsibilities. Training shall cover: (a) the agency's required credentials and their renewal timelines; (b) the Agency Credential Register and how to maintain it; (c) the renewal application process and pre-submission quality review; (d) reporting requirements for changes affecting credentials; (e) the escalation protocol for credential-threatening events; (f) Governing Body reporting obligations.

10.2 The Compliance Officer shall receive training on the regulatory monitoring obligations defined in this policy, including the requirement to notify the Administrator within 7 calendar days of identifying any new or changed licensure, certification, or accreditation requirement.

10.3 All personnel within scope (Section 3) shall sign the Policy Acknowledgment Form (Appendix C) within 14 calendar days of the policy effective date, any revision, or new appointment.

10.4 The Administrator shall include a credential maintenance compliance update as a standing topic in the annual mandatory training program, informing all staff of the importance of the agency's licenses and certifications to continued operations.

11. Version Control

11.1 This policy is maintained under the agency's enterprise policy lifecycle management system per policy EN-LC-001.

11.2 Only the most current approved version of this policy, as reflected in the policy header, is valid for any operational, compliance, or regulatory purpose. All superseded versions must be archived and clearly marked as "SUPERSEDED — NOT FOR USE."

11.3 Any substantive revision to this policy requires: (a) review and approval by the Governing Body, documented in meeting minutes; (b) re-acknowledgment by all personnel within scope within 14 calendar days of the revised effective date; (c) update to the enterprise policy index per EN-TG-001.

11.4 Non-substantive revisions (formatting, typographical corrections, updated cross-references) may be approved by the Administrator with notification to the Governing Body at the next regular meeting. Non-substantive revisions do not require re-acknowledgment.

GV-EA-005 — Agency Closure or Change of Ownership

1. Policy Header

2. Purpose

This policy establishes the procedures and notification requirements for planned agency closure, merger, change of ownership (CHOW), or voluntary termination of the Medicare provider agreement of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. A change of ownership or agency closure involves significant regulatory, legal, patient safety, and operational implications that must be managed in a systematic and compliant manner. CMS requires specific notification and transition procedures under 42 CFR Part 489, Subpart B for changes of ownership and under 42 CFR § 489.52 for voluntary termination of provider agreements. California HCAI requires separate state-level notifications. Failure to comply with these requirements may result in disruption of patient services, loss of Medicare certification, financial penalties, and legal liability. This policy ensures that the Governing Body, as the ultimate authority for the agency, directs and oversees any closure, merger, or CHOW process with full regulatory compliance and with the safety and continuity of patient care as the paramount priority.

3. Scope

This policy applies to:

The Governing Body of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. (decision-making authority)

The Agency Administrator (operational execution)

The Compliance Officer (regulatory compliance coordination)

The Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager (patient care transition)

The CFO / Revenue Cycle Director (financial closeout)

The HR Director (workforce notification and transition)

Legal Counsel retained by the agency

All agency personnel affected by a closure, merger, or change of ownership

This policy is activated when:

The Governing Body decides to permanently close the agency

The Governing Body decides to voluntarily terminate the agency's Medicare provider agreement

The agency undergoes a change of ownership as defined by 42 CFR § 489.18

The agency merges with or is acquired by another entity

Circumstances compel involuntary closure (e.g., regulatory enforcement, financial insolvency)

This policy does not apply to temporary service suspensions during emergencies (see OP-FM-005) or reductions in the scope of services (see GV-OG-003).

4. Policy Statement

4.1 Any decision to close the agency, voluntarily terminate the Medicare provider agreement, or initiate or accept a change of ownership shall be made exclusively by the Governing Body of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. The Administrator shall not independently initiate or agree to any such action without Governing Body authorization, documented in meeting minutes.

4.2 The Governing Body shall direct the closure, merger, or CHOW process to ensure: (a) all patients are safely transitioned to alternative providers with no disruption of essential services; (b) all regulatory notification requirements are met within mandated timeframes; (c) all employee obligations are fulfilled including appropriate notice and separation processes; (d) all financial obligations are resolved including outstanding claims, overpayments, and contractual liabilities; (e) all records are preserved and transferred in compliance with HIPAA, CMS, and California state retention requirements; (f) Legal Counsel is engaged to advise on all legal and regulatory aspects.

4.3 Patient safety and continuity of care shall be the highest priority in any closure or CHOW transition. No patient shall be discharged or transferred without a documented plan for continued care, per policy CL-CP-006 and CL-CP-007.

4.4 The agency shall comply with all CMS notification requirements for change of ownership under 42 CFR § 489.18, including notification to the CMS Medicare Administrative Contractor (MAC) and the state survey agency. Notification shall be submitted no later than the timeframes required by CMS and California state law.

4.5 The agency shall comply with all California HCAI notification requirements for change of ownership, closure, or surrender of license, including advance notice to HCAI and to all patients currently receiving services.

4.6 In the event of a change of ownership, the agency shall work cooperatively with the new owner to ensure the orderly transfer of the Medicare provider agreement, state license, patient records, and operational responsibilities, subject to CMS and HCAI approval.

4.7 This policy shall be reviewed on a triggered basis — activated upon any event described in Section 3. As a minimum floor, it shall also be reviewed biennially to ensure currency.

5. Definitions

6. Procedures

6.1 Governing Body Decision and Authorization

6.2 Regulatory Notifications — Change of Ownership

6.3 Regulatory Notifications — Agency Closure / Voluntary Termination

6.4 Patient Notification and Transition

6.5 Employee Notification and Workforce Transition

6.6 Financial Closeout

6.7 Record Retention and Transfer

6.8 Final Credential Surrender

6.9 Post-Closure Obligations

6.10 Involuntary Closure Procedures

6.11 Escalation and Exception Handling

7. Documentation Requirements

8. Compliance & Audit Considerations

8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

8.2 What Surveyors and Auditors Will Look For

CMS surveyors and state agency reviewers assessing a closure or CHOW will verify:

Evidence that patients were properly notified and transitioned. This is the primary regulatory concern. CMS will verify that all patients received advance written notice, were offered a choice of alternative providers, and were safely transitioned with appropriate clinical documentation (OASIS, clinical summaries, medication reconciliation). Patient abandonment — a patient left without arranged continued care — is the most serious potential finding.

Evidence that CMS and state notifications were timely. CMS will review the timing of the agency's notification relative to the closure or CHOW effective date. Late or absent notifications are regulatory violations.

Evidence that clinical records were preserved and accessible. CMS may request records for patients served during the agency's period of certification. Inability to produce records is a post-closure compliance failure.

Evidence that OASIS submissions were completed. CMS will verify that all required OASIS assessments (transfer, discharge) were completed and transmitted per OASIS requirements.

Evidence that financial obligations were resolved. CMS may conduct a post-closure audit of claims submitted during the agency's period of certification. Unresolved overpayments, late-filed claims, or billing irregularities are compliance concerns.

8.3 Common Failure Points

9. References

9.1 Federal Regulations

9.2 CMS Guidance

9.3 State Requirements

9.4 Cross-Referenced Agency Policies

10. Training & Acknowledgment Requirements

10.1 The Administrator, Director of Nursing, Compliance Officer, CFO, and HR Director shall receive training on this policy within 14 calendar days of appointment. Training shall cover: (a) the types of events that trigger this policy; (b) the regulatory notification requirements and timelines for CMS, HCAI, and DHCS; (c) the patient transition process and the paramount priority of patient safety; (d) the employee notification and WARN Act requirements; (e) the financial closeout process; (f) the record retention and transfer obligations; (g) the post-closure obligations.

10.2 All Governing Body members shall receive orientation to this policy as part of their governance onboarding per GV-GB-001, Section 10.1, with emphasis on: (a) the Governing Body's exclusive decision-making authority for closure and CHOW; (b) the Governing Body's oversight role during the transition; (c) the regulatory consequences of non-compliance.

10.3 All personnel within scope shall sign the Policy Acknowledgment Form (Appendix B) within 14 calendar days of the policy effective date, any revision, or new appointment.

10.4 In the event this policy is activated, the Administrator shall conduct an orientation session for all agency staff within 7 calendar days of the Governing Body's closure/CHOW decision, informing staff of: (a) the nature and timeline of the event; (b) their role in patient transition activities; (c) the employee notification and separation process; (d) confidentiality obligations; (e) the prohibition on patient abandonment.

11. Version Control

11.1 This policy is maintained under the agency's enterprise policy lifecycle management system per policy EN-LC-001.

11.2 Only the most current approved version of this policy, as reflected in the policy header, is valid for any operational, compliance, or regulatory purpose. All superseded versions must be archived and clearly marked as "SUPERSEDED — NOT FOR USE."

11.3 Any substantive revision to this policy requires: (a) review and approval by the Governing Body, documented in meeting minutes; (b) re-acknowledgment by all personnel within scope within 14 calendar days of the revised effective date; (c) update to the enterprise policy index per EN-TG-001.

11.4 Non-substantive revisions (formatting, typographical corrections, updated cross-references) may be approved by the Administrator with notification to the Governing Body at the next regular meeting. Non-substantive revisions do not require re-acknowledgment.

11.5 This policy is assigned a Triggered review cycle. It shall be reviewed: (a) immediately upon any event described in Section 3; (b) biennially as a minimum floor, regardless of whether a triggering event has occurred; (c) upon any change to CMS regulations governing CHOW or voluntary termination (42 CFR Part 489) or California HCAI licensure requirements.

8. Final Completeness Statement

This framework v7.0 represents the current, implemented enterprise policy taxonomy for Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. All 253 policies across 10 domains and 42 subdomains have been validated for ID integrity, structural correctness, IBM metadata completeness (Owner/Steward, Status, Review Cycle, Access Tier, Regulatory Tags), subdomain uniqueness, regulatory coverage, and non-redundancy. Version 7.0 adds 9 new operational policies addressing previously uncodified regulatory requirements (HIPAA comprehensive privacy, BAA management, incident response, data governance, FWA, AI governance, Cal/OSHA IIPP, workforce training governance, and employee health), introduces the Regulatory Tag System as a formal enterprise metadata layer, and updates all indexes and counts. The framework is certified at 100% IBM Knowledge Catalog / Watson governance artifact compliance and is ready to serve as the canonical source for system and application development.

P. Regulatory Tag Governance (NEW — v7.0)

P1. Purpose and Definition

The Regulatory Tag System is a cross-domain classification layer used to identify policies that materially support major regulatory obligations regardless of their domain or subdomain placement within the enterprise taxonomy. Regulatory Tags are additive metadata; they do not alter the taxonomy structure, domain assignments, subdomain assignments, classification tiers, access tiers, or ownership/stewardship designations.

P2. Active Tags (Current State)

P3. Assignment Governance

P3.1 Authority

Regulatory Tags are assigned by the Compliance Officer in consultation with the relevant Domain Owner/Steward. Final tag assignments for new or revised policies shall be approved by the Compliance Officer or the Governing Body (for Tier 4 policies).

P3.2 Assignment Events

Tags shall be assigned or reviewed:

At policy creation: During the policy development and approval process per GV-PM-001, the Compliance Officer shall evaluate and assign applicable Regulatory Tags before publication.

At major policy revision: During the policy review and revision cycle per GV-PM-002, existing tags shall be validated and new tags assigned if the revision changes the policy's regulatory relevance.

Upon regulatory change: When a federal, state, or local regulatory change is identified per CO-RA-001, the Compliance Officer shall evaluate whether affected policies require tag addition, modification, or removal.

Annual validation: All Regulatory Tag assignments shall be validated during the annual framework review, concurrent with the policy review cycle. The Compliance Officer shall present the annual tag validation report to the Governing Body at the first quarterly meeting of each calendar year.

P3.3 Assignment Criteria

A Regulatory Tag is assigned to a policy when the policy substantively and operationally addresses one or more requirements of the tagged regulatory framework. Tags are not assigned based on incidental keyword presence or tangential relevance. The test for assignment is:

Does this policy, if removed from the agency's policy library, create a material gap in the agency's compliance with the tagged regulatory framework?

If yes, the tag is assigned. If no, the tag is not assigned.

P3.4 Cross-Domain Consistency

The Compliance Officer shall ensure that Regulatory Tag assignments are consistent across domains. A regulatory requirement that is materially addressed by multiple policies across different domains shall have consistent tagging across all relevant policies.

P4. Reporting and Filtering

Regulatory Tags enable the following capabilities:

P5. Future Expansion

The Regulatory Tag System is extensible by design. Future framework versions may introduce additional tags as operational need and regulatory landscape dictate. Potential future tags include, but are not limited to:

CMS — Policies directly addressing CMS Conditions of Participation

CDPH — Policies addressing California Department of Public Health requirements

OIG — Policies addressing Office of Inspector General compliance expectations

EP — Policies addressing Emergency Preparedness requirements (42 CFR § 484.102)

MEDICARE BILLING — Policies addressing Medicare billing and reimbursement compliance

Additional tags shall be introduced through the framework revision process (EN-TG-001) and require Compliance Officer recommendation and Governing Body approval. Tags may not be introduced outside the formal framework revision process.

P6. Integration with IBM Governance Model

The Regulatory Tag System is designed as a natural extension of the existing IBM-aligned enterprise governance model. It complements — and does not conflict with — the following existing metadata layers:

The Regulatory Tag System satisfies the IBM Metadata Extensibility standard by demonstrating that the framework can incorporate additional classification layers without structural modification to the existing taxonomy.

# HR Policy



POLICY HR-TA-001

Recruitment & Hiring Standards

1. Policy Header

2. Purpose

This policy establishes standardized requirements for the recruitment, screening, and hiring of all employees and contracted staff at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. The policy ensures that only qualified, eligible, and competent individuals are employed by the agency in compliance with 42 CFR § 484.105 (organization and administration), 42 CFR § 484.80 (home health aide qualifications), applicable California home health licensing requirements, OIG Compliance Program Guidance for Home Health Agencies, and all federal and state equal employment opportunity laws. A structured, documented, non-discriminatory hiring process protects the agency from regulatory liability, ensures patient safety, and promotes workforce quality.

3. Scope

This policy applies to:

The HR Director and all HR department staff involved in recruitment and hiring

The Administrator

The Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager (for clinical position hiring decisions)

All hiring managers and supervisors who participate in candidate evaluation or selection

All contracted staffing agencies providing personnel to Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc.

All applicants for employment or contracted engagement with the agency

This policy does not apply to: Governing Body member appointments, which are governed by policy GV-GB-001 and the agency's bylaws or operating agreement. Volunteer recruitment is governed by HR-WM-006.

4. Policy Statements

4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall maintain a standardized, documented recruitment and hiring process that ensures all candidates are evaluated based on objective, job-related criteria as defined in current job descriptions (HR-JD series) and applicable regulatory requirements.

4.2 All hiring decisions shall comply with federal and state equal employment opportunity laws, including Title VII of the Civil Rights Act, the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA), the Age Discrimination in Employment Act (ADEA), and the California Fair Employment and Housing Act (FEHA). No applicant shall be discriminated against based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, genetic information, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

4.3 No individual shall be employed or contracted by the agency without completion of all pre-employment screening requirements defined in this policy, including but not limited to: identity verification, licensure/certification verification (HR-TA-004), criminal background check (HR-TA-002), OIG/SAM exclusion screening (HR-TA-003), and reference verification.

4.4 All positions shall have a current, approved job description (HR-TA-006; HR-JD series) on file prior to posting or recruitment for that position. No position shall be filled without a job description that defines minimum qualifications, essential functions, and regulatory requirements.

4.5 The agency shall not employ or contract with any individual who is excluded from participation in any federal healthcare program, as verified through OIG LEIE and SAM database screening per policy HR-TA-003.

4.6 All recruitment and hiring documentation shall be maintained in accordance with record retention policy CO-HP-007, with personnel file standards per HR-WM-005 and HR-WM-007.

4.7 The agency shall maintain a log of all recruitment activity sufficient to demonstrate non-discriminatory hiring practices in the event of audit, complaint, or litigation.

4.8 Only the most current approved version of this policy shall be considered valid. Superseded versions must not be used for any operational or compliance purpose.

5. Definitions

6. Procedures

6.1 Position Authorization and Job Description Verification

6.2 Job Posting and Candidate Sourcing

6.3 Interview and Evaluation Process

6.4 Conditional Offer and Pre-Employment Screening

6.5 Final Offer and Onboarding Handoff

6.6 Staffing Agency / Contract Staff Hiring

6.7 Escalation and Exception Handling

7. Documentation Requirements

8. Compliance Monitoring

8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

8.2 Surveyor Expectations

CMS surveyors and state licensing surveyors will specifically verify:

Personnel files contain evidence of pre-employment screening. Surveyors will select employee files and look for background check results, licensure verification, OIG/SAM screening, and reference checks completed prior to or on the date of hire.

Qualified staff. Surveyors will verify that employees meet the minimum qualifications defined in their job descriptions and required by regulation (e.g., RN licensure, HHA certification, therapist credentials).

No excluded individuals. Surveyors and OIG auditors will verify that no employee or contractor appears on the OIG LEIE or SAM exclusion databases.

Non-discriminatory practices. EEOC or state DFEH investigators, if triggered by a complaint, will request recruitment records including job postings, interview evaluations, and hiring rationale.

8.3 Common Failure Points

9. References

9.1 Federal Regulations

9.2 State Regulations

9.3 OIG Guidance

9.4 Cross-Referenced Agency Policies

10. Training Requirements

10.1 All HR staff involved in recruitment and hiring shall receive training on this policy within 14 calendar days of hire or assignment to recruitment duties. Training shall cover: (a) the complete recruitment process from authorization through onboarding handoff; (b) pre-employment screening requirements and zero-exception policy; (c) EEO compliance and prohibited interview inquiries; (d) California Fair Chance Act individualized assessment requirements; (e) OIG/SAM screening procedures; (f) documentation standards and use of all appendix forms.

10.2 All hiring managers and supervisors who participate in candidate evaluation shall receive training on: (a) use of the Structured Interview Evaluation Form (Appendix C); (b) prohibited interview inquiries; (c) EEO obligations; (d) scoring standards and documentation requirements. Training must be completed before the individual participates in any interview. Refresher training shall be provided annually.

10.3 All personnel within scope of this policy shall sign the Policy Acknowledgment Form (Appendix J) within 14 calendar days of the policy effective date, any revision, or new assignment to a role within scope.

10.4 The HR Director shall maintain a training completion log and report any non-compliance to the Administrator within 7 calendar days of the acknowledgment/training deadline.

11. Version Control

11.1 This policy is maintained under the agency's enterprise policy lifecycle management system per policy EN-LC-001.

11.2 Only the most current approved version of this policy, as reflected in the policy header, is valid for any operational, compliance, or regulatory purpose. All superseded versions must be archived and clearly marked as "SUPERSEDED — NOT FOR USE."

11.3 Any substantive revision to this policy requires: (a) review and approval by the HR Director and Administrator; (b) re-acknowledgment by all personnel within scope within 14 calendar days of the revised effective date; (c) update to the enterprise policy index per EN-TG-001.

11.4 Non-substantive revisions (formatting, typographical corrections, updated cross-references) may be approved by the HR Director with notification to the Administrator. Non-substantive revisions do not require re-acknowledgment.

POLICY HR-TA-002

Criminal Background Check & Screening

1. Policy Header

2. Purpose

This policy establishes mandatory requirements for conducting criminal background checks on all prospective and current employees, contractors, and volunteers of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. Criminal background screening is essential to: (a) protect the safety and welfare of patients receiving home health services in their residences; (b) comply with California Health and Safety Code requirements for home health agency personnel; (c) satisfy CMS Conditions of Participation requirements for employing qualified and suitable staff; (d) fulfill the agency's duty of care and fiduciary obligations; and (e) mitigate risk of liability arising from negligent hiring. This policy ensures that background screening is conducted consistently, documented completely, and applied in compliance with the California Fair Chance Act and all applicable federal and state fair employment laws.

3. Scope

This policy applies to:

All applicants for employment (full-time, part-time, per diem) at any stage after conditional offer

All contracted/staffing agency personnel assigned to work at or on behalf of the agency

All current employees subject to periodic rescreening as defined in this policy

All volunteers per HR-WM-006

The HR Director and all personnel responsible for initiating, reviewing, or acting upon background check results

This policy does not apply to: Governing Body members (screened per GV-GB-001 and HR-TA-003 for exclusion only, unless a Governing Body member also serves in an employment capacity). OIG/SAM exclusion screening is governed separately by HR-TA-003 but is coordinated with this policy.

4. Policy Statements

4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall conduct a criminal background check on every individual prior to their performing any work duties for the agency, including orientation, patient contact, or access to patient information.

4.2 Background checks shall be conducted through an agency-approved, FCRA-compliant (Fair Credit Reporting Act) background screening vendor and shall include, at minimum: (a) Social Security Number trace; (b) multi-state criminal records search; (c) county criminal records search for all counties of residence within the past 7 years; (d) National Sex Offender Registry search; (e) California Department of Justice (DOJ) LiveScan fingerprint check where required by California law.

4.3 The agency shall not make any adverse employment decision based solely on a criminal history finding without first conducting an individualized assessment per the California Fair Chance Act (AB 1008) and EEOC enforcement guidance, considering: (a) the nature and gravity of the offense; (b) the time elapsed since the offense or completion of sentence; (c) the nature of the job sought and its relationship to the offense.

4.4 Convictions that are automatically disqualifying regardless of individualized assessment include: (a) any offense requiring sex offender registration; (b) any conviction for abuse, neglect, or exploitation of a minor, elderly, or dependent adult; (c) any conviction for healthcare fraud; (d) any conviction currently resulting in exclusion from federal healthcare program participation.

4.5 All current employees shall be subject to periodic rescreening every 3 years or immediately upon credible report of criminal conduct, whichever occurs first.

4.6 All background check records shall be maintained in a separate, secured confidential file — not in the general personnel file — accessible only to the HR Director, Administrator, and Compliance Officer, per CO-HP-007 and applicable privacy laws.

4.7 Only the most current approved version of this policy shall be considered valid.

5. Definitions

6. Procedures

6.1 Pre-Employment Background Check Initiation

6.2 Background Check Scope

6.3 Review of Background Check Results

6.4 Individualized Assessment (Non-Automatic Disqualifiers)

6.5 Periodic Rescreening of Current Employees

6.6 Record Security and Confidentiality

7. Documentation Requirements

8. Compliance Monitoring

10. Training Requirements

10.1 The HR Director and all HR staff responsible for initiating, reviewing, or acting upon background checks shall receive training on: (a) FCRA requirements including disclosure, authorization, pre-adverse action, and adverse action processes; (b) California Fair Chance Act individualized assessment requirements; (c) automatic disqualifiers; (d) confidentiality and record security requirements; (e) use of all appendix forms. Training shall be completed within 14 calendar days of assignment and refreshed annually.

10.2 All hiring managers shall receive awareness training that: (a) background checks are mandatory and may not be bypassed; (b) no employee may begin work before clearance; (c) background check results are confidential and will not be shared with hiring managers (only PASS/FAIL). Training shall be part of the interviewer training required by HR-TA-001.

10.3 All personnel within scope shall sign the Policy Acknowledgment Form (Appendix D) within 14 calendar days of the policy effective date or new assignment.

11. Version Control

POLICY HR-TA-003

OIG/SAM Exclusion Screening

1. Policy Header

2. Purpose

This policy establishes mandatory requirements for screening all employees, contractors, vendors, volunteers, and Governing Body members of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. against the Office of Inspector General (OIG) List of Excluded Individuals/Entities (LEIE) and the System for Award Management (SAM) exclusion database. Federal law (42 USC § 1320a-7 and § 1320a-7a) prohibits any entity participating in federal healthcare programs from employing or contracting with excluded individuals. Employing an excluded individual exposes the agency to civil monetary penalties of up to $100,000 per instance, treble damages, program exclusion, and criminal prosecution. This policy ensures that the agency maintains continuous compliance through pre-employment screening, monthly ongoing screening, and immediate response protocols when an exclusion is identified.

3. Scope

This policy applies to:

All current and prospective employees (full-time, part-time, per diem)

All contracted staff, staffing agency personnel, and independent contractors

All Governing Body members (per GV-GB-001 § 6.1.4)

All vendors and suppliers with direct or indirect access to patients, patient information, or federal healthcare program funds

All volunteers per HR-WM-006

The HR Director, Compliance Officer, and all personnel responsible for conducting or overseeing exclusion screening

This policy applies regardless of whether the individual has direct patient contact. Any individual who is employed by, contracted with, or providing services on behalf of a Medicare-certified home health agency must be screened.

4. Policy Statements

4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall screen every individual identified in Section 3 against both the OIG LEIE and SAM exclusion databases prior to employment, engagement, or appointment, and monthly thereafter without exception.

4.2 No individual shall perform any work, provide any services, or conduct any business on behalf of the agency until an initial exclusion screening has been completed and documented as CLEAR.

4.3 If an individual is found to be excluded from participation in federal healthcare programs at any point — during pre-employment screening, monthly ongoing screening, or through any other means — the agency shall immediately remove the individual from all duties and initiate the response protocol defined in this policy.

4.4 The Compliance Officer shall be notified within 24 hours of any exclusion match. The Compliance Officer shall oversee the investigation and, if the exclusion is confirmed, ensure self-disclosure to the OIG per applicable self-disclosure protocols.

4.5 Monthly screening shall be conducted between the 1st and 15th of each calendar month. Results shall be documented and retained per this policy.

4.6 The agency shall screen not only by name but also by any known aliases, and shall use NPI (National Provider Identifier) where available, to reduce false negatives and false positives.

4.7 Only the most current approved version of this policy shall be considered valid.

5. Definitions

6. Procedures

6.1 Pre-Employment / Pre-Engagement Screening

6.2 Monthly Ongoing Screening

6.3 Exclusion Response Protocol

6.4 Vendor and Staffing Agency Screening

6.5 Escalation and Exception Handling

7. Documentation Requirements

8. Compliance Monitoring

8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

8.2 Common Failure Points

9. References

9.1 Federal Regulations and Guidance

9.2 Cross-Referenced Agency Policies

10. Training Requirements

10.1 The HR Director and all personnel responsible for conducting exclusion screening shall receive training within 14 calendar days of assignment on: (a) OIG LEIE and SAM database search procedures; (b) verification procedures for potential matches; (c) documentation requirements including Appendices A-D; (d) immediate response protocol for confirmed exclusions; (e) CMP exposure and the importance of timely, complete screening. Refresher training shall be provided annually.

10.2 The Compliance Officer shall receive training on: (a) OIG Self-Disclosure Protocol procedures; (b) CMP calculation methodology; (c) root cause analysis for screening failures.

10.3 All agency employees shall receive awareness training during orientation (HR-TA-005) and annual compliance training (CO-CP-008) on: (a) the prohibition against employing excluded individuals; (b) the obligation to report any knowledge that a coworker, contractor, or vendor may be excluded from federal programs.

10.4 All personnel within scope shall sign the Policy Acknowledgment Form (Appendix E) within 14 calendar days of the policy effective date or new assignment.

11. Version Control

POLICY HR-TA-004

Licensure & Certification Verification

1. Policy Header

2. Purpose

This policy establishes mandatory requirements for verifying and continuously monitoring the professional licensure, certification, and registration status of all clinical and licensed personnel employed by or contracted with Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. Verification of licensure is required by 42 CFR § 484.105 and § 484.115 (Personnel Qualifications), California Health and Safety Code home health agency licensing requirements, and applicable professional practice acts. Employing individuals who do not hold current, valid, unrestricted licensure appropriate to their role exposes the agency to regulatory sanctions, survey deficiencies, malpractice liability, and criminal prosecution for unauthorized practice. This policy ensures that every licensed professional practicing under the agency's authority holds a valid, verified license at all times.

3. Scope

This policy applies to:

All Registered Nurses (RN), Licensed Vocational Nurses (LVN), Physical Therapists (PT), Physical Therapist Assistants (PTA), Occupational Therapists (OT), Certified Occupational Therapy Assistants (COTA), Speech-Language Pathologists (SLP), Medical Social Workers (MSW), and any other licensed/certified clinical professional employed by or contracted with the agency

Home Health Aides (HHA) — certification verification per 42 CFR § 484.80

All contracted/staffing agency clinical personnel

The HR Director, Director of Nursing, and all personnel responsible for licensure verification

The Administrator

4. Policy Statements

4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall verify the current, valid, unrestricted status of every professional license, certification, and registration required for each clinical position prior to the individual performing any clinical duties, and shall continuously monitor licensure status throughout employment.

4.2 Verification shall be conducted through primary source verification — direct confirmation with the issuing state licensing board, certification body, or their authorized electronic verification system. Copies of licenses provided by the applicant or employee are not sufficient as the sole means of verification.

4.3 No individual shall provide clinical services, conduct patient assessments, or perform any task requiring professional licensure until primary source verification is completed and documented as CURRENT and UNRESTRICTED.

4.4 The agency shall maintain a Licensure Expiration Tracking System (Appendix A) to proactively monitor all license expiration dates and initiate renewal verification at least 60 calendar days before expiration.

4.5 Any clinician whose license expires, is suspended, revoked, or subject to restriction shall be immediately removed from clinical duties until the licensure issue is fully resolved. Practice on an expired or restricted license is a violation of California law and agency policy.

4.6 All licensure verification records shall be maintained in the employee's personnel file per HR-WM-005 and HR-WM-007.

4.7 Only the most current approved version of this policy shall be considered valid.

5. Definitions

6. Procedures

6.1 Pre-Employment Licensure Verification

6.2 Ongoing Licensure Monitoring

6.3 Licensure Adverse Event Response

6.4 Escalation and Exception Handling

10. Training Requirements

10.1 HR staff responsible for licensure verification shall receive training on primary source verification methods for each license type, use of state licensing board websites, documentation standards, and the tracking system. Training within 14 days of assignment; refreshed annually.

10.2 All licensed clinical staff shall receive notification during orientation (HR-TA-005) of their personal obligation to maintain current licensure, report any disciplinary action to HR within 24 hours, and provide renewal evidence to HR at least 30 days before expiration.

10.3 All personnel within scope shall sign the Policy Acknowledgment Form (Appendix E) within 14 calendar days of effective date or new assignment.

POLICY HR-TA-005

Employee Orientation & Onboarding

1. Policy Header

2. Purpose

This policy establishes mandatory requirements for the orientation and onboarding of all new employees and contracted staff at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. A comprehensive, standardized orientation ensures that every individual entering the agency workforce understands the agency's mission, regulatory obligations, clinical standards, compliance requirements, safety protocols, and their role-specific responsibilities before providing any services. This policy ensures compliance with 42 CFR § 484.105 (organization and administration), 42 CFR § 484.80 (home health aide training), CMS State Operations Manual surveyor expectations, OSHA requirements, and California home health licensure standards.

3. Scope

This policy applies to:

All newly hired employees (full-time, part-time, per diem) regardless of position

All contracted/staffing agency clinical personnel prior to their first patient assignment

All individuals transitioning to a new role or department within the agency (role-specific orientation component only)

The HR Director, Director of Nursing, department supervisors, and all personnel responsible for conducting or coordinating orientation

The Administrator

This policy does not apply to: Governing Body member orientation, which is addressed in GV-GB-001 § 10. Volunteer orientation is addressed in HR-WM-006.

4. Policy Statements

4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall provide a mandatory, documented orientation program to every new employee before the employee independently performs any job duties, provides any patient care, or accesses protected health information.

4.2 Orientation shall consist of two components: (a) General Agency Orientation (required for all staff); and (b) Role-Specific/Clinical Orientation (required for clinical staff and position-specific for all other roles).

4.3 General Agency Orientation must be completed within the first 5 business days of employment. Role-Specific/Clinical Orientation must be completed within the first 30 calendar days of employment. Clinical staff may not conduct unsupervised patient visits until both components are satisfactorily completed and documented.

4.4 Orientation content shall be reviewed and updated at least annually by the HR Director (general orientation) and Director of Nursing (clinical orientation) to reflect current regulations, policies, and agency operations.

4.5 Orientation completion shall be documented on the Orientation Completion Checklist (Appendix A for General, Appendix B for Clinical) and retained in the employee's personnel file per HR-WM-005 and HR-WM-007.

4.6 Contracted/staffing agency personnel shall complete an abbreviated orientation (Appendix C) covering patient safety, infection control, HIPAA, emergency procedures, and agency-specific clinical documentation requirements before their first patient assignment.

4.7 Only the most current approved version of this policy shall be considered valid.

6. Procedures

Training within 14 days of assignment as orientation trainer; refreshed annually.

10.2 Preceptors shall receive specific training on preceptor responsibilities, supervised visit evaluation, providing constructive feedback, and identifying competency concerns requiring escalation.

POLICY HR-TA-006

Job Description & Role Definition

1. Policy Header

2. Purpose

This policy establishes requirements for the development, approval, maintenance, and distribution of written job descriptions for all positions at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. Job descriptions serve as the foundational document defining the qualifications, scope of authority, essential functions, reporting relationships, and regulatory requirements for each position. CMS surveyors verify that employees meet the qualifications defined in job descriptions per 42 CFR § 484.105 and § 484.115. Written job descriptions also support ADA compliance, performance management, recruitment, disciplinary processes, and workforce planning.

3. Scope

This policy applies to:

All positions within Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. including clinical, administrative, and support roles

All hiring managers, supervisors, and department heads responsible for defining or maintaining job descriptions

The HR Director and Director of Nursing

The Administrator

4. Policy Statements

4.1 Every position at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall have a current, written, approved job description on file with the HR Director.

4.2 Job descriptions shall be developed and approved before any individual is recruited for or appointed to a position per HR-TA-001 § 6.1.2.

4.3 Each job description must contain, at minimum, the following elements: (a) position title; (b) department/discipline; (c) FLSA classification (exempt/non-exempt); (d) reporting relationship (reports to); (e) supervisory responsibilities; (f) position summary; (g) essential functions (ADA-compliant language); (h) minimum qualifications (education, experience, licensure/certification); (i) preferred qualifications; (j) physical requirements and working conditions; (k) regulatory requirements specific to the position; (l) approval signatures and date.

4.4 Job descriptions shall be reviewed at least biennially (every 24 months) or upon: (a) regulatory change affecting the position; (b) significant change in duties; (c) vacancy requiring recruitment; (d) organizational restructuring.

4.5 Each employee shall receive a copy of their current job description at hire, upon any revision, and at each annual performance evaluation, and shall sign an acknowledgment.

4.6 Job descriptions for clinical positions must align with the HR-JD series policies (HR-JD-000 through HR-JD-011) and applicable professional practice acts.

4.7 Only the most current approved version shall be considered valid.

5. Definitions

6. Procedures

POLICY HR-TD-001

Annual Mandatory Training Requirements

1. Policy Header

2. Purpose

This policy defines the agency's annual mandatory training requirements for all employees to ensure continuous compliance with CMS Conditions of Participation, OSHA standards, HIPAA, OIG compliance guidance, California home health licensing requirements, and agency operational standards. Annual training reinforces critical knowledge, addresses emerging risks, fulfills regulatory mandates, and supports the QAPI program's commitment to continuous improvement per 42 CFR § 484.65.

3. Scope

This policy applies to: All employees of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. (full-time, part-time, per diem) regardless of position. Contracted staff training requirements are addressed through staffing agency contractual obligations and verified per HR-TA-001 § 6.6.

4. Policy Statements

4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall maintain an Annual Mandatory Training Program that requires every employee to complete defined training topics each calendar year.

4.2 The Annual Mandatory Training Calendar (Appendix A) shall be established by the HR Director in collaboration with the Director of Nursing, Compliance Officer, and Risk Manager by December 15 of each year for the upcoming year.

4.3 All mandatory training must be completed by each employee within the calendar year (January 1 – December 31). New hires who start after July 1 must complete all remaining mandatory training by December 31 of their hire year or within 6 months of hire, whichever is later.

4.4 Training may be delivered through in-person classroom, online/e-learning, competency fairs, simulations, or a combination, provided that: (a) content meets regulatory requirements; (b) completion is individually documented; (c) competency is assessed where required.

4.5 The HR Director shall maintain an Annual Training Compliance Dashboard (Appendix B) tracking completion rates by employee, department, and topic.

4.6 Failure to complete mandatory training within the required timeframe shall result in progressive action: (a) written reminder at 30 days overdue; (b) supervisor notification at 45 days overdue; (c) administrative suspension from clinical duties (clinical staff) or disciplinary action per HR-ER-002 at 60 days overdue.

4.7 Only the most current approved version shall be valid.
