| Approved By | Governing Body Chair — Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. |
| Last Reviewed | 2025-07-10 |
| Next Review Date | 2026-07-10 |
| Supersedes | N/A (Initial Version) |
| Regulatory Tags | HIPAA, CA |

## 2. Purpose
This policy establishes the comprehensive privacy management program for Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. governing the collection, use, disclosure, retention, and destruction of protected health information (PHI), electronic protected health information (ePHI), and sensitive categories of health data. This policy ensures simultaneous compliance with the HIPAA Privacy Rule (45 CFR Part 160 and Part 164, Subparts A and E), the California Confidentiality of Medical Information Act (CMIA) (Cal. Civ. Code §§ 56–56.37), the Information Practices Act (Cal. Civ. Code § 1798 et seq.), and federal substance use disorder confidentiality requirements (42 CFR Part 2). This policy operationalizes all patient privacy rights, workforce privacy obligations, and sensitive data protections into a single, survey-defensible governance instrument.
## 3. Scope
This policy applies to:
All members of the workforce of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. including employees, contractors, per diem staff, volunteers, students, and interns
All members of the Governing Body
The Agency Administrator
The Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager
The Compliance Officer / Privacy Officer
All business associates and subcontractors who access, receive, create, maintain, or transmit PHI on behalf of the agency
All information systems, paper records, verbal communications, and electronic media containing PHI or ePHI
This policy does not apply to de-identified health information as defined under 45 CFR § 164.514(a)–(c), provided de-identification has been performed and documented per approved methodology.
## 4. Policy Statements
4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall maintain a comprehensive privacy program that satisfies all requirements of the HIPAA Privacy Rule (45 CFR Part 164, Subpart E), the CMIA (Cal. Civ. Code §§ 56–56.37), and 42 CFR Part 2 for substance use disorder records.
4.2 The agency shall designate a Privacy Officer with authority to develop, implement, and enforce all privacy policies and procedures. The Privacy Officer may be the same individual as the Compliance Officer, provided adequate authority and independence are maintained.
4.3 All uses and disclosures of PHI shall be limited to the minimum necessary to accomplish the intended purpose, per 45 CFR § 164.502(b) and policy CO-DG-101. Treatment, payment, and health care operations (TPO) uses are governed by role-based access profiles defining the minimum necessary for each job function.
4.4 The agency shall maintain and distribute a Notice of Privacy Practices (NPP) to all patients at the first service delivery contact, per 45 CFR § 164.520. The NPP shall describe all uses and disclosures, patient rights, and the agency's legal duties. A signed acknowledgment of receipt shall be obtained; if the patient declines to sign, the attempt and refusal shall be documented.
4.5 Patients have the following rights, which the agency shall honor within the timeframes required by HIPAA and California law:
Right to access PHI (45 CFR § 164.524) — responded to within 30 days (one 30-day extension permitted with written notice)
Right to request amendment of PHI (45 CFR § 164.526) — responded to within 60 days (one 30-day extension permitted)
Right to receive an accounting of disclosures (45 CFR § 164.528) — responded to within 60 days (one 30-day extension permitted)
Right to request restrictions on certain uses and disclosures (45 CFR § 164.522(a))
Right to request confidential communications (45 CFR § 164.522(b))
Right to receive a copy of the NPP (45 CFR § 164.520)
Right to file a complaint without retaliation
4.6 The agency shall apply heightened protections to the following categories of sensitive data, which are subject to more restrictive disclosure rules under California law and/or federal regulations:
Mental health records (Cal. Welf. & Inst. Code § 5328; CMIA)
HIV/AIDS test results and diagnosis (Cal. Health & Safety Code §§ 120975–121020)
Substance use disorder records (42 CFR Part 2)
Minor consent records (Cal. Fam. Code § 6920 et seq.)
Genetic information (GINA; Cal. Civ. Code § 56.17)
4.7 Substance use disorder records protected under 42 CFR Part 2 shall not be disclosed without the patient's specific written consent, except as permitted by 42 CFR Part 2 (medical emergency, qualified research, audit/evaluation, court order meeting § 2.64–2.67 requirements). Re-disclosure is prohibited and the agency shall include the Part 2 re-disclosure notice with any permitted disclosure.
4.8 All workforce members shall receive HIPAA privacy training within 14 calendar days of hire and annually thereafter. Training shall include CMIA requirements, sensitive data handling, and the agency's specific privacy procedures. Completion shall be documented and tracked per HR-TR-101.
4.9 Sanctions for privacy violations shall be applied consistently per CO-CP-004 (Code of Conduct & Ethics) and HR-ER-002 (Disciplinary Action & Progressive Discipline). Sanctions shall be proportionate to the severity of the violation and documented in the employee's personnel file. Failure to report a known privacy violation is itself a sanctionable offense.
4.10 Only the most current approved version of this policy shall be considered valid. Any revision requires re-acknowledgment by all workforce members within 14 calendar days of the revised effective date.
## 5. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Protected Health Information (PHI) | Individually identifiable health information transmitted or maintained in any form or medium by the agency or its business associates, as defined in 45 CFR § 160.103. |
| Electronic Protected Health Information (ePHI) | PHI transmitted or maintained in electronic media, as defined in 45 CFR § 160.103. |
| CMIA | California Confidentiality of Medical Information Act (Cal. Civ. Code §§ 56–56.37), which imposes additional state-level privacy protections beyond HIPAA. |
| Minimum Necessary | The principle that uses, disclosures, and requests for PHI shall be limited to the minimum amount reasonably necessary to accomplish the intended purpose, per 45 CFR § 164.502(b). |
| Sensitive Data | Categories of health information subject to heightened protections under California law or federal regulation, including mental health, HIV/AIDS, substance use disorder, minor consent, and genetic information. |
| Notice of Privacy Practices (NPP) | The document required by 45 CFR § 164.520 that informs patients of the agency's privacy practices, their rights, and the agency's legal duties. |
| 42 CFR Part 2 | Federal regulations governing the confidentiality of substance use disorder patient records maintained by federally assisted programs. |
| Privacy Officer | The individual designated by the agency to develop, implement, and enforce privacy policies and receive privacy complaints, per 45 CFR § 164.530(a)(1). |

## 6. Procedures
### 6.1 Privacy Program Governance

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.1.1 | Governing Body | Designate or confirm the designation of a Privacy Officer with documented authority to develop, implement, and enforce the agency's privacy program. | Prior to agency operation; confirmed annually at the first quarterly meeting. |
| 6.1.2 | Privacy Officer | Maintain a current, written privacy program document that addresses all HIPAA Privacy Rule requirements, CMIA requirements, and 42 CFR Part 2 requirements applicable to the agency. | Continuous; reviewed and updated annually or upon regulatory change. |
| 6.1.3 | Privacy Officer | Conduct an annual privacy risk assessment evaluating: (a) adequacy of current privacy policies; (b) workforce training compliance; (c) incident/complaint trends; (d) regulatory changes; (e) adequacy of safeguards for sensitive data categories. | Annually; completed within 90 calendar days of the start of each fiscal year. |
| 6.1.4 | Privacy Officer | Report privacy program status to the Compliance Officer quarterly and to the Governing Body per CO-CP-002 and GV-GB-001 reporting requirements. Report shall include: (a) privacy incidents; (b) complaint status; (c) training rates; (d) regulatory changes; (e) audit findings. | Quarterly. |

### 6.2 Notice of Privacy Practices (NPP)

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.2.1 | Privacy Officer | Develop and maintain the agency's NPP per 45 CFR § 164.520. The NPP must describe: (a) all permitted uses and disclosures of PHI; (b) patient rights; (c) agency's legal duties; (d) Privacy Officer contact information; (e) complaint filing instructions (agency and HHS). | Maintained continuously; revised upon any material change. |
| 6.2.2 | Intake Staff / Admitting Clinician | Provide the NPP to each patient (or authorized representative) at the time of first service delivery. Obtain written acknowledgment of receipt using the agency's NPP Acknowledgment Form. | At first service delivery contact. |
| 6.2.3 | Admitting Clinician | If the patient declines to sign the NPP acknowledgment, document: (a) that the NPP was provided; (b) that the patient declined to sign; (c) the reason (if stated); (d) the date and time of the attempt. | At the time of refusal. |
| 6.2.4 | Privacy Officer | Make the current NPP available on the agency's website (if applicable) and in the agency's office in a location accessible to patients and visitors. | Continuous. |

### 6.3 Patient Rights Fulfillment
#### 6.3.1 Right to Access

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.3.1.1 | Patient | Submit a written request to access PHI using the agency's Access Request Form or in any written format identifying the patient and the information requested. | N/A (patient-initiated). |
| 6.3.1.2 | Privacy Officer / Health Information Designee | Log the request in the Patient Rights Request Tracker with: (a) date received; (b) patient name; (c) information requested; (d) response deadline. | Within 2 business days of receipt. |
| 6.3.1.3 | Privacy Officer / Health Information Designee | Verify identity of the requestor per agency identity verification procedures. If the request is submitted by a personal representative, verify authority per 45 CFR § 164.502(g). | Within 5 business days of receipt. |
| 6.3.1.4 | Privacy Officer / Health Information Designee | Provide the requested information in the form and format requested by the patient, if readily producible. If not readily producible, provide in hard copy or other mutually agreed format. Fees, if any, shall not exceed the cost of labor for copying, supplies, and postage, per 45 CFR § 164.524(c)(4). Under CMIA, the first copy must be provided at no charge. | Within 30 calendar days of receipt; one 30-day extension permitted with written notice to patient stating the reason and expected completion date. |
| 6.3.1.5 | Privacy Officer | If access is denied in whole or in part (only grounds permitted under 45 CFR § 164.524(a)(2)–(3)), provide the patient with a written denial that includes: (a) the basis for denial; (b) a statement of the patient's right to have the denial reviewed; (c) the process for requesting review; (d) complaint filing instructions. | Within the 30-day response period. |

#### 6.3.2 Right to Amendment

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.3.2.1 | Patient | Submit a written request to amend PHI including the reason for the requested amendment. | N/A (patient-initiated). |
| 6.3.2.2 | Privacy Officer | Log the request and review the amendment request in consultation with the clinician(s) responsible for the relevant record entries. | Within 10 business days of receipt. |
| 6.3.2.3 | Privacy Officer | Grant or deny the amendment. If granted: append the amendment to the record and notify the patient and any persons/entities the patient identifies who received the original information. If denied (only grounds permitted under 45 CFR § 164.526(a)(2)): provide written denial including: (a) basis; (b) right to submit a statement of disagreement; (c) process for complaint. | Within 60 calendar days; one 30-day extension permitted with written notice. |

#### 6.3.3 Right to Accounting of Disclosures

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.3.3.1 | All Workforce Members | Document all disclosures of PHI that are not for TPO, not authorized by the patient, and not otherwise excluded under 45 CFR § 164.528(a) in the Disclosure Log. Documentation must include: (a) date of disclosure; (b) name and address of recipient; (c) brief description of PHI disclosed; (d) purpose of disclosure or copy of request. | At the time of each qualifying disclosure. |
| 6.3.3.2 | Privacy Officer | Upon receipt of a patient request for accounting of disclosures, compile the accounting from the Disclosure Log for the period requested (up to 6 years prior to the date of request). | Within 60 calendar days; one 30-day extension permitted with written notice. First accounting in any 12-month period is provided at no charge. |

#### 6.3.4 Right to Request Restrictions and Confidential Communications

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.3.4.1 | Privacy Officer | Evaluate all patient requests to restrict uses or disclosures. The agency is not required to agree to a restriction, except that the agency must agree to restrict disclosure to a health plan if: (a) the disclosure is for payment or health care operations; (b) the PHI pertains solely to a service for which the patient has paid in full out of pocket (45 CFR § 164.522(a)(1)(vi)). | Within 10 business days of receipt. |
| 6.3.4.2 | Privacy Officer | Document all agreed-upon restrictions in the patient's record and communicate the restriction to all workforce members with access to the record. Ensure EHR system flags are applied if technically feasible. | Within 5 business days of agreeing to the restriction. |
| 6.3.4.3 | Privacy Officer | Honor all reasonable requests for confidential communications (e.g., alternative address or phone number for receiving communications). | Upon receipt; implemented within 5 business days. |

### 6.4 Sensitive Data Protections

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.4.1 | Privacy Officer | Maintain a Sensitive Data Classification Matrix identifying all categories of sensitive data maintained by the agency, the applicable legal authority for heightened protections, the specific restrictions on use and disclosure, and the segregation or flagging requirements in the EHR. | Maintained continuously; reviewed annually. |
| 6.4.2 | All Clinical Staff | Prior to disclosing any mental health information, verify that the disclosure is authorized under Cal. Welf. & Inst. Code § 5328 or an applicable exception. Document the legal basis for the disclosure. | At each disclosure event. |
| 6.4.3 | All Clinical Staff | Prior to disclosing HIV/AIDS test results or diagnosis, obtain the patient's specific written authorization per Cal. Health & Safety Code § 121015, unless an enumerated exception applies. The authorization must be separate from any general authorization for release of medical records. | At each disclosure event. |
| 6.4.4 | All Clinical Staff | 42 CFR Part 2 records shall be maintained in a segregated section of the record (physically or electronically) with restricted access. Disclosure requires patient-specific written consent meeting Part 2 consent requirements (identity of recipient, purpose, how much/what kind, date/signature, right to revoke). Include the Part 2 re-disclosure prohibition notice with every permitted disclosure. | Continuous. |
| 6.4.5 | All Clinical Staff | For minor consent records (services obtained by a minor under Cal. Fam. Code § 6920 et seq. without parental consent), do not disclose information to the minor's parent or guardian without the minor's authorization unless: (a) required by law; or (b) the clinician determines in professional judgment that the minor lacks capacity to make healthcare decisions. Document the determination. | At each relevant encounter. |
| 6.4.6 | Privacy Officer / IT Director | Ensure the EHR system is configured to: (a) flag sensitive data categories; (b) restrict access to authorized roles only; (c) generate audit logs for all access to sensitive data records; (d) prevent unauthorized export or download. | Implemented prior to receiving sensitive data; validated annually. |

### 6.5 Workforce Privacy Training

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.5.1 | Privacy Officer / HR Director | Deliver HIPAA privacy training to all new workforce members. Training must include: (a) overview of HIPAA Privacy Rule; (b) CMIA requirements; (c) sensitive data categories and handling requirements; (d) patient rights; (e) minimum necessary principle; (f) agency-specific PHI access and disclosure procedures; (g) incident reporting; (h) sanctions for violations. | Within 14 calendar days of hire/engagement. |
| 6.5.2 | Privacy Officer | Deliver annual refresher privacy training to all workforce members. Content must be updated to reflect any regulatory changes, incident trends, or policy revisions from the preceding year. | Annually; completed within 60 calendar days of the start of each calendar year. |
| 6.5.3 | Privacy Officer | Deliver targeted retraining to any workforce member involved in a privacy incident or found non-compliant during audit. | Within 14 calendar days of incident closure or audit finding. |
| 6.5.4 | HR Director | Track training completion in the Learning Management System (LMS) per HR-TR-101 and report non-compliance to the Privacy Officer and department manager. | Within 7 calendar days of any missed deadline. |

### 6.6 Sanctions

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.6.1 | Privacy Officer | Investigate all reported or suspected privacy violations per CO-CP-007 (Compliance Investigation Process). Document findings, severity determination, and recommended sanction. | Investigation initiated within 7 calendar days of report; completed within 30 calendar days. |
| 6.6.2 | HR Director / Privacy Officer | Apply sanctions proportionate to the severity of the violation per the agency's Sanction Matrix: (a) unintentional minor violation: verbal counseling with documentation; (b) repeated minor violation: written warning and mandatory retraining; (c) knowing or willful violation: suspension, termination, and/or referral to law enforcement as required by law; (d) failure to report a known violation: treated as a separate sanctionable offense at the same tier as the underlying violation. | Within 14 calendar days of investigation completion. |
| 6.6.3 | Privacy Officer | Document all sanctions in: (a) the employee's personnel file; (b) the privacy incident log; (c) the quarterly compliance report to the Governing Body. | At the time of sanction. |

## 8. Compliance Measurement
### 8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

| Compliance Indicator | Measurement Method | Acceptable Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| NPP provided and acknowledged at admission | Audit of patient records for NPP acknowledgment | ≥ 98% acknowledgment rate; 100% documented attempt rate. |
| Patient rights requests responded to within regulatory timeframes | Review of Patient Rights Request Tracker | 100% within required timeframes. |
| Workforce privacy training completion | LMS report | 100% initial training within 14 days of hire; 100% annual refresher completion. |
| Sensitive data access restricted appropriately | EHR audit log review; access control audit | Zero unauthorized access events to sensitive data categories. |
| Disclosure log maintained for accounting purposes | Compliance audit of disclosure log completeness | 100% of qualifying disclosures documented. |
| Sanctions applied for violations | Review of privacy incident log and HR records | 100% of confirmed violations result in documented sanctions per sanction matrix. |
| Privacy risk assessment completed annually | Review of compliance files | Completed within 90 calendar days of fiscal year start. |
| 42 CFR Part 2 re-disclosure notice included with disclosures | Audit of Part 2 disclosure documentation | 100% compliance. |

### 8.2 Surveyor Expectations
CMS surveyors and state auditors will specifically verify:
NPP distribution and acknowledgment. Surveyors will review a sample of patient records to verify that the NPP was provided at the first service delivery contact and that an acknowledgment or documented refusal is present.
Patient rights fulfillment. Surveyors will review the Patient Rights Request Tracker and a sample of completed requests to verify timeliness and completeness of responses to access, amendment, and accounting requests.
Minimum necessary implementation. Surveyors will verify that the agency has implemented role-based access policies and that workforce members can articulate the minimum necessary principle.
Sensitive data protections. California Department of Public Health (CDPH) surveyors will verify CMIA compliance, HIV/AIDS confidentiality, and mental health record protections. Federal auditors may review 42 CFR Part 2 compliance for substance use disorder records.
Training and awareness. Surveyors will request training records and may interview staff regarding privacy procedures and patient rights.
Sanction policy and enforcement. Surveyors will verify that a sanction policy exists and has been applied when violations occurred.
### 8.3 Common Failure Points

| Failure Point | Risk | Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| NPP acknowledgment not obtained or refusal not documented | Survey deficiency; potential HIPAA penalty; CMIA violation | Standardize NPP distribution in admission workflow; audit monthly. |
| Patient access requests delayed beyond 30 days without documented extension | HIPAA violation; state complaint | Implement tracking system with automated deadline alerts. |
| No segregation or heightened protection for sensitive data categories | CMIA violation; 42 CFR Part 2 violation; state enforcement | Configure EHR to flag and restrict sensitive data; conduct annual audit of access controls. |
| 42 CFR Part 2 re-disclosure notice omitted | Federal violation; potential loss of grant funding or compliance standing | Include standard Part 2 notice in all disclosure templates; audit quarterly. |
| Privacy training not completed within required timeframes | Survey finding; increased risk of workforce errors | LMS automated reminders; non-compliance escalation per HR-TR-101. |
| Sanction policy exists but not enforced | Surveyor will cite failure to enforce; undermines compliance culture | Document all sanctions; include in quarterly Governing Body report. |
| Disclosure log incomplete or not maintained | Cannot fulfill accounting of disclosures requests; HIPAA violation | Mandatory field in EHR disclosure workflow; quarterly audit. |

## 10. Training Requirements
All workforce members shall receive comprehensive HIPAA/CMIA privacy training within 14 calendar days of hire/engagement. Training must cover all elements identified in Section 6.5.1. Training shall be delivered via the agency's LMS with documented completion.
Annual refresher privacy training shall be completed by all workforce members within 60 calendar days of the start of each calendar year. Content shall be updated annually by the Privacy Officer.
Targeted retraining shall be required for any workforce member involved in a privacy incident or audit finding, within 14 calendar days of incident closure.
All workforce members shall sign the Privacy & Confidentiality Acknowledgment Form at hire and annually thereafter, attesting to their understanding of HIPAA, CMIA, and sensitive data requirements.
The Privacy Officer shall maintain training records in the LMS and report completion rates in the quarterly compliance report.
## 11. Version Control
This policy is maintained under the agency's enterprise policy lifecycle management system per EN-LC-001.
Only the most current approved version, as reflected in the policy header, is valid for any operational, compliance, or regulatory purpose. Superseded versions must be archived and clearly marked "SUPERSEDED — NOT FOR USE."
Any substantive revision requires: (a) review and approval by the Governing Body; (b) re-acknowledgment by all workforce members within 14 calendar days of the revised effective date; (c) update to the enterprise policy index per EN-TG-001.
Non-substantive revisions (formatting, typographical corrections, updated cross-references) may be approved by the Privacy Officer with notification to the Governing Body at the next regular meeting. Non-substantive revisions do not require re-acknowledgment.
# POLICY CO-BA-101 — Business Associate & Vendor PHI Management
## Policy Header

| Version | 1.0 |
| Effective Date | 2025-07-10 |
| Status | ACTIVE |
| Review Cycle | Annual |

| Policy Owner/Steward | Compliance Officer |
| Approved By | Governing Body Chair — Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. |
| Last Reviewed | 2025-07-10 |
| Next Review Date | 2026-07-10 |
| Supersedes | N/A (Initial Version) |
| Regulatory Tags | HIPAA, CA |

## 2. Purpose
This policy establishes the requirements for identifying, qualifying, contracting with, monitoring, and terminating business associates and vendors who access, create, receive, maintain, or transmit protected health information (PHI) on behalf of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. This policy ensures compliance with the HIPAA Privacy Rule (45 CFR § 164.502(e) and § 164.504(e)), the HIPAA Security Rule (45 CFR § 164.314), the HITECH Act (42 U.S.C. § 17931 et seq.), and the California Confidentiality of Medical Information Act (CMIA) (Cal. Civ. Code § 56.10(c)). The agency shall not permit any entity to access PHI without an executed Business Associate Agreement (BAA) that meets all regulatory requirements.
## 3. Scope
This policy applies to:
All third-party entities that access, create, receive, maintain, or transmit PHI on behalf of the agency, including but not limited to: electronic health record (EHR) vendors, billing/coding services, cloud storage providers, IT service providers, shredding services, interpreters/translation services, collection agencies, consultants, auditors, and legal counsel
All workforce members who engage, manage, or oversee vendor relationships involving PHI
The Compliance Officer / Privacy Officer
The Administrator
The IT Director / CISO
All subcontractor relationships through which PHI may flow downstream
This policy does not apply to: (a) disclosures to treating providers for treatment purposes (45 CFR § 164.502(a)(1)(ii)); (b) disclosures to plan sponsors per 45 CFR § 164.504(f); (c) conduit exceptions (postal services, internet service providers acting solely as conduits).
## 4. Policy Statements
4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall execute a compliant BAA with every business associate prior to permitting access to PHI, per 45 CFR § 164.502(e)(1) and CMIA Cal. Civ. Code § 56.10(c). No PHI shall be shared, transmitted, or made accessible to any entity until a fully executed BAA is on file.
4.2 The agency shall maintain a Business Associate Master Registry documenting all active and terminated business associate relationships, including: entity name, services provided, PHI categories accessed, BAA execution date, BAA expiration/renewal date, risk classification, and assigned internal owner.
4.3 All vendors with potential PHI access shall be classified into a risk tier prior to BAA execution:
Tier 1 — High Risk: Entities with direct, ongoing, and unrestricted access to PHI (e.g., EHR vendors, billing services, cloud hosting providers)
Tier 2 — Moderate Risk: Entities with limited or role-restricted access to PHI (e.g., consultants, auditors)
Tier 3 — Low Risk: Entities with incidental or one-time access potential (e.g., shredding services, on-site equipment maintenance)
4.4 BAA content shall include, at minimum, all elements required by 45 CFR § 164.504(e)(2) and § 164.314(a)(2), including but not limited to: (a) permitted uses and disclosures; (b) obligation to safeguard PHI; (c) obligation to report breaches; (d) obligation to make PHI available for patient access requests; (e) obligation to return or destroy PHI upon termination; (f) subcontractor requirements; (g) termination provisions.
4.5 The agency shall conduct vendor due diligence prior to BAA execution including: (a) verification of entity's HIPAA compliance program; (b) review of security controls for Tier 1 and Tier 2 vendors; (c) OIG/SAM exclusion screening; (d) reference verification for new Tier 1 vendors.
4.6 Business associate relationships shall be monitored throughout the term. Tier 1 vendors shall be reviewed annually, including confirmation that the vendor has not been excluded from federal programs and that no material changes have occurred in the vendor's security posture or services.
4.7 Upon termination of a business associate relationship, the agency shall ensure: (a) return or destruction of all PHI held by the business associate; (b) written certification of PHI destruction or return; (c) revocation of all system access within 24 hours of termination; (d) update of the Business Associate Master Registry.
4.8 Business associates are directly liable for breach notification to the agency within the timeframes specified in the BAA (not to exceed 30 calendar days of discovery, per HITECH). The agency shall include breach responsibility provisions in all BAAs.
## 5. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Business Associate | A person or entity that performs functions or activities on behalf of, or provides certain services to, a covered entity that involve access to PHI, as defined in 45 CFR § 160.103. |
| Business Associate Agreement (BAA) | A written agreement between a covered entity and a business associate that establishes the permitted uses and disclosures of PHI and the safeguards the business associate must implement, per 45 CFR § 164.504(e). |
| Subcontractor | A person or entity to whom a business associate delegates a function, activity, or service involving PHI. |
| Business Associate Master Registry | The agency's centralized log of all business associate relationships, BAA status, risk classification, and monitoring history. |

## 6. Procedures
### 6.1 Identification and Risk Classification

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.1.1 | All Department Heads | Identify all vendors, contractors, and service providers who access, create, receive, maintain, or transmit PHI in the course of providing services to the agency. Submit identified entities to the Compliance Officer. | Ongoing; comprehensive review annually. |
| 6.1.2 | Compliance Officer | Review each identified entity to determine if the entity meets the definition of a business associate under 45 CFR § 160.103. Document the determination. | Within 14 calendar days of identification. |
| 6.1.3 | Compliance Officer | Assign a risk tier (Tier 1, 2, or 3) based on the nature, scope, and volume of PHI access. Document the classification rationale. | At the time of determination. |

### 6.2 Due Diligence and BAA Execution

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.2.1 | Compliance Officer | Conduct vendor due diligence appropriate to the risk tier. Tier 1: formal security questionnaire, evidence of HIPAA compliance program, SOC 2 or equivalent report review, OIG/SAM screening. Tier 2: security questionnaire and OIG/SAM screening. Tier 3: OIG/SAM screening and written attestation of PHI handling capability. | Prior to BAA execution. |
| 6.2.2 | Compliance Officer / Legal Counsel | Prepare and execute a BAA containing all elements required by 45 CFR § 164.504(e)(2) and § 164.314(a)(2). The BAA shall be reviewed by legal counsel for Tier 1 vendors. | Prior to any PHI access. |
| 6.2.3 | Compliance Officer | Enter the business associate into the Business Associate Master Registry with: (a) entity name and contact; (b) services provided; (c) PHI categories accessed; (d) risk tier; (e) BAA execution date; (f) BAA term/renewal date; (g) internal owner; (h) due diligence completion date; (i) OIG/SAM screening date. | Within 7 calendar days of BAA execution. |
| 6.2.4 | IT Director / CISO | For Tier 1 and Tier 2 vendors requiring system access: provision role-based access per IT-SC-002, configure audit logging per IT-DR-003, and apply encryption requirements per IT-SC-003. | Prior to any system access. |

### 6.3 Ongoing Monitoring

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.3.1 | Compliance Officer | Conduct annual reviews of all Tier 1 business associates including: (a) revalidation of services and PHI access scope; (b) OIG/SAM re-screening; (c) confirmation that vendor security controls remain adequate; (d) review of any reported incidents or breaches. | Annually. |
| 6.3.2 | Compliance Officer | Conduct biennial reviews of Tier 2 business associates. | Biennially. |
| 6.3.3 | Compliance Officer | Verify BAA renewal or renegotiation prior to expiration for all active business associates. | At least 60 calendar days prior to BAA expiration. |
| 6.3.4 | Compliance Officer | Report the status of all business associate relationships and any identified concerns to the Governing Body as part of the quarterly compliance report. | Quarterly. |

### 6.4 Termination and Offboarding

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.4.1 | Compliance Officer / Contract Owner | Upon termination of a business associate relationship, issue a written notice to the business associate requiring: (a) return or destruction of all PHI, including PHI held by subcontractors; (b) written certification of return/destruction within 30 calendar days. | At termination. |
| 6.4.2 | IT Director / CISO | Revoke all system access, VPN credentials, and remote access for the terminated business associate. | Within 24 hours of termination. |
| 6.4.3 | Compliance Officer | Update the Business Associate Master Registry to reflect termination, including: (a) termination date; (b) PHI return/destruction certification date; (c) access revocation confirmation. | Within 7 calendar days of termination. |
| 6.4.4 | Compliance Officer | If the business associate refuses or is unable to return or destroy PHI, document the reason and extend HIPAA protections to the retained PHI per 45 CFR § 164.504(e)(2)(ii)(J). | At the time of determination. |

### 6.5 Breach Responsibility

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.5.1 | Compliance Officer | Ensure all BAAs require the business associate to report suspected or confirmed breaches to the agency without unreasonable delay, and in no event later than 30 calendar days after discovery. | At BAA execution. |
| 6.5.2 | Compliance Officer | Upon receiving a breach notification from a business associate, initiate the agency's breach response per CO-IR-101, including HIPAA 4-factor risk assessment and California breach notification if applicable. | Within 24 hours of notification receipt. |

## 8. Compliance Measurement
### 8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

| Compliance Indicator | Measurement Method | Acceptable Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| BAA executed prior to PHI access | Review of Business Associate Master Registry and BAA files | 100% — no PHI access without executed BAA. |
| Due diligence completed per risk tier | Audit of due diligence records | 100% completion prior to BAA execution. |
| Annual/biennial reviews completed on schedule | Compliance calendar review | 100% on-time completion. |
| OIG/SAM screening current for all BAs | Screening log review | 100% screened at onboarding and at each annual review. |
| BAA renewals processed before expiration | Registry review | Zero lapsed BAAs. |
| Terminated BA PHI returned/destroyed and certified | Termination records review | 100% PHI disposition documented within 30 days of termination. |

### 8.2 Surveyor Expectations
Surveyors will request the Business Associate Master Registry and select a sample of BAAs for review.
Surveyors will verify that BAAs contain all required elements per 45 CFR § 164.504(e).
Surveyors will ask whether the agency has a process for monitoring business associate compliance and what happens when a BA reports a breach.
CDPH surveyors may verify CMIA authorization requirements for vendor PHI access.
### 8.3 Common Failure Points

| Failure Point | Risk | Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| PHI shared with vendor before BAA is executed | HIPAA violation; potential civil monetary penalty | Implement "no BAA, no access" policy with IT access provisioning gated by BAA verification. |
| BAAs missing required elements | Deficient BAA treated as no BAA; HIPAA violation | Use agency-standard BAA template reviewed by legal counsel; do not accept vendor-only BAAs without review. |
| No systematic tracking of BA relationships | Unknown BA exposure; inability to account for PHI flow | Maintain Business Associate Master Registry as a controlled document; review quarterly. |
| Terminated vendor retains system access | Unauthorized PHI access; potential breach | IT offboarding checklist includes BA access revocation within 24 hours. |
| No monitoring of Tier 1 vendor security posture | Undetected degradation of BA safeguards | Annual review with documented assessment. |

## 2. Purpose
This policy establishes the comprehensive incident response and breach notification program for Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. covering the detection, classification, investigation, containment, remediation, breach determination, notification, and documentation of security incidents and breaches involving protected health information (PHI) and personally identifiable information (PII). This policy ensures compliance with the HIPAA Breach Notification Rule (45 CFR §§ 164.400–164.414), the HITECH Act (42 U.S.C. § 17932), California data breach notification law (Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.82), and the CMIA breach provisions (Cal. Civ. Code § 56.36).
## 3. Scope
This policy applies to:
All incidents involving the unauthorized acquisition, access, use, or disclosure of PHI, ePHI, or PII maintained by Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc.
All workforce members, business associates, subcontractors, and any entity with access to agency PHI
All information media — electronic, paper, verbal, and visual
All locations where PHI is stored, processed, transmitted, or accessed
## 4. Policy Statements
4.1 All workforce members shall report suspected or confirmed security incidents to the Privacy Officer and IT Director within 1 hour of discovery. Failure to report a suspected incident is a sanctionable offense.
4.2 The agency shall classify all security incidents using a standardized severity framework:
Level 1 — Critical: Confirmed breach affecting ≥ 500 individuals; ransomware affecting PHI systems; confirmed unauthorized access to sensitive data categories
Level 2 — High: Confirmed breach affecting < 500 individuals; unauthorized disclosure of PHI to a single unauthorized recipient; lost or stolen device containing unencrypted PHI
Level 3 — Moderate: Unauthorized access to PHI without evidence of acquisition or viewing; misdirected fax or email to wrong recipient (PHI not accessed)
Level 4 — Low: Near-miss events; policy violations without PHI exposure; unsuccessful phishing attempts
4.3 For every incident involving PHI, the Privacy Officer shall conduct the HIPAA 4-factor risk assessment per 45 CFR § 164.402(2) to determine whether a breach has occurred:
Factor 1: Nature and extent of PHI involved (types of identifiers, likelihood of re-identification)
Factor 2: Unauthorized person who used the PHI or to whom the disclosure was made
Factor 3: Whether the PHI was actually acquired or viewed
Factor 4: Extent to which risk to the PHI has been mitigated
4.4 If the 4-factor risk assessment demonstrates greater than a low probability that PHI has been compromised, the incident is a reportable breach under HIPAA. All three exceptions must also be evaluated: (a) unintentional acquisition by workforce member acting under authority (45 CFR § 164.402(1)(i)); (b) inadvertent disclosure between authorized persons (45 CFR § 164.402(1)(ii)); (c) good faith belief that unauthorized person could not retain information (45 CFR § 164.402(1)(iii)).
4.5 Notification timelines:
Individual notification (HIPAA): Without unreasonable delay, not later than 60 calendar days from the date of discovery of the breach (45 CFR § 164.404(b))
HHS notification (≥ 500 individuals): Within 60 calendar days via HHS breach portal (45 CFR § 164.408(b))
HHS notification (< 500 individuals): Within 60 calendar days after the end of the calendar year in which the breach was discovered (45 CFR § 164.408(c))
Media notification (≥ 500 individuals in a single state/jurisdiction): Within 60 calendar days (45 CFR § 164.406)
California notification (Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.82): In the most expedient time possible and without unreasonable delay. If breach involves ≥ 500 California residents, notify the California Attorney General
CMIA notification: If breach of medical information, notify per Cal. Civ. Code § 56.36
4.6 All investigations shall be completed within 30 calendar days of incident discovery. The Privacy Officer and IT Director shall co-lead investigations involving ePHI. The Compliance Officer shall be notified of all Level 1 and Level 2 incidents within 2 hours.
4.7 The agency shall conduct a post-incident review for all Level 1 and Level 2 incidents, including root cause analysis per QA-AE-002 and corrective action development per QA-AE-003.
## 5. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Security Incident | The attempted or successful unauthorized access, use, disclosure, modification, or destruction of information or interference with system operations in an information system, per 45 CFR § 164.304. |
| Breach | The acquisition, access, use, or disclosure of PHI in a manner not permitted under the HIPAA Privacy Rule which compromises the security or privacy of the PHI, per 45 CFR § 164.402. |
| Discovery | A breach is treated as discovered as of the first day on which the breach is known to the agency or, by exercising reasonable diligence, would have been known, per 45 CFR § 164.404(a)(2). |
| 4-Factor Risk Assessment | The risk assessment required by 45 CFR § 164.402(2) to determine whether an impermissible use or disclosure constitutes a reportable breach. |
| Unsecured PHI | PHI not rendered unusable, unreadable, or indecipherable to unauthorized persons through encryption or destruction per HHS guidance (74 FR 42740). |

## 6. Procedures
### 6.1 Incident Detection and Reporting

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.1.1 | All Workforce Members | Report any suspected or confirmed security incident to the Privacy Officer and IT Director via: (a) incident hotline; (b) email to privacy@careindeed.com; or (c) in person. Report must include: who discovered it, what happened, when, who is affected, and what PHI is involved. | Within 1 hour of discovery. |
| 6.1.2 | Privacy Officer | Log the incident in the Security Incident Tracker with: (a) incident number; (b) date/time reported; (c) reporter; (d) description; (e) initial severity classification; (f) assigned investigator. | Within 2 hours of receipt. |
| 6.1.3 | Privacy Officer | Notify the Compliance Officer, Administrator, and IT Director for Level 1 and Level 2 incidents. Notify the Governing Body Chair for Level 1 incidents. | Level 1: within 2 hours. Level 2: within 4 hours. |

### 6.2 Investigation

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.2.1 | Privacy Officer / IT Director | Assemble the Incident Response Team (IRT). For Level 1: Privacy Officer, IT Director, Compliance Officer, Administrator, and legal counsel. For Level 2–3: Privacy Officer and IT Director. | Within 4 hours of Level 1 report; within 24 hours of Level 2–3 report. |
| 6.2.2 | IRT | Contain the incident: (a) isolate affected systems; (b) revoke compromised credentials; (c) secure affected paper records; (d) preserve evidence including audit logs, screenshots, and physical evidence. | Immediately upon containment decision. |
| 6.2.3 | IRT | Investigate: (a) determine the root cause; (b) identify all affected individuals; (c) identify all PHI involved; (d) determine the duration of unauthorized access; (e) interview relevant witnesses; (f) review system audit logs per IT-DR-003. | Investigation completed within 30 calendar days of discovery. |
| 6.2.4 | Privacy Officer | Complete the HIPAA 4-factor risk assessment (Section 4.3). Document all four factors and the rationale for breach/no-breach determination. Legal counsel shall review Level 1 determinations. | Within 30 calendar days of discovery. |

### 6.3 Breach Determination and Notification

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.3.1 | Privacy Officer | If the 4-factor risk assessment determines breach: prepare and deliver individual notification letters. Letters must include: (a) brief description of the breach; (b) types of information involved; (c) steps individuals should take to protect themselves; (d) what the agency is doing to investigate and mitigate; (e) contact information for questions. | Within 60 calendar days of discovery (HIPAA); in the most expedient time possible (CA). |
| 6.3.2 | Privacy Officer | If ≥ 500 individuals affected: file notification with HHS via the breach portal. Notify prominent media outlets serving the affected state/jurisdiction. | Within 60 calendar days of discovery. |
| 6.3.3 | Privacy Officer | If < 500 individuals affected: log the breach for annual HHS notification. | Annual submission within 60 days after calendar year end. |
| 6.3.4 | Privacy Officer | If ≥ 500 California residents affected: notify the California Attorney General. | In the most expedient time possible per Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.82(f). |
| 6.3.5 | Privacy Officer | If the 4-factor risk assessment determines no breach: document the analysis and retain per documentation requirements. No external notification required. | At the time of determination. |

### 6.4 Remediation and Post-Incident Review

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.4.1 | IRT | Implement corrective actions to address the root cause and prevent recurrence, per QA-AE-003. | Corrective action plan within 14 calendar days of investigation completion. |
| 6.4.2 | Privacy Officer / IT Director | Conduct post-incident review for Level 1 and Level 2 incidents. Document: (a) what happened; (b) root cause; (c) effectiveness of response; (d) lessons learned; (e) policy/procedure changes required. | Within 30 calendar days of incident closure. |
| 6.4.3 | Privacy Officer | Report incident outcomes and corrective actions in the quarterly compliance report to the Governing Body. Level 1 incidents shall also be reported to the Governing Body at a special meeting if the next quarterly meeting is more than 30 days away. | Quarterly; special report for Level 1 per timing criteria. |

| Security Incident Tracker | Centralized log of all incidents with status | Privacy Officer | Compliance file | Maintained continuously; retained 6 years. |
| 4-factor risk assessment | Written breach determination analysis | Privacy Officer | Compliance file | Completed within 30 days; retained 6 years. |
| Individual notification letters | Copy of letters sent to affected individuals | Privacy Officer | Compliance file | Retained 6 years. |
| HHS breach notification | Submission confirmation | Privacy Officer | Compliance file | Retained 6 years. |
| CA Attorney General notification | Submission confirmation | Privacy Officer | Compliance file | Retained 6 years. |
| Investigation records | Investigation files including interviews, audit logs, evidence | Privacy Officer / IT Director | Compliance file; IT security file | Retained 6 years. |
| Post-incident review reports | Written review with root cause and lessons learned | Privacy Officer | Compliance file; QAPI records | Retained 6 years. |
| Corrective action plans | CAP documentation with timeline and accountability | Privacy Officer | Compliance file; QAPI records | Retained 6 years. |

## 8. Compliance Measurement
### 8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

| Compliance Indicator | Measurement Method | Acceptable Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Incidents reported within 1 hour of discovery | Security Incident Tracker review | 100% compliance. |
| 4-factor risk assessment completed within 30 days | Tracker review | 100% within 30 days for all PHI incidents. |
| Notifications issued within regulatory deadlines | Notification records review | 100% compliance with HIPAA and CA timelines. |
| Post-incident reviews completed for Level 1/2 | Review records audit | 100% within 30 days of incident closure. |
| Corrective actions implemented | CAP tracking | 100% implementation within CAP timeline. |

### 8.2 Surveyor Expectations
Surveyors will review the Security Incident Tracker for evidence of a functioning incident response program.
Surveyors will request 4-factor risk assessment documentation for any incidents during the survey look-back period.
Surveyors will verify notification timeliness and content compliance.
CDPH surveyors may specifically ask about California breach notification compliance.
### 8.3 Common Failure Points

| Failure Point | Risk | Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Workforce members do not recognize or report incidents | Delayed discovery; extended breach exposure | Annual security awareness training per IT-UP-004; quarterly incident reporting reminders. |
| 4-factor risk assessment not documented | Surveyor treats as breach by default | Standardized risk assessment template; legal counsel review for Level 1. |
| Notification deadlines missed | HIPAA civil monetary penalty ($100–$50,000 per violation; $1.5M annual cap per violation category) | Automated deadline tracking in Security Incident Tracker. |
| California-specific notification requirements overlooked | State enforcement action | Include CA-specific notification steps in all incident response workflows. |
| Business associate breach not detected or reported timely | Delayed discovery extends notification clock | BAA breach reporting clause requiring notification within 30 days; annual BA review per CO-BA-101. |

# POLICY CO-DG-101 — Data Governance & Minimum Necessary Enforcement
## Policy Header

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Policy ID | CO-DG-101 |
| Title | Data Governance & Minimum Necessary Enforcement |
| Domain | CO — Compliance & Regulatory |
| Subdomain | HP — HIPAA & Privacy |
| Classification Tier | REQUIRED |
| Version | 1.0 |
| Effective Date | 2025-07-10 |
| Status | ACTIVE |
| Review Cycle | Annual |
| Access Tier | Tier 2 — Restricted |
| Policy Owner/Steward | Compliance Officer |
| Approved By | Governing Body Chair — Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. |
| Last Reviewed | 2025-07-10 |
| Next Review Date | 2026-07-10 |
| Supersedes | N/A (Initial Version) |
| Regulatory Tags | HIPAA |

## 2. Purpose
This policy establishes the data governance program for Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. governing the lifecycle of protected health information (PHI) and electronic protected health information (ePHI) from creation through destruction. This policy operationalizes the HIPAA minimum necessary standard (45 CFR § 164.502(b)), defines access control validation requirements, mandates data minimization practices, enforces export and download controls, prevents unauthorized shadow systems, and ensures alignment with record retention requirements. This policy serves as the enterprise-level governance instrument for PHI lifecycle management and data stewardship.
## 3. Scope
This policy applies to all PHI and ePHI created, received, maintained, or transmitted by the agency in any medium, and to all workforce members, business associates, and systems that access, process, or store such data.
## 4. Policy Statements
4.1 The agency shall implement a PHI lifecycle management framework governing data creation, collection, use, disclosure, storage, transmission, archival, and destruction. Each phase shall have defined controls, responsible parties, and audit mechanisms.
4.2 The minimum necessary standard (45 CFR § 164.502(b)) shall be operationalized through role-based access profiles. Each job function shall have a defined PHI access profile specifying: (a) which categories of PHI the role may access; (b) the volume of records accessible; (c) the permitted uses; (d) the permitted disclosure recipients. Access profiles shall be reviewed annually.
4.3 Data minimization shall be enforced at every point of PHI handling: (a) collect only the PHI required for the identified purpose; (b) use only the PHI required to perform the task; (c) disclose only the PHI required by the recipient; (d) retain only the PHI required by the retention schedule.
4.4 All PHI exports, downloads, bulk queries, and external transmissions shall require documented justification and shall be logged. Bulk exports (≥ 50 records) shall require supervisory approval prior to execution.
4.5 Shadow systems — any unauthorized repository of PHI outside agency-approved systems (including personal drives, personal email, USB storage, personal cloud accounts, spreadsheets, and non-approved applications) — are prohibited. Violation constitutes a sanctionable offense.
4.6 PHI retention and destruction shall comply with CO-HP-007 (Record Retention & Destruction). Data subject to litigation hold shall be preserved per RM-ER-006 regardless of retention schedule.
4.7 The IT Director / CISO shall implement technical controls supporting data governance including: (a) role-based access control in the EHR and all PHI systems; (b) automatic session timeouts; (c) export/download logging; (d) DLP (Data Loss Prevention) monitoring where technically feasible; (e) encryption per IT-SC-003.
## 5. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| PHI Lifecycle | The complete journey of protected health information from creation/collection through use, disclosure, storage, archival, and final destruction. |
| Minimum Necessary | The HIPAA requirement that uses, disclosures, and requests for PHI be limited to the minimum amount reasonably necessary to accomplish the intended purpose, per 45 CFR § 164.502(b). |
| Role-Based Access Profile | A documented specification of the PHI categories, volumes, and uses permitted for a defined job function. |
| Shadow System | Any repository, tool, or application used to store, process, or transmit PHI that has not been approved by the agency's IT and Compliance functions. |
| Data Minimization | The practice of limiting PHI collection, use, disclosure, and retention to the minimum required for the identified purpose. |

## 6. Procedures
### 6.1 PHI Lifecycle Governance

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.1.1 | Compliance Officer / IT Director | Maintain a PHI Data Inventory documenting: (a) all systems that create, store, process, or transmit PHI; (b) data categories in each system; (c) data flows between systems; (d) authorized users per system; (e) retention period per data category. | Maintained continuously; comprehensive review annually. |
| 6.1.2 | IT Director / CISO | Implement technical controls for each lifecycle phase: (a) creation — validated input forms, structured data entry; (b) storage — encryption at rest per IT-SC-003; (c) transmission — encryption in transit; (d) archival — defined archive procedures; (e) destruction — secure deletion/shredding per CO-HP-007. | Continuous. |
| 6.1.3 | Compliance Officer | Conduct annual data governance audit reviewing: (a) PHI Data Inventory accuracy; (b) access profile currency; (c) export/download log review; (d) shadow system detection; (e) retention compliance. | Annually. |

### 6.2 Minimum Necessary Access Control

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.2.1 | Compliance Officer / Department Heads | Develop and document Role-Based Access Profiles for every job function that accesses PHI. Each profile specifies: (a) PHI categories accessible; (b) volume limits; (c) permitted uses; (d) permitted disclosure recipients. | Initial implementation; updated within 14 calendar days of any job function change. |
| 6.2.2 | IT Director / CISO | Configure EHR and all PHI systems to enforce role-based access profiles. Verify configuration matches documented profiles. | At initial implementation and after any system change. |
| 6.2.3 | Compliance Officer | Review all access profiles annually in consultation with Department Heads. Verify that no role has access exceeding the minimum necessary for its function. | Annually. |
| 6.2.4 | IT Director / CISO | Conduct quarterly access recertification for high-risk systems (EHR, billing, claims). Department Heads must certify that all users under their authority have appropriate access levels. | Quarterly. |

### 6.3 Export, Download, and Transmission Controls

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.3.1 | IT Director / CISO | Implement logging for all PHI exports, downloads, and bulk queries from the EHR and all PHI-containing systems. Logs must capture: (a) user; (b) date/time; (c) data exported; (d) destination; (e) justification. | Continuous. |
| 6.3.2 | All Workforce Members | Document the business justification for any PHI export or download prior to execution. Bulk exports (≥ 50 records) require written supervisory approval. | At each export/download event. |
| 6.3.3 | IT Director / CISO | Review export/download logs monthly. Flag and investigate anomalies including: (a) exports exceeding normal volume for the user's role; (b) exports to non-standard destinations; (c) exports outside business hours. | Monthly review; investigation within 7 calendar days of anomaly detection. |

### 6.4 Shadow System Prevention

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |

| 6.4.2 | All Workforce Members | Do not store, process, or transmit PHI using any system, device, account, or application not approved by the agency's IT and Compliance functions. This includes personal email, personal devices (unless enrolled in approved BYOD per IT-UP-001), personal cloud storage, and non-approved communication platforms. | Continuous. |
| 6.4.3 | IT Director / CISO | Report all detected shadow systems to the Compliance Officer. Treat shadow system violations as security incidents per CO-IR-101. | Within 24 hours of detection. |

### 6.5 Retention Alignment

| 6.5.1 | Compliance Officer | Verify that PHI retention periods in the PHI Data Inventory align with CO-HP-007 (Record Retention & Destruction) and applicable regulatory requirements. | Annually. |
| 6.5.2 | IT Director / CISO | Implement automated or manual destruction procedures for PHI that has exceeded its retention period, unless subject to litigation hold or regulatory audit. | Per retention schedule; verified quarterly. |

## 2. Purpose
This policy establishes the comprehensive fraud, waste, and abuse (FWA) prevention, detection, investigation, and remediation program for Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. This policy ensures compliance with the federal False Claims Act (31 U.S.C. §§ 3729–3733), the Anti-Kickback Statute (42 U.S.C. § 1320a-7b(b)), the Stark Law (42 U.S.C. § 1395nn), the Deficit Reduction Act of 2005 (§ 6032), OIG Compliance Program Guidance for Home Health Agencies, and CMS program integrity requirements.
## 3. Scope
This policy applies to all workforce members, Governing Body members, contractors, subcontractors, agents, and business associates of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. in connection with all federal and state healthcare program participation.
## 4. Policy Statements
4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. maintains a zero-tolerance policy for fraud, waste, and abuse. All workforce members are responsible for preventing, detecting, and reporting suspected FWA.
4.2 The agency shall maintain the following definitions:
Fraud: Knowingly and willfully executing or attempting to execute a scheme to defraud any healthcare program or to obtain money or property by means of false pretenses, representations, or promises.
Waste: Overutilization of services or practices that directly or indirectly result in unnecessary costs to federal healthcare programs, whether due to mismanagement, deficient practices, or abusive practices.
Abuse: Actions inconsistent with sound fiscal, business, or medical practices that result in unnecessary cost or in reimbursement for services not medically necessary or that fail to meet professionally recognized standards.
4.3 The agency shall provide accessible reporting mechanisms for suspected FWA including: (a) the compliance hotline per CO-CP-006; (b) direct report to the Compliance Officer; (c) written report via the compliance mailbox; (d) anonymous reporting option. Reports may be made anonymously and shall be protected under the agency's non-retaliation policy (CO-CP-005).
4.4 No workforce member shall be retaliated against for reporting suspected FWA in good faith. Retaliation is itself a sanctionable offense subject to immediate disciplinary action up to and including termination and referral to legal counsel.
4.5 All reported or detected FWA concerns shall be investigated per CO-CP-007 (Compliance Investigation Process). The Compliance Officer shall lead or oversee all investigations with appropriate independence.
4.6 Upon confirmation of FWA, the agency shall: (a) cease the fraudulent, wasteful, or abusive practice immediately; (b) quantify overpayment if applicable; (c) refund overpayments within 60 calendar days of identification per 42 U.S.C. § 1320a-7k(d) and the CMS 60-day repayment rule; (d) report to appropriate federal/state authorities as required by law; (e) implement corrective action per QA-AE-003; (f) apply workforce sanctions per HR-ER-002.
4.7 Disciplinary actions for confirmed FWA involvement include but are not limited to: (a) mandatory retraining; (b) written reprimand; (c) suspension; (d) termination; (e) referral to law enforcement; (f) referral to professional licensing boards.
4.8 The agency shall conduct proactive FWA monitoring including: (a) billing pattern analysis per FN-FP-007; (b) claims audit sampling per CO-RA-002; (c) visit documentation vs. claims reconciliation per CO-DC-004; (d) referral pattern monitoring per CO-FA-001.
## 5. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| False Claims Act (FCA) | Federal statute (31 U.S.C. §§ 3729–3733) that imposes liability on persons who submit false claims to the government, including treble damages and per-claim penalties. |
| Qui Tam | A provision of the FCA that allows private persons (relators/whistleblowers) to file lawsuits on behalf of the government against entities that submit false claims. |
| 60-Day Repayment Rule | The requirement under 42 U.S.C. § 1320a-7k(d) that identified overpayments be reported and returned within 60 calendar days of identification or the date of the next cost report, whichever is later. |

## 6. Procedures
### 6.1 Prevention

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.1.1 | Compliance Officer | Deliver FWA training to all workforce members. Training must cover: (a) definitions of fraud, waste, and abuse; (b) False Claims Act including qui tam provisions; (c) Anti-Kickback Statute; (d) examples of FWA specific to home health; (e) reporting mechanisms; (f) non-retaliation protections; (g) consequences. | Within 14 calendar days of hire; annually thereafter. |
| 6.1.2 | Compliance Officer | Conduct annual FWA risk assessment covering: (a) billing practices; (b) referral relationships; (c) coding accuracy; (d) documentation completeness; (e) visit verification; (f) employee and contractor screening; (g) vendor relationships. | Annually; completed within 90 calendar days of fiscal year start. |
| 6.1.3 | CFO / Revenue Cycle Director | Implement proactive billing monitoring controls including claims denial trending, duplicate claim detection, LUPA monitoring, and visit-to-claim reconciliation per FN-FP-007 and CO-DC-004. | Continuous; reported quarterly. |

### 6.2 Detection and Reporting

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.2.1 | All Workforce Members | Report suspected FWA through any available mechanism: compliance hotline, direct report, written submission, or anonymous report. Do not investigate independently. | Immediately upon suspicion. |
| 6.2.2 | Compliance Officer | Log all FWA reports in the FWA Concern Tracker. Conduct preliminary assessment within 5 business days to determine whether investigation is warranted. | Logged within 24 hours; assessment within 5 business days. |
| 6.2.3 | Compliance Officer | Initiate formal investigation per CO-CP-007 for all reports warranting investigation. Engage legal counsel for reports involving potential criminal activity, False Claims Act exposure, or self-disclosure consideration. | Investigation initiated within 7 calendar days of determination. |

### 6.3 Investigation and Response

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.3.1 | Compliance Officer | Complete investigation per CO-CP-007. Document: (a) findings of fact; (b) determination (substantiated/unsubstantiated); (c) scope and financial impact; (d) recommended corrective action; (e) recommended sanctions; (f) recommended self-disclosure. | Within 60 calendar days of investigation initiation. |
| 6.3.2 | Compliance Officer / CFO | If overpayment is identified, quantify the overpayment and initiate refund within 60 calendar days of identification per 42 U.S.C. § 1320a-7k(d). | Refund within 60 calendar days. |
| 6.3.3 | Compliance Officer | Report confirmed FWA to the Governing Body per GV-GB-001 § 6.5. For Level 1 findings (confirmed fraud, willful misconduct, or regulatory referral), notify the Governing Body Chair within 48 hours. | Level 1: 48 hours. All others: next quarterly meeting. |
| 6.3.4 | Compliance Officer / Legal Counsel | Evaluate self-disclosure obligations. If disclosure to OIG or CMS is warranted, prepare and submit self-disclosure per OIG Self-Disclosure Protocol. | Per legal counsel guidance; within regulatory deadlines. |

### 6.4 Corrective Action and Sanctions

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.4.1 | Compliance Officer | Develop corrective action plan per QA-AE-003 addressing the root cause and systemic vulnerabilities. | Within 14 calendar days of investigation completion. |
| 6.4.2 | HR Director / Compliance Officer | Apply sanctions proportionate to the severity and culpability per HR-ER-002. Document in personnel file and FWA Concern Tracker. | Within 14 calendar days of investigation completion. |
| 6.4.3 | Compliance Officer | Track corrective action implementation and effectiveness. Report to Governing Body until closure. | At each quarterly meeting until resolved. |

## 2. Purpose
This policy establishes governance requirements for the use of artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), large language models (LLMs), and automated systems in the operations of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. This policy ensures that AI-assisted tools are used responsibly, transparently, and in compliance with HIPAA, the CMIA, CMS Conditions of Participation, and applicable professional standards. No AI or automated system shall make autonomous clinical decisions, generate fabricated documentation, or process PHI without authorization and safeguards.
## 3. Scope
This policy applies to all AI, ML, LLM, robotic process automation (RPA), and other automated systems used by the agency for any purpose including but not limited to: clinical decision support, documentation assistance, coding/billing support, scheduling optimization, quality analysis, predictive analytics, and administrative automation. This policy applies to all workforce members, contractors, and vendors who develop, deploy, or use such systems in connection with agency operations.
## 4. Policy Statements
4.1 No AI or automated system shall make autonomous clinical decisions. All clinical decisions — including diagnosis, treatment planning, medication management, care plan modifications, and patient assessments — require human clinical judgment by a licensed professional. AI may provide decision support inputs, but the licensed clinician retains full accountability for the clinical decision.
4.2 All AI-generated content used in clinical documentation, OASIS assessments, or care planning must be reviewed, validated, and authenticated by the responsible licensed clinician before becoming part of the clinical record. The clinician's signature on an AI-assisted document constitutes attestation that the content is accurate and reflects the clinician's independent professional judgment.
4.3 No AI system shall fabricate, hallucinate, or generate clinical observations, patient assessments, vital signs, interview responses, or any other clinical data. All clinical documentation must reflect actual patient encounters and direct clinical observations. Use of AI to generate fictitious clinical content constitutes fraud and is subject to immediate termination and potential legal referral.
4.4 PHI shall not be entered into, processed by, or transmitted to any AI system unless: (a) the system has been approved by the agency's IT Director / CISO and Compliance Officer; (b) a BAA is in place if the system is operated by a third party; (c) the system meets HIPAA Security Rule technical safeguard requirements; (d) data minimization principles are applied (only the minimum necessary PHI is used).
4.5 All AI systems used in agency operations shall be classified and approved:
Category A — Approved for PHI: Systems that have undergone full security assessment, BAA execution (if external), and privacy impact analysis. Listed on the Approved AI Systems Registry.
Category B — Approved, No PHI: Systems approved for use with de-identified data or non-PHI operational data only.
Category C — Prohibited: Systems that have not been assessed or that have failed assessment. Use of Category C systems with agency data is a sanctionable offense.
4.6 All AI system outputs affecting patient care, coding, billing, or compliance decisions shall be auditable. The agency shall maintain the ability to trace any AI-assisted decision or output to: (a) the input data; (b) the AI system used; (c) the human who reviewed and approved the output; (d) the date/time of review.
4.7 The agency shall maintain an AI Use Register documenting all AI systems in use, their category, purpose, data inputs, PHI exposure, approval status, responsible department, and review date.
## 5. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Artificial Intelligence (AI) | Any computational system that performs tasks normally requiring human intelligence, including learning, reasoning, pattern recognition, natural language processing, or automated decision-making. |
| Clinical Decision Support (CDS) | AI systems that provide information, alerts, recommendations, or risk assessments to support (not replace) clinical decision-making by licensed professionals. |
| AI Fabrication / Hallucination | AI-generated content that presents information as factual when it is not derived from actual data, observations, or verified sources. In clinical contexts, this includes any AI output that invents patient conditions, assessments, or observations not obtained through actual clinical encounter. |
| Approved AI Systems Registry | The agency's controlled list of all AI systems authorized for use, their classification (Category A, B, or C), and their approved use cases. |

## 6. Procedures
### 6.1 AI System Approval

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.1.1 | Requesting Department | Submit an AI System Approval Request to the IT Director / CISO and Compliance Officer. Request must include: (a) system name and vendor; (b) intended use; (c) data inputs required (PHI, de-identified, non-health); (d) deployment model (cloud, on-premise, hybrid); (e) clinical vs. non-clinical use. | Prior to any use. |
| 6.1.2 | IT Director / CISO | Conduct technical security assessment including: (a) data storage and encryption; (b) access controls; (c) audit logging capability; (d) data retention/deletion practices; (e) vendor security posture (SOC 2 or equivalent for Category A). | Within 30 calendar days of request. |
| 6.1.3 | Compliance Officer | Conduct privacy impact analysis including: (a) PHI exposure assessment; (b) minimum necessary evaluation; (c) BAA requirement determination; (d) HIPAA compliance evaluation; (e) California law compliance evaluation. | Within 30 calendar days of request. |
| 6.1.4 | IT Director / Compliance Officer | Assign category (A, B, or C) based on assessment results. Category A requires Administrator approval. Category C systems are prohibited. | Upon assessment completion. |
| 6.1.5 | IT Director | Add approved systems to the Approved AI Systems Registry with: (a) system name; (b) vendor; (c) category; (d) approved use cases; (e) PHI exposure level; (f) BAA status; (g) responsible department; (h) approval date; (i) next review date. | Within 7 calendar days of approval. |

Modify all inaccurate or fabricated content before signing. | At each AI-assisted documentation event. |

Sample a minimum of 10% of AI-assisted clinical documents per quarter and evaluate for: (a) accuracy; (b) completeness; (c) absence of fabricated content; (d) alignment with clinician observations. | Quarterly. |

| 6.3.2 | All Workforce Members | Report any suspected AI misuse, fabricated content, or unauthorized AI system to the Compliance Officer immediately. | Upon discovery. |

| 6.4.3 | Compliance Officer | Report AI governance status in the quarterly compliance report to the Governing Body, including: (a) systems approved/denied; (b) incidents; (c) audit findings; (d) regulatory developments. | Quarterly. |
