# DOMAIN: CL — Clinical Operations
## CL-CP-001 — Plan of Care Development & Approval
### 1. Policy Header

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Policy ID | CL-CP-001 |
| Policy Title | Plan of Care Development & Approval |
| Domain | CL — Clinical Operations |
| Subdomain | CP — Care Planning |
| Classification Tier | REQUIRED |
| Status | ACTIVE |
| Review Cycle | Annual |
| Access Tier | Tier 2 — Restricted |
| Policy Owner / Steward | Director of Nursing |
| Effective Date | 2025-07-10 |
| Version | 1.0 |
| Approved By | Governing Body Chair — Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. |
| Last Reviewed | 2025-07-10 |
| Next Review Date | 2026-07-10 |
| Supersedes | N/A (Initial Version) |

### 2. Purpose
This policy establishes the requirements for developing, approving, implementing, and maintaining an individualized plan of care (POC) for every patient admitted to home health services at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. The plan of care is the foundational clinical document that authorizes, defines, and guides all services delivered to a patient during a certification period. It is simultaneously a clinical roadmap, a legal authorization for skilled services, and a billing instrument — any deficiency in its development, physician approval, or content directly compromises patient safety, regulatory compliance, and reimbursement integrity.
This policy ensures compliance with 42 CFR § 484.60 — Condition of Participation: Care Planning, Coordination, and Quality of Care, which mandates that a plan of care be established and periodically reviewed by a physician for every patient receiving home health services. It also ensures compliance with CMS PDGM episode management requirements, OASIS data collection obligations, and the agency's documentation and billing alignment standards.
### 3. Scope
This policy applies to:
All registered nurses (RNs) responsible for completing the comprehensive assessment and establishing the plan of care
All clinical disciplines contributing to the plan of care (PT, OT, SLP, MSW, HHA)
The Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager
All intake and admissions staff who initiate the plan of care process
Physicians and allowed practitioners who review and approve plans of care
The Medical Records and Health Information staff
The Revenue Cycle team responsible for billing based on the approved plan of care
This policy applies at Start of Care (SOC), Resumption of Care (ROC), and Recertification (RECERT) for every patient served by Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. It does not govern individual visit notes, which are governed by CL-CD-001, or OASIS-specific data collection requirements, which are governed by CL-OA-001 through CL-OA-019.
### 4. Policy Statement
4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall establish a written, individualized plan of care for every patient admitted to home health services prior to or at the initiation of services, as required by 42 CFR § 484.60(a).
4.2 The plan of care shall be developed by the registered nurse responsible for the patient's care in collaboration with the patient, the patient's caregiver(s), the patient's attending physician or allowed practitioner, and all clinical disciplines involved in the patient's care.
4.3 No skilled home health services shall be provided to a patient without a physician-approved plan of care. Verbal orders for services may be initiated prior to written physician signature, provided the verbal order is received, documented, and authenticated in compliance with policy CL-CP-004 (Verbal Order Receipt & Authentication).
4.4 The plan of care shall be signed and dated by the physician or allowed practitioner before the agency submits a claim for Medicare home health services. For initial certification periods, the physician must sign the plan of care — which may be the OASIS-generated CMS-485 or equivalent — within the timeframe required by CMS.
4.5 The plan of care shall contain all elements required by 42 CFR § 484.60(a), as defined in Section 5 of this policy and detailed in Appendix A.
4.6 The plan of care shall be patient-centered, based on the findings of the comprehensive assessment (CL-CA-001), and shall reflect the patient's goals, functional limitations, and individual clinical needs.
4.7 No services shall be provided that are not authorized by the plan of care and a corresponding physician order. Any service not reflected in the current plan of care requires a new or amended physician order before the service is rendered, except in clinical emergencies where safety requires immediate action followed by immediate physician notification per CL-CP-003.
4.8 The plan of care shall be reviewed, revised, and recertified at least every 60 calendar days and whenever a significant change in the patient's condition warrants modification, per policy CL-CP-002.
4.9 The physician-approved plan of care, the OASIS assessment, the physician orders, and all visit documentation must be internally consistent. Discrepancies between these documents constitute documentation integrity failures governed by policy CO-DC-004.
4.10 Only the most current physician-approved version of a patient's plan of care shall be operative. Superseded plan versions shall be retained in the clinical record but clearly marked as no longer active.
### 5. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Plan of Care (POC) | The written document, established by the home health agency and approved by the physician, that specifies the patient's diagnosis, functional limitations, types and frequency of services to be furnished, medications, treatments, safety measures, and patient goals. Referred to in CMS documentation as the CMS-485 or Home Health Certification and Plan of Care. |
| Physician | A doctor of medicine (MD) or osteopathy (DO) legally authorized to practice medicine. For home health purposes, the physician responsible for signing the plan of care must not be employed by or have a financial relationship with the agency that would constitute a violation of the Stark Law, per 42 CFR § 424.22. |
| Allowed Practitioner | A nurse practitioner (NP), clinical nurse specialist (CNS), or physician assistant (PA) who is working in collaboration with a physician in accordance with state law, and who is authorized under 42 CFR § 424.22 to certify eligibility for home health services and approve the plan of care. |
| Certification Period | A period of not more than 60 calendar days during which the physician certifies that the patient is eligible for home health services. Each certification period requires a signed plan of care. |
| Start of Care (SOC) | The first billable visit made to a patient who has been admitted for a new episode of home health care. |
| Resumption of Care (ROC) | The first billable visit following a patient's return to the agency after an inpatient facility stay. |
| Recertification (RECERT) | The process of renewing a patient's plan of care for a subsequent 60-day certification period, based on a physician's determination that the patient continues to meet eligibility criteria and requires ongoing skilled services. |
| Verbal Order | An oral communication from a physician or allowed practitioner to a qualified clinician that authorizes a specific clinical action, governed by policy CL-CP-004. |
| CMS-485 | The Home Health Certification and Plan of Care form, or its electronic equivalent in the agency's EHR, that serves as the formal plan of care document for Medicare billing purposes. |
| PDGM | Patient-Driven Groupings Model — the Medicare home health prospective payment system that classifies patients into payment categories based on clinical grouping, functional level, comorbidity adjustments, and admission source, all of which are derived from the plan of care and OASIS assessment. |
| Homebound Status | The condition of a patient who has a condition due to an illness or injury that restricts their ability to leave home except with considerable effort, as defined in 42 CFR § 409.42(a). Homebound status must be certified by the physician and documented in the plan of care. |
| Individualized | Tailored to the specific needs, goals, diagnoses, functional limitations, and living situation of each patient, as opposed to a standardized or template-driven approach without patient-specific modifications. |

### 6. Procedures
#### 6.1 Initiating the Plan of Care Process at Start of Care

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.1.1 | Intake Staff / Administrator | Upon acceptance of a referral and determination that the patient meets admission criteria per OP-IM-002, assign the case to a qualified registered nurse for the comprehensive assessment and plan of care development. Ensure the patient's attending physician has been identified and contact information is documented in the intake record. | At the time of referral acceptance; assignment made no later than 1 business day before the scheduled SOC visit. |
| 6.1.2 | Assigned RN | Prior to the SOC visit, review all available referral documentation including hospital discharge summaries, physician orders, medication lists, recent laboratory results, and any therapy evaluations, to prepare for the comprehensive assessment. Do not pre-populate the plan of care with information that has not been verified through direct patient assessment. | Before the SOC visit. |
| 6.1.3 | Assigned RN | Conduct the comprehensive assessment at the SOC visit in compliance with policy CL-CA-001, including completion of all required OASIS data elements per policies CL-OA-001 through CL-OA-019. The SOC visit must occur within 48 hours of the referral or on the physician-ordered start date, whichever is earlier. | Within 48 hours of referral or on the physician-ordered start date. |
| 6.1.4 | Assigned RN | During or immediately following the SOC comprehensive assessment, develop the patient-specific plan of care incorporating: (a) all diagnoses, including the primary diagnosis and relevant secondary diagnoses supported by clinical documentation; (b) patient-specific functional limitations; (c) all skilled services ordered including discipline type, frequency, and duration; (d) medications including a complete medication list with dosages; (e) treatments and procedures; (f) safety measures; (g) patient goals — short-term and long-term, stated in measurable and patient-centered terms; (h) physician-ordered equipment and supplies; (i) patient/caregiver education needs and plan; (j) homebound status narrative. | Developed during or immediately following the SOC visit; documented in the EHR within 24 hours of the SOC visit. |
| 6.1.5 | Assigned RN | Collaborate with the patient and caregiver(s) in developing the plan of care. Document the patient's participation in goal-setting and any patient preferences, cultural considerations, or language access needs that affect the plan. | During the SOC visit. |
| 6.1.6 | Assigned RN | Identify all clinical disciplines needed based on the assessment findings. If additional disciplines are indicated (PT, OT, SLP, MSW), place orders per the physician referral or secure a verbal order per CL-CP-004 and document the referral to those disciplines within the plan of care. | Within 24 hours of the SOC assessment. |

#### 6.2 Required Elements of the Plan of Care
The plan of care for each patient shall contain, at minimum, all of the following elements as required by 42 CFR § 484.60(a) and CMS billing requirements. Absence of any required element constitutes a documentation deficiency subject to correction per CO-DC-003.

| Required Element | Content Standard | Policy Reference |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Patient identifying information | Full legal name, date of birth, Medicare/Medicaid number, address, emergency contact | CL-CA-001 |
| Attending physician | Name, NPI, address, telephone | CL-CP-003 |
| Certification period | Start and end dates of the 60-day episode | CL-CP-008 |
| Diagnoses | Primary diagnosis (the condition chiefly responsible for the patient's need for home health) and all relevant secondary diagnoses, coded to the highest level of specificity per ICD-10-CM | FN-CM-002 |
| Homebound status | Narrative description of the patient's homebound status with specific functional limitations | CL-CA-005 |
| Types and frequency of services | Each discipline ordered (RN, PT, OT, SLP, MSW, HHA), visit frequency per week or month, and estimated duration | CL-SD-001 through CL-SD-008 |
| Medications | Complete medication list including drug name, dose, route, frequency, and purpose | CL-SD-012 |
| Treatments and procedures | All skilled clinical interventions ordered (wound care, IV therapy, etc.) | CL-SD-010, CL-SD-011 |
| Safety measures | Environmental safety, fall risk precautions, high-risk medication monitoring | CL-SD-015, RM-PS-001 |
| Patient goals | Measurable short-term and long-term goals, patient-centered and time-bound | CL-CA-001 |
| Equipment and supplies | DME and supply items ordered | OP-SL-004 |
| Patient/caregiver education | Topics to be addressed and teaching plan | CL-SD-017 |
| Physician signature and date | Must be signed and dated by the certifying physician or allowed practitioner | CL-CP-003 |
| Prognosis | Physician's prognosis for restoration of normal health | 42 CFR § 484.60(a) |

#### 6.3 Physician Approval Process

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.3.1 | Assigned RN / Clinical Coordinator | Within 24 hours of finalizing the plan of care in the EHR, transmit the plan of care to the patient's certifying physician for review, approval, and signature. Transmission shall be via fax, secure electronic transmission, or physician portal. Document the date, method, and recipient of transmission in the clinical record. | Within 24 hours of POC finalization; documented at time of transmission. |
| 6.3.2 | Clinical Coordinator / Director of Nursing | Initiate tracking of the pending physician signature in the agency's physician order tracking system per policy CL-CP-009. Log the date transmitted, the physician's name and fax/contact number, and the expected return date. | At the time of transmission. |
| 6.3.3 | Clinical Coordinator | If no signed plan of care is received within 7 calendar days of transmission, initiate the first follow-up contact. Document the follow-up attempt including date, time, method, and person contacted. | 7 calendar days after transmission without return. |
| 6.3.4 | Clinical Coordinator | If no signed plan of care is received within 14 calendar days of transmission, escalate to the Director of Nursing for second-level follow-up. The Director of Nursing or designee shall contact the physician's office directly by telephone and document the conversation. | 14 calendar days after transmission without return. |
| 6.3.5 | Director of Nursing | If no signed plan of care is received within 21 calendar days of transmission despite documented follow-up, escalate to the Administrator. Assess whether continued services are appropriate pending physician signature. Document all escalation actions. | 21 calendar days after transmission without return. |
| 6.3.6 | Revenue Cycle / Director of Nursing | The agency shall not submit a final claim for a Medicare home health episode until a signed plan of care is on file for that episode. Verbal orders initiating care are permissible, but billing requires a signed plan of care. If the physician signature is not obtained, the episode is not billable and the Director of Nursing and Revenue Cycle Director must determine whether services should be discontinued. | Before claim submission for each episode. |
| 6.3.7 | Medical Records | File the signed plan of care in the patient's clinical record within 3 calendar days of receipt. Verify that the physician signature is dated, legible or accompanied by printed name and NPI, and covers the full certification period. Flag any unsigned, undated, or electronically unsigned plans of care for Director of Nursing review before filing. | Within 3 calendar days of receipt. |

#### 6.4 Multidisciplinary Coordination in Plan of Care Development

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.4.1 | Director of Nursing | Ensure that all disciplines providing services to the patient have reviewed the plan of care and that their discipline-specific goals, interventions, and visit frequencies are accurately reflected. No discipline shall provide services that conflict with or exceed what is authorized in the plan of care without a new physician order. | Within 48 hours of the SOC visit. |
| 6.4.2 | Each Clinical Discipline Provider | Upon receiving a referral for a new patient, review the plan of care within 24 hours of assignment. Confirm that the ordered services are within the discipline's scope of practice, are clinically appropriate based on the OASIS assessment and available records, and are supported by a current physician order. If any ordered service appears clinically inappropriate or outside scope, immediately contact the Director of Nursing. | Within 24 hours of assignment. |
| 6.4.3 | Assigned RN | Serve as the primary coordinator for the patient's plan of care. Document all clinical communications regarding the plan of care in the patient's clinical record. Any discipline-specific addition, modification, or concern regarding the plan of care shall be communicated to the assigned RN, who will coordinate with the physician per CL-CP-003. | Ongoing throughout the certification period. |
| 6.4.4 | Director of Nursing | Conduct or ensure that a care coordination communication occurs among all disciplines involved in the patient's care no later than 14 calendar days after SOC for patients receiving three or more disciplines. The communication may occur via telephone, secure messaging, or a documented care conference. Document the date, participants, topics discussed, and any plan of care modifications agreed upon. | Within 14 calendar days of SOC for patients receiving three or more disciplines. |

#### 6.5 Patient and Caregiver Engagement in Plan of Care

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.5.1 | Assigned RN | At the SOC visit, review the plan of care with the patient and caregiver(s) in plain language, ensuring they understand: (a) the services that will be provided and their frequency; (b) the goals of care; (c) their rights related to care decisions, including the right to refuse services; (d) how to contact the agency with questions or concerns; (e) safety measures specific to their condition and home environment. Provide the patient with a written copy of the plan of care or a plain-language summary in the patient's primary language. | During the SOC visit. |
| 6.5.2 | Assigned RN | Document the patient's and caregiver's understanding of and participation in the plan of care, including any expressed disagreements with specific goals or services, any modifications made based on patient preference (within physician-ordered parameters), and any language access services provided per OP-PA-003. | In the SOC visit note within 24 hours of the visit. |
| 6.5.3 | Assigned RN | If the patient or caregiver declines a specific ordered service, document the refusal per the agency's informed refusal process, notify the physician, and assess whether the refusal affects the patient's eligibility for continued home health services. | Immediately upon refusal; physician notification within 24 hours. |

#### 6.6 Escalation and Exception Handling

| Condition | Escalation Path | Corrective Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Plan of care is incomplete or missing required elements at the time of the first billable visit | Assigned RN escalates to Director of Nursing | Director of Nursing reviews and requires completion before any claim is submitted. Services may continue if the verbal order is properly documented per CL-CP-004. | Completion required before claim submission. |
| Physician refuses to sign the plan of care as written | Assigned RN and Director of Nursing contact the physician | Director of Nursing engages the physician to resolve clinical disagreements. Modify the plan of care per the physician's direction if clinically appropriate. If the physician declines to certify the patient at all, initiate discharge planning per CL-CP-006. | Resolution within 7 calendar days of refusal. |
| Patient refuses to participate in plan of care development | Assigned RN documents refusal and notifies Director of Nursing | Director of Nursing assesses whether the patient's capacity to refuse is intact. Engage the patient's legal representative if capacity is in question. Document refusal, actions taken, and outcome. | Immediate documentation; assessment within 24 hours. |
| Services are being delivered that are not reflected in the plan of care | Director of Nursing identifies the discrepancy | Stop non-authorized services immediately. Obtain a verbal or written physician order for any service that should have been included. Review for billing compliance with Revenue Cycle Director per CO-DC-004. Report to Compliance Officer if billing has already occurred. | Stop services immediately; order obtained within 24 hours; compliance review within 5 business days. |
| Plan of care is submitted to the physician but cannot be located in the record | Clinical Coordinator escalates to Director of Nursing | Conduct a full audit trail review in the EHR. If the plan of care was transmitted but not returned, re-transmit. If there is a gap in the audit trail, assess for data integrity concerns per CO-DC-001 and report to Compliance Officer. | Audit trail review within 3 business days of identification. |

### 8. Compliance & Audit Considerations
#### 8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

| Compliance Indicator | Measurement Method | Acceptable Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Plans of care contain all required elements per 42 CFR § 484.60(a) | Monthly audit of a random sample of SOC plans of care using the Documentation Audit Tool (Appendix C) | ≥95% of audited plans contain all required elements; 100% target |
| Plans of care are physician-signed before claim submission | Cross-reference of billing records with physician signature dates in the EHR | Zero claims submitted without a signed plan of care on file |
| Plans of care are developed within 24 hours of SOC visit | Audit of POC finalization dates against SOC visit dates | ≥95% of SOC plans finalized within 24 hours of the SOC visit |
| Physician follow-up is documented for all unsigned plans | Review of the orders tracking module for plans pending signature longer than 7 days | All plans pending signature longer than 7 days have documented follow-up attempts |
| Patient participation in plan of care is documented | Review of SOC visit notes for patient engagement documentation | ≥95% of SOC visit notes document patient/caregiver participation in plan of care review |
| Plan of care is consistent with OASIS assessment and physician orders | Triangulation audit per CO-DC-004 | Zero tolerance for material inconsistencies between POC, OASIS, and orders on audited records |

#### 8.2 What Surveyors and Auditors Will Look For
CMS surveyors conducting a standard survey under the State Operations Manual (SOM) Appendix B will specifically verify under Tag G160 (42 CFR § 484.60):
Evidence that a plan of care exists for every patient. Surveyors will request clinical records and verify that a written, physician-approved plan of care exists for each active patient and for each certification period of sampled past patients. Missing plans of care or unsigned plans are Condition-level deficiency risks.
Evidence that the plan of care contains all required elements. Surveyors will review plans of care for completeness per 42 CFR § 484.60(a). Commonly cited deficiencies include: missing homebound status narrative, vague or unmeasurable goals, incomplete medication lists, and visit frequencies that do not match delivered services.
Evidence that the plan of care is patient-centered and individualized. Surveyors distinguish between plans that are genuinely tailored to the patient and plans that appear to be templated without individualization. Cookie-cutter goal language (e.g., "patient will improve") without patient-specific metrics is a common deficiency.
Evidence of physician approval. Surveyors will verify physician signatures on plans of care and cross-reference with service dates to confirm that signed plans of care predate or accompany the services billed. Surveys will also verify that the certifying physician is eligible (not employed by or financially related to the agency in a prohibited manner).
Evidence that the plan of care is consistent with services delivered. Surveyors will compare ordered visit frequencies against actual visit delivery records. Significant and unexplained variances are cited as documentation integrity failures and potential False Claims Act concerns.
Evidence of patient participation. Surveyors may interview patients and caregivers about their knowledge of their plan of care and whether they were involved in developing their goals.
#### 8.3 Common Failure Points

| Failure Point | Risk | Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Plan of care developed by non-RN staff or templated without individualization | CMS deficiency under 42 CFR § 484.60; potential False Claims Act risk | Require RN development of all SOC plans of care; Director of Nursing conducts quality review of new SOC plans |
| Goals stated in non-measurable terms ("patient will improve ADLs") | Survey citation for inadequate plan of care; inability to demonstrate outcome achievement | Train all RNs on SMART goal-writing; use goal templates with required metrics |
| Services delivered that are not on the plan of care | Billing compliance risk; potential False Claims Act; survey deficiency | Implement visit authorization checking in scheduling system; audit monthly per CO-DC-004 |
| Physician signature obtained but not retained in clinical record | Missing documentation during survey; inability to support billing | Implement document receipt verification workflow; Director of Nursing reviews all unsigned episode records weekly |
| Plan of care not updated following significant change in patient condition | Clinical risk; documentation integrity failure | Train all clinicians on significant change criteria; Director of Nursing reviews mid-episode plan changes quarterly |
| Visit frequency on the plan of care does not match OASIS functional level | PDGM classification error; potential overpayment or underpayment; billing compliance risk | Conduct OASIS-to-POC consistency check at each SOC before claim submission per CO-DC-004 |

### 10. Training & Acknowledgment Requirements
10.1 All registered nurses responsible for conducting SOC assessments and developing plans of care shall receive competency-validated training on plan of care development requirements within 14 calendar days of hire and annually thereafter. Training shall be conducted by the Director of Nursing or a qualified designee and shall include: (a) all required elements of the plan of care per 42 CFR § 484.60(a); (b) ICD-10 primary diagnosis selection for PDGM; (c) SMART goal-writing for home health; (d) physician order management and the verbal order process; (e) plan of care transmission and tracking; (f) common survey deficiencies and how to avoid them; (g) the agency's EHR plan of care workflow.
10.2 All other clinical disciplines (PT, OT, SLP, MSW) shall receive orientation to plan of care processes relevant to their discipline-specific contributions within 14 calendar days of hire, covering: (a) how to read and confirm the plan of care; (b) their obligation not to deliver services outside the plan of care; (c) how to initiate a discipline-specific order change request through the assigned RN.
10.3 All personnel within scope of this policy shall sign the Policy Acknowledgment Form (Appendix B) within 14 calendar days of the policy effective date, any revision, or new hire/appointment.
10.4 The Director of Nursing shall verify training completion and competency for all RNs in plan of care development prior to their independently conducting SOC assessments. Competency shall be documented using the SOC Competency Assessment Tool (Appendix D).
### 11. Version Control
11.1 This policy is maintained under the agency's enterprise policy lifecycle management system per policy EN-LC-001.
11.2 Only the most current approved version of this policy, as reflected in the policy header, is valid for any operational, compliance, or regulatory purpose. All superseded versions must be archived and clearly marked as "SUPERSEDED — NOT FOR USE."
11.3 Any substantive revision to this policy requires: (a) review and approval by the Governing Body, documented in meeting minutes; (b) re-acknowledgment by all personnel within scope within 14 calendar days of the revised effective date; (c) update to the enterprise policy index per EN-TG-001.
11.4 Non-substantive revisions (formatting, typographical corrections, updated cross-references) may be approved by the Administrator with notification to the Governing Body at the next regular meeting.

## CL-CP-002 — Plan of Care Review & Update
### 1. Policy Header

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Policy ID | CL-CP-002 |
| Policy Title | Plan of Care Review & Update |
| Domain | CL — Clinical Operations |
| Subdomain | CP — Care Planning |
| Classification Tier | REQUIRED |
| Status | ACTIVE |
| Review Cycle | Annual |
| Access Tier | Tier 2 — Restricted |
| Policy Owner / Steward | Director of Nursing |
| Effective Date | 2025-07-10 |
| Version | 1.0 |
| Approved By | Governing Body Chair — Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. |
| Last Reviewed | 2025-07-10 |
| Next Review Date | 2026-07-10 |
| Supersedes | N/A (Initial Version) |

### 2. Purpose
This policy mandates the periodic review and update of every patient's plan of care throughout the episode of home health care, at each recertification period, and whenever a significant change in the patient's condition warrants modification. The plan of care is not a static document. It must be a living clinical instrument that evolves with the patient's condition, reflects the patient's current functional status and goals, and accurately represents the services being delivered at any point during the certification period. A plan of care that does not reflect the patient's current clinical reality fails its primary function as both a clinical guide and a billing authorization document, and constitutes a documentation compliance failure under 42 CFR § 484.60.
This policy ensures that plans of care at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. are reviewed at defined intervals, that clinical changes trigger prompt plan modifications with corresponding physician orders, and that the recertification process is completed within the regulatory timeline established by CMS.
### 3. Scope
This policy applies to:
All registered nurses managing active patient caseloads
All clinical disciplines (PT, OT, SLP, MSW) providing services under the plan of care
The Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager
Clinical Coordinators responsible for recertification tracking
Physicians and allowed practitioners who review and sign updated plans of care
Medical Records and Revenue Cycle staff involved in episode management
This policy applies during every active certification period and at every recertification for all patients served by Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc.
### 4. Policy Statement
4.1 The plan of care for every active patient shall be formally reviewed by the responsible registered nurse at a minimum of every 30 calendar days during the certification period, regardless of whether a change is indicated.
4.2 The plan of care shall be comprehensively reviewed and updated at each recertification period — no later than every 60 calendar days — and the updated plan of care shall be transmitted to and signed by the certifying physician within the recertification timeline defined in policy CL-CP-008.
4.3 A plan of care modification shall be initiated within 24 hours whenever any of the following significant change conditions are identified: (a) a new diagnosis or significant worsening of an existing diagnosis; (b) a new medication, medication change, or medication discontinuation that affects the clinical picture; (c) a change in the patient's functional status that affects the type, frequency, or intensity of services needed; (d) a new physician order that adds, removes, or modifies any service; (e) a hospitalization, emergency department visit, or other inpatient event; (f) a patient or caregiver-reported change in condition or safety concern; (g) a fall or other adverse event; (h) a change in the patient's discharge goals or the clinical outlook for discharge.
4.4 All modifications to the plan of care shall be supported by a corresponding physician order. No change in service type, frequency, or discipline shall be implemented before a verbal or written physician order is obtained per policy CL-CP-003.
4.5 The updated and physician-approved plan of care shall be internally consistent with all OASIS data collected during the applicable assessment time point and with all visit documentation in the patient's clinical record.
4.6 The Director of Nursing shall conduct a supervisory review of all active patient plans of care no less than every 30 calendar days to identify cases where the plan of care is outdated, services do not match orders, or recertification is approaching without a completed assessment.
4.7 A LUPA (Low Utilization Payment Adjustment) risk review shall be integrated into the plan of care review process to identify patients at risk of not meeting the minimum visit threshold, per policy QA-PI-006.
### 5. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Plan of Care Review | A formal, documented clinical assessment of the patient's current status, the appropriateness of the current plan of care, progress toward goals, and any needed modifications. |
| Significant Change in Condition (SCC) | A major decline or improvement in the patient's health status that is not expected to resolve without further intervention and that affects the type, frequency, or intensity of care needed. |
| Mid-Episode Modification | A change to the plan of care that occurs during a certification period, prior to the recertification assessment. |
| Recertification | The process by which a physician re-certifies that a patient continues to meet the criteria for Medicare home health benefits for a subsequent 60-day certification period. |
| 60-Day Certification Period | The maximum duration of a Medicare home health certification, beginning on the first day of the episode and ending 60 calendar days later. |
| LUPA (Low Utilization Payment Adjustment) | A reduced Medicare payment that applies when a patient receives fewer than the minimum number of visits required for their PDGM payment category during a certification period. |
| Discharge Planning | The process of identifying the patient's anticipated discharge date and criteria, and planning the clinical transition out of home health care, governed by policy CL-CP-006. |
| Episode Management | The clinical and administrative oversight of a patient's episode of care from SOC through discharge, including plan of care currency, visit frequency compliance, and recertification. |

### 6. Procedures
#### 6.1 Routine 30-Day Plan of Care Review

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.1.1 | Assigned RN | Conduct a formal plan of care review at a minimum of every 30 calendar days during each certification period. The review shall assess: (a) the patient's current clinical status compared to the status at SOC or last review; (b) progress toward each short-term and long-term goal — with specific measurable notation of progress, plateau, or regression; (c) whether the current service type and frequency remain appropriate; (d) whether any new diagnosis, medication change, or functional change has occurred that requires a plan modification; (e) whether the patient is on track for discharge within the anticipated episode timeframe; (f) LUPA risk — whether delivered visits are on track to meet the PDGM minimum visit threshold. | Every 30 calendar days from the SOC date or last formal review date. |
| 6.1.2 | Assigned RN | Document the 30-day review findings in the patient's clinical record using the agency's structured Plan of Care Review Note. The note shall explicitly state: (a) the review date; (b) findings for each active goal (progressing / plateaued / regressed / goal met); (c) current status of each ordered service; (d) any plan changes initiated or physician notifications made; (e) updated estimated discharge date and criteria. | Documented in the EHR within 24 hours of the review. |
| 6.1.3 | Assigned RN | If the 30-day review reveals that the plan of care remains appropriate and no modifications are needed, document the reaffirmation of the plan and update the Next Review Date in the EHR. A reaffirmation is not a modification and does not require a new physician order, but must be documented. | Within 24 hours of review. |
| 6.1.4 | Director of Nursing | Conduct a supervisory review of all active patient plans of care in the agency's caseload at minimum every 30 calendar days. The supervisory review shall identify: (a) any plan that has not been reviewed within 30 days; (b) any plan where delivered visits significantly deviate from ordered frequency; (c) any plan approaching the 60-day recertification deadline without a completed recertification assessment; (d) any patient who has not had a skilled visit within the past 14 calendar days without documented justification. | Every 30 calendar days; documented in the Director of Nursing's supervisory review log. |
| 6.1.5 | Director of Nursing | Document the findings of the supervisory review and direct the responsible clinician to take corrective action for any identified deficiency. All corrective actions shall be documented with target completion dates. | Within 48 hours of supervisory review completion. |

#### 6.2 Mid-Episode Plan of Care Modification (Significant Change)

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.2.1 | Discovering Clinician (any discipline) | Any clinician who identifies a significant change in the patient's condition during a visit shall document the clinical findings in the visit note and notify the assigned RN and/or Director of Nursing on the same day. The notification must include: (a) the nature of the change; (b) the patient's current clinical status; (c) the clinician's clinical assessment of the change; (d) any immediate safety concerns. | On the same day the change is identified. |
| 6.2.2 | Assigned RN | Upon notification or independent identification of a significant change, contact the physician within 24 hours to report the change, obtain clinical guidance, and secure any needed orders for plan modification. Document the physician contact, the information communicated, and the physician's response. | Within 24 hours of identifying the significant change. |
| 6.2.3 | Assigned RN | Obtain a verbal or written physician order for any change to the plan of care per policy CL-CP-003. For verbal orders, follow the read-back and documentation requirements of CL-CP-004. The order must specifically authorize the type and scope of the plan change before it is implemented. | Order obtained before implementing the plan change; verbal order documented within 24 hours. |
| 6.2.4 | Assigned RN | Update the plan of care in the EHR to reflect the authorized modification. Update: (a) diagnoses if applicable; (b) service types and frequencies; (c) medications if changed; (d) goals if the change affects the patient's functional status or discharge trajectory; (e) safety measures if new risks are identified. | Within 24 hours of receiving the physician order. |
| 6.2.5 | Assigned RN | Notify all other disciplines involved in the patient's care of the plan modification and updated orders. Document the notification in the clinical record. | Within 24 hours of updating the plan. |
| 6.2.6 | Assigned RN | Assess whether the significant change may require an unplanned OASIS assessment (Resumption of Care after an inpatient stay, or significant change assessment per CMS OASIS guidance). Consult the Director of Nursing if the assessment type is uncertain. If a new OASIS is required, initiate per CL-OA-001. | Within 24 hours of the significant change identification. |
| 6.2.7 | Director of Nursing | Review all mid-episode plan modifications within 7 calendar days of notification. Confirm that: (a) physician orders support all modifications; (b) OASIS data was updated if required; (c) billing reflects the updated plan; (d) all disciplines were notified. Document the supervisory review. | Within 7 calendar days of notification of the modification. |

#### 6.3 Recertification Plan of Care Review

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.3.1 | Clinical Coordinator / Director of Nursing | Generate a recertification tracking report no later than the 40th day of each active certification period, identifying all patients whose certification period ends within the next 20 days. Confirm that each patient has a recertification assessment scheduled and an assigned clinician. | No later than Day 40 of each certification period. |
| 6.3.2 | Assigned RN | Conduct the comprehensive recertification assessment between Day 56 and Day 60 of the current certification period (5-day assessment window), in compliance with CMS OASIS timing requirements and policy CL-CA-004. Complete all required OASIS data elements for the recertification time point. | Between Day 56 and Day 60 of the current certification period. |
| 6.3.3 | Assigned RN | Based on the recertification assessment, develop the updated plan of care for the subsequent certification period. The recertification plan of care shall: (a) reflect the patient's current clinical status as documented in the recertification OASIS; (b) update all diagnoses to reflect current conditions; (c) update goals to reflect progress achieved in the current period and new goals for the subsequent period; (d) update service types and frequencies based on current clinical needs; (e) update medications; (f) include a recertification narrative justifying continued need for skilled services based on current clinical findings. | Developed within 24 hours of the recertification assessment visit. |
| 6.3.4 | Assigned RN / Clinical Coordinator | Transmit the recertification plan of care to the certifying physician for signature no later than the last day of the current certification period. Document the date and method of transmission. | No later than Day 60 of the current certification period; earlier transmission is strongly recommended to allow time for physician review and signature. |
| 6.3.5 | Clinical Coordinator | Track the recertification plan of care signature per policy CL-CP-008. If not received within 7 calendar days of the start of the new certification period, initiate escalation per CL-CP-008 timelines. | Per CL-CP-008 tracking protocol. |
| 6.3.6 | Assigned RN | Review the patient's discharge candidacy at each recertification. If the patient has met discharge criteria per CL-CP-006, initiate discharge planning rather than recertification. Do not recertify a patient who no longer meets Medicare eligibility criteria for home health services. | At each recertification assessment. |

#### 6.4 Documentation of Discharge Planning Integration

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.4.1 | Assigned RN | At each 30-day review and at recertification, document the patient's current estimated discharge date and discharge criteria. If the estimated discharge date has changed, document the reason for the change (e.g., slower progress, new diagnosis, new goals). | At each review. |
| 6.4.2 | Assigned RN | If a patient reaches the 90th day of continuous home health services without a documented discharge plan, escalate to the Director of Nursing for a clinical necessity review. The Director of Nursing shall determine whether continued services are medically necessary and shall consult with the physician. | At or before Day 90 of continuous services. |

#### 6.5 LUPA Risk Monitoring Integration

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.5.1 | Director of Nursing / Clinical Coordinator | During the 30-day plan of care review, cross-reference each patient's delivered visit count against the PDGM minimum visit threshold for their payment category. Flag any patient at risk of a LUPA (defined as fewer than the required minimum visits with fewer than 10 days remaining in the certification period) for immediate clinical review. | At each 30-day review; also triggered by daily visit delivery report review. |
| 6.5.2 | Director of Nursing | For patients flagged as LUPA-at-risk, assess whether: (a) the clinical plan supports additional visits within the remaining episode timeframe; (b) the physician would authorize additional visit frequency; (c) there are clinical barriers to visit delivery (patient refusals, scheduling failures). Implement interventions as clinically appropriate per policy QA-PI-006. | Within 24 hours of LUPA risk identification. |

#### 6.6 Escalation and Exception Handling

| Condition | Escalation Path | Corrective Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 30-day review not completed within required timeframe | Director of Nursing identifies during supervisory review | Director of Nursing directs the assigned RN to complete the review immediately. Review completion documented. Persistent non-compliance addressed through HR-ER-002. | Review completed within 3 calendar days of identification. |
| Significant change identified but physician not notified within 24 hours | Director of Nursing reviews and contacts physician directly | Director of Nursing contacts physician and documents the contact. Evaluates whether the delay caused any clinical harm. If harm is suspected, initiates incident reporting per RM-ER-002. | Director of Nursing contact within 24 hours of identification of the missed notification. |
| Recertification assessment not completed within the 5-day window (Day 56–60) | Director of Nursing identifies via recertification tracking report | Director of Nursing assesses the reason for the missed window. If the window is missed, consult with Compliance Officer regarding billing implications. Complete the assessment as soon as clinically possible. | Director of Nursing assessment within 24 hours; Compliance Officer consultation within 48 hours. |
| Plan of care is modified without a supporting physician order | Director of Nursing reviews during supervisory audit | Director of Nursing immediately obtains a verbal physician order ratifying the change retroactively where possible. Assesses billing impact. Reports to Compliance Officer if billing has occurred for services without orders. | Physician order obtained within 24 hours; Compliance Officer notification within 48 hours. |
| Patient is recertified but does not clinically meet Medicare eligibility criteria | Compliance Officer conducts medical necessity review | Compliance Officer initiates a medical necessity audit of the episode. If claim has been submitted, assess for overpayment per FN-BC-004. Consider voluntary refund per OIG self-disclosure protocols if warranted. | Audit initiated within 7 calendar days; refund action within 60 calendar days per FN-BC-004. |

| Requirement | Document / Record | Responsible Party | Location | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 30-day plan of care review note | Structured Plan of Care Review Note documenting current status, goal progress, and plan disposition | Assigned RN | EHR — clinical notes | Within 24 hours of review; retained minimum 7 years |
| Mid-episode modification | Updated plan of care in EHR with supporting physician order | Assigned RN | EHR — plan of care and orders | Within 24 hours of receiving physician order |
| Physician notification for significant change | Documentation of contact, information communicated, and physician response | Assigned RN | EHR — communication notes | Within 24 hours of significant change identification |
| Discipline notification of plan modification | Documentation of notification to all involved disciplines | Assigned RN | EHR — communication notes | Within 24 hours of plan update |
| Director of Nursing supervisory review log | Monthly supervisory review findings for all active patients | Director of Nursing | EHR or Director of Nursing supervisory file | Every 30 calendar days; retained minimum 7 years |
| Recertification assessment and plan | OASIS recertification assessment and updated plan of care for the subsequent period | Assigned RN | EHR — OASIS and plan of care | Completed Days 56–60; transmitted to physician no later than Day 60 |
| LUPA risk monitoring | Documentation of LUPA risk review and interventions | Director of Nursing | EHR — clinical management notes | At each 30-day review for at-risk patients; retained minimum 7 years |
| Policy acknowledgment | Signed acknowledgment of this policy (Appendix A) | Each individual; Administrator (collection) | Policy acknowledgment file | Within 14 calendar days of effective date, revision, or hire |

### 8. Compliance & Audit Considerations
#### 8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

| Compliance Indicator | Measurement Method | Acceptable Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 30-day review completed for all active patients | Director of Nursing supervisory review log; EHR review date audit | ≥95% of active patients with documented 30-day review within required timeframe |
| Significant changes result in physician notification within 24 hours | Audit of physician contact notes against visit dates in patient records with documented clinical changes | ≥95% of significant changes have physician notification documented within 24 hours |
| Recertification assessments completed within the Day 56–60 window | Recertification tracking report cross-referenced with OASIS assessment dates | ≥95% of recertification assessments completed within the 5-day window |
| All plan modifications supported by physician orders | Monthly documentation audit cross-referencing plan changes with orders | Zero tolerance for plan modifications without supporting physician orders on audited records |
| LUPA risk review integrated into 30-day reviews | Review of Director of Nursing supervisory log for LUPA risk notation | 100% of episodes with LUPA risk noted and documented interventions |

#### 8.2 What Surveyors and Auditors Will Look For
CMS surveyors will specifically examine:
Evidence that plans of care are reviewed at least every 60 days (and more frequently as indicated). Surveyors will check clinical records for documented reviews. A plan of care that is unchanged from SOC through a full 60-day episode without any documented review is a strong indicator of passive care management and will be cited.
Evidence that significant clinical changes prompt plan modifications. Surveyors will identify patients who had hospitalizations, significant medication changes, or new diagnoses during the episode and verify that the plan of care was updated. An unchanged plan following a clinical change is a common deficiency.
Evidence that all plan modifications are physician-ordered. Surveyors will cross-reference changes in service type or frequency between the original and current plan of care with the physician orders on file. Service changes without supporting orders are a False Claims Act risk and a CMS deficiency.
Evidence of recertification within the required window. Surveyors will request all OASIS assessments and cross-reference their dates with the certification period dates. Recertification assessments outside the Day 56–60 window are a documentation compliance failure and may affect billing.
Evidence that plans of care reflect the patient's actual current condition. Surveyors will compare the plan of care goals and functional status descriptions against visit notes from the same period. A plan describing a patient as "independent in ambulation" while visit notes document the patient as bed-bound is a documentation integrity failure.
#### 8.3 Common Failure Points

| Failure Point | Risk | Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No documented 30-day reviews — reviews treated as implicit in visit notes | Survey deficiency; inability to demonstrate active care management | Implement structured Plan of Care Review Note in EHR; Director of Nursing supervisory review enforces compliance |
| Recertification assessment completed but physician signature not tracked | Episode billing without signed recertification plan | Integrate recertification tracking into CL-CP-008 system; billing hold until signature confirmed |
| Hospitalization not identified as significant change requiring plan update | Plan of care does not reflect post-hospital clinical picture; clinical and billing compliance risk | Train all clinicians on SCC criteria; Director of Nursing supervisory review flags hospitalizations automatically |
| Clinicians use copy-forward function in EHR without genuine review | Plan of care does not reflect current patient status; documentation integrity failure | Disable or restrict copy-forward for plan of care fields; Director of Nursing audits copy-forward patterns |

### 10. Training & Acknowledgment Requirements
10.1 All registered nurses shall receive training on plan of care review requirements within 14 calendar days of hire and annually thereafter, including: (a) the criteria for significant change in condition; (b) the structured 30-day review process and required documentation; (c) the recertification assessment window and timeline; (d) the LUPA risk review process; (e) the EHR Plan of Care Review Note documentation standard.
10.2 The Director of Nursing shall receive training on supervisory review obligations, including the monthly caseload review process and escalation procedures, at hire and annually thereafter.
10.3 All personnel within scope shall sign the Policy Acknowledgment Form (Appendix A) within 14 calendar days of the policy effective date, any revision, or new appointment.

## CL-CP-003 — Physician Orders & Order Management
### 1. Policy Header

| Field | Value |

| Policy ID | CL-CP-003 |
| Policy Title | Physician Orders & Order Management |
| Domain | CL — Clinical Operations |

| Status | ACTIVE |
| Review Cycle | Annual |

### 2. Purpose
This policy establishes the requirements for obtaining, documenting, managing, and authenticating all physician orders at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. Every skilled home health service, treatment, medication, and clinical intervention delivered to a patient must be authorized by a valid, current physician order. The physician order is the legal authorization for clinical action — without it, services are not reimbursable under Medicare, are not defensible clinically, and may constitute unauthorized practice. This policy ensures that all physician orders are obtained before services are rendered (except in clinical emergencies followed immediately by physician notification), are properly documented in the clinical record, are authenticated within required timeframes, and are maintained in a manner that supports the clinical record's integrity, billing compliance, and survey defensibility.
### 3. Scope
This policy applies to:
All registered nurses and licensed vocational nurses receiving, transcribing, or documenting physician orders
All clinical disciplines (PT, OT, SLP, MSW) receiving discipline-specific orders
Physicians, nurse practitioners, clinical nurse specialists, and physician assistants issuing orders
Medical Records staff responsible for order management in the EHR
Clinical Coordinators managing physician order tracking
The Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager
Revenue Cycle staff verifying order support for billed services
This policy does not govern OASIS assessment time points or recertification processes specifically (see CL-CA-004 and CL-CP-008), though all orders generated at those junctures fall under this policy.
### 4. Policy Statement
4.1 No skilled home health service shall be provided to any patient without a valid, current physician order authorizing that service. This requirement applies to all disciplines, all visit types, and all clinical interventions including medications, treatments, procedures, equipment, and supplies.
4.2 All physician orders shall be obtained from a physician, nurse practitioner, clinical nurse specialist, or physician assistant who is legally authorized to practice in California, who is not excluded from participation in federal healthcare programs, and who does not have a financial relationship with the agency that violates the Stark Law or Anti-Kickback Statute.
4.3 Written orders from the physician are the preferred format. Verbal orders are permissible when a written order cannot be obtained in advance of a clinical need, provided they are received and documented per policy CL-CP-004 and authenticated by the physician within the timeframes specified in Section 6.3.
4.4 All orders shall be specific, legible, dated, and signed (for written orders) or documented and authenticated (for verbal orders). Orders containing ambiguous language, missing elements, or requiring clinical interpretation shall not be executed without clarification from the ordering physician.
4.5 All orders in effect for a patient shall be current, consistent with the active plan of care, and reflected in the patient's medication and treatment lists. No order may be executed beyond its effective date or outside its specified scope without renewal or modification.
4.6 The agency shall maintain a complete and organized Order Management Record in each patient's clinical record, documenting every order received, the date received, the ordering physician, and the authentication status.
4.7 Physician orders and the services delivered under those orders must be in alignment. The Revenue Cycle team shall not bill for any service that is not supported by a dated, authenticated physician order on file, consistent with policy CO-DC-004.
### 5. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Physician Order | A directive issued by a physician or allowed practitioner that authorizes a specific clinical service, treatment, medication, or intervention for a patient. In home health, orders may be written or verbal. |
| Written Order | An order communicated in writing — whether on paper, via fax, via secure email, or via a physician portal — and signed by the ordering physician at the time of issuance. |
| Verbal Order | An oral communication from a physician or allowed practitioner to a qualified clinician that authorizes a specific clinical action. Verbal orders are governed in detail by policy CL-CP-004. |
| Authentication | The process by which a physician reviews, confirms, and signs a transcribed verbal order, confirming that the order as transcribed reflects what was communicated. |
| Allowed Practitioner | A nurse practitioner (NP), clinical nurse specialist (CNS), or physician assistant (PA) authorized under 42 CFR § 424.22 and California state law to issue home health orders. |
| Standing Order | A pre-established written order that authorizes a clinician to perform a defined action under defined clinical conditions without obtaining a new order each time. Standing orders must be physician-approved, date-specific, and patient-specific. |
| Order Set | A pre-defined, physician-approved group of orders that are commonly ordered together for a specific condition or clinical scenario. Order sets must be individually reviewed and approved for each patient. |
| Order Clarification | Communication between a clinician and the ordering physician to resolve an ambiguous, incomplete, or potentially unsafe order before execution. |
| Change Order | An order that modifies an existing order — for example, changing a medication dose, changing a visit frequency, or adding a new service. |
| Discharge Order | An order from the physician authorizing discharge of the patient from home health services. |

### 6. Procedures
#### 6.1 Obtaining Physician Orders — General Requirements

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.1.1 | Assigned RN / Clinical Discipline | Before providing any new service, treatment, medication, or clinical intervention that is not already covered by a current active physician order, contact the ordering physician or allowed practitioner to obtain an order. Verbal orders are acceptable where a written order cannot be obtained in advance, per policy CL-CP-004. | Before service is rendered. |
| 6.1.2 | Assigned RN | Verify that the individual issuing the order is: (a) a licensed physician, NP, CNS, or PA legally authorized to practice in California; (b) not on the OIG exclusion list (verified at the time of initial engagement with the agency and at least annually thereafter per HR-TA-003); (c) the patient's certifying or attending physician, or a covering physician authorized to issue orders for this patient. If there is uncertainty about the ordering individual's authority, do not accept the order and immediately contact the Director of Nursing. | Before accepting any order. |
| 6.1.3 | All Clinicians | Do not accept orders that are: (a) undated; (b) unsigned (for written orders); (c) unsigned after the required authentication period (for verbal orders); (d) ambiguous regarding the service, dosage, route, or frequency; (e) outside the scope of the plan of care without a corresponding plan modification. Contact the physician for clarification before proceeding with any order that has these deficiencies. | Before executing any deficient order. |
| 6.1.4 | Assigned RN | Document all new orders in the patient's Order Management Record in the EHR within 24 hours of receipt. Include: (a) the order date; (b) the name and credential of the ordering physician; (c) the order type (written or verbal); (d) the complete order content; (e) the date and method of receipt; (f) authentication status and expected authentication date for verbal orders. | Within 24 hours of receipt. |

#### 6.2 Written Order Management

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.2.1 | Medical Records / Assigned RN | Upon receipt of a written order from the physician, verify that the order is: (a) legible; (b) dated; (c) signed by the ordering physician; (d) sufficiently specific to authorize the intended service without clinical interpretation. If any element is missing, return the order to the physician for correction before it is entered into the EHR as active. | Within 24 hours of receipt. |
| 6.2.2 | Medical Records / Assigned RN | Enter the written order into the EHR Order Management Record. Mark the order as "Written — Signed" and document the date received and the date entered. | Within 24 hours of receipt and verification. |
| 6.2.3 | Medical Records / Clinical Coordinator | File the original written order (or a verified electronic copy if received via fax or portal) in the patient's clinical record. Ensure the order is accessible to all treating clinicians. | Within 3 calendar days of receipt; original retained minimum 7 years. |
| 6.2.4 | Assigned RN | Verify that every service delivered to the patient is covered by a current, active written or authenticated verbal order. If a service is delivered before a written order is received (under an authorized verbal order), confirm that the verbal order is being tracked for authentication per CL-CP-004. | Before each visit; continuous. |

#### 6.3 Verbal Order Authentication

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.3.1 | Assigned RN | All verbal orders shall be authenticated by the ordering physician within 7 calendar days of the verbal order being given, per California Nursing Practice Act requirements and agency policy CL-CP-004. | Within 7 calendar days of the verbal order. |
| 6.3.2 | Clinical Coordinator | Track all outstanding verbal order authentications in the physician order tracking system per policy CL-CP-009. Flag any verbal order that has not been returned for authentication within 5 calendar days of issuance and initiate follow-up with the physician's office. | Follow-up initiated at 5 calendar days; escalated at 7 calendar days. |
| 6.3.3 | Director of Nursing | Any verbal order that has not been authenticated within 7 calendar days shall be escalated to the Director of Nursing. The Director of Nursing shall contact the physician directly by telephone and document the contact. | On Day 7 from issuance if not returned. |
| 6.3.4 | Revenue Cycle | No claim shall be submitted for a service authorized by a verbal order that has not been authenticated within the required timeframe. If an unauthenticated order is identified on a previously submitted claim, notify the Compliance Officer immediately per CO-DC-004. | At the time of claim preparation; ongoing compliance monitoring. |

#### 6.4 Emergency Orders

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.4.1 | Clinician at the Patient's Home | In a clinical emergency where immediate action is required to protect the patient's safety and the treating clinician determines that a service is clinically necessary before a physician order can be obtained, the clinician may take the minimum clinical action necessary to stabilize the patient. | Immediately as clinically required. |
| 6.4.2 | Clinician at the Patient's Home | Simultaneously with or immediately following the emergency action, contact the physician (or covering physician or on-call physician) to report the situation and obtain a verbal order ratifying the action taken. If no physician is available, activate the agency's after-hours on-call clinical protocol per OP-SL-002. | Physician contact initiated within 15 minutes of the emergency action. |
| 6.4.3 | Clinician at the Patient's Home | If the situation requires emergency medical services, call 911 immediately. Notify the Director of Nursing of the emergency within 2 hours of the event regardless of its resolution. | 911: immediately. Director of Nursing notification: within 2 hours. |
| 6.4.4 | Assigned RN / Clinician | Document the emergency action in the visit note including: (a) the clinical finding that necessitated action; (b) the action taken; (c) the physician contacted and the verbal order received; (d) the patient's response to the intervention; (e) any referral to emergency services. | Within 24 hours of the visit; emergency visit note shall be immediately flagged for Director of Nursing review. |

#### 6.5 Order Changes and Discontinuation

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.5.1 | Assigned RN | When a change order is received (modifying an existing order), immediately update the patient's plan of care in the EHR to reflect the change. Mark the previous order as superseded and document the date the change was received. | Within 24 hours of receiving the change order. |
| 6.5.2 | Assigned RN | Notify all disciplines affected by an order change within 24 hours. Document the notification in the clinical record. | Within 24 hours of the order change. |
| 6.5.3 | Assigned RN | When a service is discontinued by physician order, immediately update the plan of care and notify the affected discipline. If the patient is a home health aide patient, coordinate the HHA scheduling change with the Operations team. Document all notifications. | Within 24 hours of discontinuation order. |

#### 6.6 Escalation and Exception Handling

| Condition | Escalation Path | Corrective Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| An order is received from an individual who cannot be verified as an authorized prescriber | Clinician immediately contacts Director of Nursing | Director of Nursing investigates the ordering individual's credentials and refuses to execute the order until authorization is confirmed. If the individual is confirmed to be unauthorized, report to Compliance Officer. | Verification required before order execution; Compliance Officer notification within 24 hours of confirmation of unauthorized ordering. |
| A clinician executes a service without any order | Director of Nursing reviews upon identification | Director of Nursing retroactively contacts the physician for ratification order. Assesses for billing compliance. Reports to Compliance Officer. Provides corrective counseling to the clinician. | Physician contact within 24 hours; Compliance Officer notification within 48 hours. |
| An order contains a medication dose or route that appears clinically unsafe | Receiving clinician contacts Director of Nursing before executing | Director of Nursing contacts the physician to clarify the order. Do not execute the order until clarification is received. Document the concern, the contact, and the physician's response. | Do not execute; physician clarification before execution; full documentation within 24 hours. |
| Physician refuses to authenticate a verbal order and denies giving it | Director of Nursing contacts physician directly | Director of Nursing reviews the clinical situation and the order transcription. If the order was legitimately given, document all facts. If the order is in dispute, consult the Compliance Officer and Legal Counsel if needed. Do not bill for any service under a disputed, unauthenticated order. | Director of Nursing contact within 24 hours; Compliance Officer within 48 hours if unresolved. |

### 7. Documentation Requirements

| Requirement | Document / Record | Responsible Party | Location | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Order Management Record | Complete log of all physician orders for each patient including order type, date, content, and authentication status | Assigned RN / Medical Records | EHR — Order Management module | Updated within 24 hours of each order receipt; retained minimum 7 years |
| Original written orders | Original signed orders or verified electronic copies | Medical Records | EHR or physical order file | Filed within 3 calendar days of receipt; retained minimum 7 years |
| Verbal order documentation | Transcribed verbal order per CL-CP-004 with tracking for physician authentication | Receiving Clinician | EHR — Order Management module | Documented within 24 hours of verbal order; authenticated within 7 calendar days |
| Emergency action documentation | Visit note documenting emergency actions, physician contact, and verbal order | Treating Clinician | EHR — visit note | Within 24 hours of the visit; flagged for Director of Nursing review |
| Order clarification documentation | Documentation of contact with physician regarding ambiguous or deficient orders | Assigned RN | EHR — communication notes | Within 24 hours of contact; retained minimum 7 years |
| Policy acknowledgment | Signed acknowledgment (Appendix A) | Each individual; Administrator (collection) | Policy acknowledgment file | Within 14 calendar days of effective date, revision, or hire |

### 8. Compliance & Audit Considerations
#### 8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

| Compliance Indicator | Measurement Method | Acceptable Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| All services delivered under active physician orders | Monthly audit cross-referencing visit delivery records with active orders | Zero services delivered without a current active order on audited records |
| All verbal orders authenticated within 7 calendar days | Physician order tracking report — authentication date vs. verbal order date | ≥98% of verbal orders authenticated within 7 calendar days |
| No claims submitted without authenticated orders | Revenue Cycle pre-bill order verification | Zero claims submitted without a signed or authenticated order on file |
| No ambiguous or deficient orders executed without clarification | Director of Nursing review of order clarification documentation | All identified deficient orders have documented clarification before execution |

#### 8.2 What Surveyors and Auditors Will Look For
Surveyors will request clinical records and cross-reference every service in visit notes against the physician orders on file. They will specifically verify that verbal orders are authenticated and that no service was rendered outside the scope of an active order. Missing or unauthenticated orders linked to billed services are False Claims Act risk items and are commonly referred for further investigation.
#### 8.3 Common Failure Points

| Failure Point | Risk | Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Verbal orders not authenticated within 7 days | Billing compliance risk; survey deficiency; unauthenticated orders not billable | CL-CP-009 tracking system; Director of Nursing escalation at Day 5 |
| Services added mid-episode without new orders | False Claims Act risk; survey citation | Train all clinicians that any service change requires a new order; audit monthly per CO-DC-004 |
| Ambiguous orders executed without clarification | Patient safety risk; liability exposure | Train all clinicians on order clarification requirement; Director of Nursing open-door policy for order questions |
| Orders not consistently entered in EHR within 24 hours | Documentation gap; audit trail failure | EHR order entry workflow monitoring by Director of Nursing |

### 10. Training & Acknowledgment Requirements
10.1 All clinicians authorized to receive physician orders shall receive competency-validated training on order management requirements within 14 calendar days of hire and annually thereafter, including: (a) what constitutes a valid written vs. verbal order; (b) the elements required for a complete order; (c) the order clarification process for ambiguous orders; (d) the verbal order authentication requirement and timeline; (e) the EHR Order Management workflow; (f) consequences of executing services without orders.
10.2 All personnel within scope shall sign the Policy Acknowledgment Form (Appendix A) within 14 calendar days of the effective date, any revision, or hire.
