## 2. Purpose
This policy defines the requirements for clinical supervision of all professional and paraprofessional staff providing patient care at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. Clinical supervision is the systematic process by which the agency ensures that all clinical services are delivered safely, competently, and in accordance with the plan of care, professional standards, and regulatory requirements. This policy establishes the supervision structure, frequency, documentation requirements, and escalation procedures for the oversight of RNs, LVNs, PTs, PTAs, OTs, COTAs, SLPs, MSWs, and HHAs. It implements the requirements of 42 CFR § 484.75 (skilled professional services) and 42 CFR § 484.80 (home health aide services) as they relate to clinical supervision.
## 3. Scope
This policy applies to the Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager, all clinical supervisors (RNs, PTs, OTs), all supervised staff (LVNs, PTAs, COTAs, HHAs), and all professional staff (RNs, PTs, OTs, SLPs, MSWs) subject to administrative and clinical oversight.
## 4. Policy Statement
4.1 The Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager is responsible for the oversight and supervision of all clinical services provided by the agency, as required by 42 CFR § 484.115(b). The Director of Nursing shall be a registered nurse who is currently licensed in California, meets the CMS qualification requirements, and has the authority and accountability to ensure the clinical quality and regulatory compliance of all services.
4.2 The supervision structure shall operate at three levels:
Level 1 — Director of Nursing Oversight: The Director of Nursing provides enterprise-level clinical oversight of all disciplines and clinical functions, including: review of clinical outcomes, quality indicators, documentation compliance, and survey readiness.
Level 2 — Discipline-Specific Professional Supervision: Licensed professionals (PTs, OTs) supervise their respective assistants (PTAs, COTAs) per discipline-specific practice act requirements. RNs supervise LVNs. These supervisory relationships are defined in the discipline-specific service policies (CL-SD-001 through CL-SD-007).
Level 3 — HHA Supervision: RNs (or therapists, when applicable) supervise HHAs per the 14-day supervisory visit schedule defined in CL-SD-006.
4.3 The Director of Nursing shall conduct a supervisory review of each clinical discipline at minimum monthly, covering: (a) documentation quality and timeliness; (b) plan of care adherence; (c) visit frequency compliance; (d) clinical outcomes and patient satisfaction; (e) competency concerns identified.
4.4 The Director of Nursing shall conduct a direct on-site supervisory visit with each clinician at minimum once during their first 60 days of employment and at least annually thereafter. For clinicians with identified performance concerns, the Director of Nursing shall increase the frequency of supervisory visits to no less than monthly until the concern is resolved.
4.5 All supervisory activities shall be documented including: the date, supervisor name, staff member supervised, observations made, findings, any corrective guidance provided, and any follow-up actions required.
4.6 If a supervisor identifies a clinical practice deficiency that poses a risk to patient safety, the supervisor shall: (a) immediately address the safety concern; (b) remove the staff member from the clinical situation if warranted; (c) report the event to the Director of Nursing within 4 hours; (d) initiate incident reporting per RM-ER-002 if patient harm has occurred or was narrowly avoided.
## 5. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Clinical Supervision | The ongoing process of overseeing, evaluating, and directing the clinical work of staff to ensure safe, competent, and compliant patient care delivery. |
| Supervisory Visit | An on-site visit by a supervisor to observe, assess, and evaluate a staff member's clinical performance during patient care delivery. |
| Administrative Supervision | Oversight of non-clinical aspects of a staff member's performance including scheduling compliance, documentation timeliness, and policy adherence. |
| Clinical Oversight | The Director of Nursing's enterprise-level responsibility for monitoring and ensuring the quality, safety, and compliance of all clinical operations. |
| Corrective Guidance | Verbal or written instruction provided by a supervisor to address identified deficiencies in a staff member's clinical practice. |

## 6. Procedures
### 6.1 Director of Nursing Monthly Clinical Review

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.1.1 | Director of Nursing | Conduct a monthly review of each clinical discipline covering: documentation quality (random chart audit of ≥5% of each discipline's visit notes), plan of care adherence, visit frequency compliance (comparing delivered visits to ordered visits), clinical outcome indicators, patient complaint trending, and competency evaluation status. | Monthly. |
| 6.1.2 | Director of Nursing | Document findings in a Monthly Clinical Supervision Report. Identify discipline-specific trends, individual performance concerns, and system-level issues. Assign corrective actions with responsible parties and timelines. | Within 5 business days of the review period end. |
| 6.1.3 | Director of Nursing | Present summary findings to the Administrator and QAPI Committee at least quarterly per QA-PG-003. | Quarterly. |

### 6.2 New Employee Clinical Supervision

| 6.2.2 | Director of Nursing / Preceptor | Conduct at least one on-site supervisory visit (joint home visit with the new employee and preceptor) within the first 30 days of employment. | Within the first 30 days. |

Determine whether the employee is approved for independent practice or requires extended supervision. Document the determination. | At Day 60 of employment. |

The visit shall include observation of the clinician's assessment technique, patient interaction, clinical judgment, and documentation practices. | Annually; more frequently for performance concerns. |

| 6.3.3 | Director of Nursing | For clinicians with identified performance concerns, increase the supervisory frequency to at minimum monthly and develop a Performance Improvement Plan in coordination with HR per HR-ER-001. | Increased supervision begins within 7 calendar days of concern identification. |

Document all supervisory reviews and visits. | Per the schedules in the respective policies. |

# CL-SD-009 — Telehealth & Remote Monitoring Services
## 1. Policy Header

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Policy ID | CL-SD-009 |
| Policy Title | Telehealth & Remote Monitoring Services |
| Domain | CL — Clinical Operations |
| Subdomain | SD — Service Delivery |
| Classification Tier | RECOMMENDED |
| Status | ACTIVE |
| Review Cycle | Annual |
| Access Tier | Tier 2 — Restricted |
| Policy Owner / Steward | Director of Nursing |
| Effective Date | 2025-07-10 |
| Version | 1.0 |
| Approved By | Governing Body Chair — Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. |
| Last Reviewed | 2025-07-10 |
| Next Review Date | 2026-07-10 |
| Supersedes | N/A (Initial Version) |

## 2. Purpose
This policy establishes the standards for the delivery, documentation, and oversight of telehealth services and remote patient monitoring (RPM) at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. Telehealth and RPM technologies represent supplemental tools that can enhance patient monitoring, improve clinical outcomes, support earlier intervention, and reduce unnecessary hospitalizations — but they do not replace in-person skilled visits. Under current CMS rules, telehealth encounters are not counted as billable home health visits for Medicare payment purposes (though this may evolve with future CMS rulemaking). This policy ensures that telehealth services are used appropriately to complement the plan of care, are properly documented, and do not substitute for required in-person visits.
## 3. Scope
This policy applies to all clinical staff using telehealth or RPM technology with patients, the Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager, IT staff supporting telehealth platforms, and Operations staff managing telehealth scheduling.
## 4. Policy Statement
4.1 Telehealth services at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. include video visits, telephone encounters, and remote patient monitoring (e.g., automated transmission of vital signs, weight, blood glucose, oxygen saturation) used as supplements to the physician-approved plan of care.
4.2 Telehealth encounters shall not be used as a substitute for required in-person skilled visits. The agency shall ensure that all visits counted for Medicare billing purposes are in-person visits conducted in the patient's home. Telehealth encounters may supplement — but not replace — the visit frequencies specified in the plan of care.
4.3 All telehealth services shall be authorized by a physician order, reflected in the plan of care, and documented in the patient's clinical record. The plan of care shall specify the type of telehealth service, frequency, clinical parameters to be monitored, and the responsible clinician.
4.4 Patient consent for telehealth services shall be obtained and documented before initiating telehealth. The consent shall address: (a) the nature of telehealth services; (b) how the patient's data will be transmitted, stored, and used; (c) the patient's right to refuse telehealth and receive in-person services instead; (d) that telehealth does not replace in-person emergency services and the patient should call 911 in an emergency.
4.5 All telehealth technology used by the agency shall comply with HIPAA security requirements per CO-HP-002. Only agency-approved, encrypted platforms shall be used for video visits or data transmission. Consumer-grade, non-encrypted platforms (e.g., standard SMS, non-HIPAA-compliant video apps) shall not be used for clinical communications involving PHI.
4.6 RPM data shall be reviewed by the assigned clinician at minimum daily for actively monitored patients, or per the frequency specified in the plan of care. Clinically significant data (vital signs outside defined parameters, weight changes indicating fluid retention, blood glucose outside target range) shall trigger a same-day clinical response including patient contact, physician notification, and visit scheduling as clinically indicated.
4.7 The Director of Nursing shall ensure that all clinicians using telehealth are trained on the technology, documentation requirements, and clinical protocols specific to telehealth encounters.
4.8 Telehealth and RPM services shall be integrated into the agency's QAPI program per QA-PG-001, with outcome metrics tracked including: patient engagement, alert response times, hospitalization rates for RPM patients, and patient satisfaction.
## 5. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Telehealth | The use of telecommunications technology to deliver clinical services remotely, including video visits and telephone encounters, as a supplement to in-person care. |
| Remote Patient Monitoring (RPM) | The use of electronic devices to collect and transmit patient physiological data (vital signs, weight, blood glucose, oxygen saturation) from the patient's home to the agency for clinical review. |
| Video Visit | A live, synchronous audio-visual encounter between a clinician and a patient conducted via a HIPAA-compliant telehealth platform. |
| Telephone Encounter | A clinical interaction conducted by telephone between a clinician and a patient, typically for follow-up, symptom assessment, or care coordination. |
| Alert Threshold | A predefined clinical parameter (e.g., systolic BP >180, weight gain >3 lbs in 24 hours) that, when exceeded, triggers a clinical response protocol. |

## 6. Procedures
### 6.1 Patient Enrollment in Telehealth / RPM

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.1.1 | Assigned RN | Assess the patient's appropriateness for telehealth and/or RPM based on: (a) clinical condition and monitoring needs; (b) patient's or caregiver's ability to use the technology; (c) availability of reliable internet or cellular service; (d) patient's willingness to participate. | At SOC or when telehealth is indicated. |
| 6.1.2 | Assigned RN | Obtain and document the patient's informed consent for telehealth services using the Telehealth Consent Form (Appendix A). | Before initiating telehealth. |
| 6.1.3 | Assigned RN | Obtain a physician order for telehealth and/or RPM services per CL-CP-003. | Before initiating telehealth. |
| 6.1.4 | Assigned RN / IT Support | Set up the telehealth and/or RPM equipment in the patient's home. Provide training to the patient and caregiver on how to use the equipment. Document the training and the patient's demonstrated competency. | During an in-person visit. |
| 6.1.5 | Assigned RN | Establish patient-specific alert thresholds in the RPM platform based on the physician's orders and the patient's clinical parameters. | At the time of RPM setup. |

### 6.2 Telehealth Visit Execution

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.2.1 | Assigned Clinician | Conduct telehealth visits per the plan of care schedule using the agency-approved HIPAA-compliant platform. | Per plan of care. |
| 6.2.2 | Assigned Clinician | Document the telehealth encounter in the patient's EHR within 24 hours including: (a) date, time, and duration of the encounter; (b) platform used; (c) clinical assessment findings (within the limitations of the telehealth modality); (d) patient's reported symptoms and status; (e) interventions provided (education, medication review, care coordination); (f) plan for follow-up. | Within 24 hours. |
| 6.2.3 | Assigned Clinician | Clearly note in the documentation that the encounter was conducted via telehealth and is not counted as an in-person billable visit. | In the visit note. |

### 6.3 RPM Data Review and Response

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.3.1 | Assigned Clinician | Review RPM data at minimum daily for actively monitored patients. Document the review. | Daily or per the plan of care. |
| 6.3.2 | Assigned Clinician | When RPM data exceeds the established alert threshold, contact the patient by telephone within 2 hours to assess the clinical situation. Document the contact and findings. | Within 2 hours of alert. |
| 6.3.3 | Assigned Clinician | If the RPM alert indicates a clinically significant change, notify the physician per CL-CP-005, schedule an in-person visit if clinically warranted, and initiate a plan of care modification per CL-CP-002 if indicated. | Same day as alert. |
| 6.3.4 | Assigned Clinician | If the patient fails to transmit RPM data for 2 consecutive days without notification, contact the patient by telephone to assess the situation. If the patient is unreachable, schedule an in-person visit. | By the end of the 2nd day of non-transmission. |

### 6.4 Escalation and Exception Handling

| Condition | Escalation Path | Corrective Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Patient unable to use telehealth technology | Assigned RN assesses alternatives | Provide additional training or involve caregiver. If technology cannot be managed, discontinue telehealth and rely on in-person visits only. Notify physician. | Within 7 calendar days. |
| RPM data reveals a critical clinical value (e.g., BP >200/120, SpO2 <85%) | Assigned Clinician contacts patient and physician immediately | Instruct the patient to call 911 if emergency is indicated. Arrange an immediate in-person visit if non-emergent but critical. | Immediate contact. |
| HIPAA breach via telehealth platform | Report per CO-HP-003 | Suspend use of the affected platform. Complete breach assessment per CO-HP-003. Notify IT Director. | Platform suspended immediately; breach assessment within 24 hours. |

## 7. Documentation Requirements

| Requirement | Document / Record | Responsible Party | Location | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Telehealth consent | Telehealth Consent Form (Appendix A) | Assigned RN | EHR — consent forms | Before initiating telehealth |
| Telehealth visit note | Encounter documentation per Section 6.2.2 | Assigned Clinician | EHR — clinical notes | Within 24 hours |
| RPM daily data review | Documentation of daily data review and any actions | Assigned Clinician | EHR — RPM monitoring notes | Daily; retained minimum 7 years |
| RPM alert response documentation | Documentation of alert, patient contact, and clinical actions | Assigned Clinician | EHR — clinical notes | Same day as alert |
| Policy acknowledgment | Signed acknowledgment (Appendix B) | Each individual | Policy acknowledgment file | Within 14 calendar days |

## 8. Compliance & Audit Considerations

| Compliance Indicator | Measurement Method | Acceptable Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Telehealth consent on file for all telehealth patients | Chart audit | 100% |
| Telehealth encounters not billed as in-person visits | Billing audit cross-referencing telehealth notes with claims | Zero telehealth encounters billed as in-person visits |
| RPM data reviewed daily for monitored patients | RPM platform review logs | ≥95% of days with documented review |
| Alert response within 2 hours | RPM alert log with response timestamps | ≥95% |

# CL-SD-010 — IV Therapy & Infusion Services
## 1. Policy Header

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Policy ID | CL-SD-010 |
| Policy Title | IV Therapy & Infusion Services |
| Domain | CL — Clinical Operations |
| Subdomain | SD — Service Delivery |
| Classification Tier | ESSENTIAL |
| Status | ACTIVE |
| Review Cycle | Annual |
| Access Tier | Tier 2 — Restricted |
| Policy Owner / Steward | Director of Nursing |
| Effective Date | 2025-07-10 |
| Version | 1.0 |
| Approved By | Governing Body Chair — Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. |
| Last Reviewed | 2025-07-10 |
| Next Review Date | 2026-07-10 |
| Supersedes | N/A (Initial Version) |

## 2. Purpose
This policy defines the clinical standards, competency requirements, safety protocols, and documentation expectations for intravenous (IV) therapy and infusion services provided by Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. IV therapy in the home setting includes peripheral and central venous access device management, IV antibiotic therapy, IV hydration, total parenteral nutrition (TPN), blood product administration (if within scope and authorized by the agency), chemotherapy infusion support (limited scope), and IV medication administration. These are among the highest-risk skilled services provided in home health due to the potential for serious complications including infection (central line-associated bloodstream infections — CLABSI), air embolism, infiltration/extravasation, adverse drug reactions, fluid overload, and anaphylaxis. This policy ensures that all IV therapy services are delivered by competency-validated RNs with the clinical judgment and emergency preparedness to manage complications in the home setting.
## 3. Scope
This policy applies to all RNs providing IV therapy and infusion services, the Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager, Clinical Coordinators scheduling IV visits, pharmacy partners providing IV medications and supplies, and Revenue Cycle staff verifying IV service documentation. LVNs shall not independently administer IV therapy at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. except under direct, on-site RN supervision and only for those IV tasks within the LVN's California BPC § 2859 scope.
## 4. Policy Statement
4.1 IV therapy services shall be authorized by a physician order that specifies: (a) the IV medication or solution; (b) dose, rate, and route (peripheral vs. central); (c) frequency and duration of infusions; (d) vascular access device type; (e) monitoring parameters; (f) laboratory testing schedule if applicable.
4.2 Only RNs who have completed the agency's IV Therapy Competency Program and demonstrated competency in all required IV skills shall be authorized to provide IV therapy services independently. The Director of Nursing shall maintain a current roster of IV-competency-validated RNs.
4.3 The IV Therapy Competency Program shall include demonstrated competency in: (a) peripheral IV insertion and management; (b) central venous access device (CVAD) management including PICC lines, Port-a-Cath access, and tunneled catheters; (c) IV medication preparation and administration; (d) infusion pump operation and troubleshooting; (e) aseptic technique and central line bundle compliance; (f) recognition and management of IV therapy complications (infiltration, extravasation, phlebitis, air embolism, catheter-related bloodstream infection, anaphylaxis); (g) emergency response for IV-related adverse events in the home setting.
4.4 Before each IV infusion, the administering RN shall: (a) verify the physician order; (b) verify patient identity using two identifiers per OP-PA-002; (c) verify the medication using the "Five Rights" (right patient, right medication, right dose, right route, right time); (d) assess the vascular access device site for signs of infection, displacement, or malfunction; (e) verify IV solution integrity (expiration date, clarity, absence of particles); (f) confirm availability of emergency supplies including anaphylaxis kit.
4.5 The RN shall remain with the patient during the initial 15 minutes of any new IV medication infusion to monitor for adverse reactions, and shall remain for the duration of any high-risk infusion (first-dose antibiotics, blood products, chemotherapy agents).
4.6 All central line care shall follow the agency's Central Line Bundle Protocol (Appendix A), which includes: hand hygiene before access; chlorhexidine skin antisepsis; sterile barrier precautions during dressing changes; optimal catheter site care; and daily assessment of line necessity.
4.7 All IV therapy complications and adverse events shall be reported to the physician immediately, documented in the clinical record, and reported through the agency's incident reporting system per RM-ER-002.
4.8 The agency shall coordinate with the infusion pharmacy for medication procurement, compounding, delivery, and clinical support. The agency shall verify that the pharmacy holds appropriate state and federal licenses.
## 5. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Peripheral IV Access | Intravenous access established through a peripheral vein, typically in the hand, forearm, or antecubital fossa, using a peripheral IV catheter. |
| Central Venous Access Device (CVAD) | A vascular access device with the distal tip positioned in a large central vein, including PICC lines, tunneled catheters, and implanted ports. |
| PICC (Peripherally Inserted Central Catheter) | A central venous catheter inserted through a peripheral vein with the tip advanced to the superior vena cava. |
| Infiltration | The inadvertent administration of IV solution into the surrounding tissue rather than the vein. |
| Extravasation | The inadvertent administration of a vesicant medication into surrounding tissue, causing tissue damage. |
| Central Line Bundle | An evidence-based set of practices performed together to reduce central line-associated bloodstream infections (CLABSI). |
| Anaphylaxis | A severe, potentially life-threatening allergic reaction that can occur rapidly during IV medication administration. |
| Five Rights | A safety verification protocol: right patient, right medication, right dose, right route, right time. |

## 6. Procedures
### 6.1 Pre-Infusion Assessment and Preparation

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.1.1 | Assigned RN | Before each IV visit, review: the physician order including any recent changes; the patient's current medication list for potential drug interactions; recent laboratory results relevant to the infusion (e.g., trough levels for vancomycin, renal function for nephrotoxic drugs); the patient's allergy list. | Before departure for the visit. |
| 6.1.2 | Assigned RN | Verify that all required supplies and medications are available and not expired, including: IV solution or medication, administration set, flush supplies, dressing change supplies (if CVAD), infusion pump (if required), anaphylaxis kit (epinephrine, diphenhydramine, syringes, 911 contact). | Before departure. |
| 6.1.3 | Assigned RN | Upon arrival, verify patient identity using two identifiers. Perform pre-infusion assessment: vital signs (baseline before infusion), vascular access site assessment, current symptoms, and any patient-reported concerns since the last visit. | At the start of the visit. |
| 6.1.4 | Assigned RN | Verify the medication using the Five Rights protocol. If there is any discrepancy between the physician order and the medication on hand, do not administer — contact the physician and pharmacy. | Before administration. |

### 6.2 IV Administration

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.2.1 | Assigned RN | Access the vascular device using aseptic technique. For CVADs, follow the Central Line Bundle Protocol (Appendix A). Perform a normal saline flush before medication administration to verify line patency. | Before each infusion. |
| 6.2.2 | Assigned RN | Initiate the infusion at the physician-ordered rate. Set infusion pump alarms if applicable. Remain with the patient for at least the first 15 minutes of any new medication or the full duration for high-risk infusions. | During infusion. |
| 6.2.3 | Assigned RN | Monitor the patient throughout the infusion for: vital sign changes; signs of adverse reaction (rash, hives, pruritus, dyspnea, chest tightness, hypotension, facial/tongue swelling); signs of infiltration or extravasation (swelling, pain, blanching at the IV site); signs of fluid overload (dyspnea, edema, crackles on auscultation). | Throughout infusion. |
| 6.2.4 | Assigned RN | Upon completion of the infusion, flush the vascular access device per protocol. Apply heparin lock or saline lock as ordered. Assess the patient's post-infusion status. Document post-infusion vital signs. | At infusion completion. |

### 6.3 Vascular Access Device Management

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.3.1 | Assigned RN | For patients with CVADs, perform site assessment and dressing change per the Central Line Bundle Protocol (Appendix A) at minimum every 7 calendar days for transparent dressings, every 48 hours for gauze dressings, and immediately if the dressing is soiled, damp, or loosened. | Per the dressing change schedule. |
| 6.3.2 | Assigned RN | Assess CVAD site at each visit for: redness, swelling, tenderness, drainage, catheter migration, and signs of infection. Document all findings. | At each visit. |
| 6.3.3 | Assigned RN | If signs of CVAD infection are identified (fever, site redness/drainage, bacteremia symptoms), immediately notify the physician, obtain orders for blood cultures and site cultures if ordered, and document all findings and actions. | Immediately upon identification. |

### 6.4 Emergency Response for IV Complications

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.4.1 | Assigned RN | If anaphylaxis is suspected: (a) stop the infusion immediately; (b) maintain the IV line with normal saline; (c) administer epinephrine per the physician's standing order or emergency protocol; (d) call 911; (e) monitor vital signs continuously; (f) notify the physician; (g) stay with the patient until emergency services arrive. | Immediately. |
| 6.4.2 | Assigned RN | If infiltration or extravasation occurs: (a) stop the infusion; (b) assess the severity using a standardized infiltration scale; (c) for vesicant extravasation, follow the agency's extravasation protocol including aspiration of residual drug, antidote administration if applicable, and physician notification; (d) elevate the affected extremity; (e) document. | Immediately upon identification. |
| 6.4.3 | Assigned RN | If suspected air embolism: (a) clamp the line; (b) position the patient in left lateral Trendelenburg; (c) administer oxygen; (d) call 911; (e) notify the physician. | Immediately. |
| 6.4.4 | Assigned RN | Report all IV-related complications through the agency's incident reporting system per RM-ER-002. | Within 24 hours of the event. |

### 6.5 Escalation and Exception Handling

| Condition | Escalation Path | Corrective Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Non-IV-competency-validated RN assigned to an IV patient | Director of Nursing identifies during scheduling review | Immediately reassign the patient to an IV-competency-validated RN. | Immediate reassignment. |
| IV medication received from pharmacy appears compromised (discoloration, particles, expired) | RN does not administer; contacts pharmacy and Director of Nursing | Do not administer. Contact pharmacy for replacement. Report per RM-PS-003 if a product safety concern is identified. | Do not administer; replacement requested immediately. |
| Patient requests self-administration of IV therapy | Assigned RN assesses capability; consults Director of Nursing and physician | Only with physician order, documented competency training of patient/caregiver, and a written self-administration protocol. RN continues supervisory visits. | Physician order and competency documentation before self-administration. |

## 7. Documentation Requirements

| Requirement | Document / Record | Responsible Party | Location | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Pre-infusion assessment | Vital signs, site assessment, medication verification | Assigned RN | EHR — visit note | At the start of each IV visit |
| Infusion administration record | Medication, dose, rate, route, start/stop times, patient tolerance | Assigned RN | EHR — visit note | At each infusion; within 24 hours |
| Post-infusion assessment | Vital signs, patient status, site assessment | Assigned RN | EHR — visit note | At infusion completion |
| CVAD dressing change documentation | Site condition, dressing type, observations | Assigned RN | EHR — visit note | At each dressing change |
| Complication and adverse event reports | Incident report per RM-ER-002 | Assigned RN | Incident reporting system and EHR | Within 24 hours of event |
| IV competency roster | List of IV-competency-validated RNs | Director of Nursing | Director of Nursing supervisory file | Updated continuously |
| Policy acknowledgment | Signed acknowledgment (Appendix B) | Each individual | Policy acknowledgment file | Within 14 calendar days |

## 8. Compliance & Audit Considerations

| --- | --- | --- |
| Only IV-competency-validated RNs provide IV therapy | Cross-reference IV visit assignments with competency roster | 100% |
| Five Rights verification documented for each infusion | Chart audit | ≥98% |
| Central Line Bundle Protocol followed for all CVAD dressing changes | Chart audit | ≥95% |
| All IV complications reported through incident reporting | Incident report log vs. clinical notes with documented complications | 100% |
| CVAD site assessed and documented at each IV visit | Chart audit | 100% |

10.1 All RNs assigned to provide IV therapy shall complete the agency's IV Therapy Competency Program before independently performing IV services. The program shall include didactic content, skills lab/simulation, and proctored clinical competency evaluation.

# CL-SD-011 — Wound Care Assessment & Management
## 1. Policy Header

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Policy ID | CL-SD-011 |
| Policy Title | Wound Care Assessment & Management |
| Domain | CL — Clinical Operations |
| Subdomain | SD — Service Delivery |
| Classification Tier | ESSENTIAL |
| Status | ACTIVE |
| Review Cycle | Annual |
| Access Tier | Tier 2 — Restricted |
| Policy Owner / Steward | Director of Nursing |
| Effective Date | 2025-07-10 |
| Version | 1.0 |
| Approved By | Governing Body Chair — Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. |
| Last Reviewed | 2025-07-10 |
| Next Review Date | 2026-07-10 |
| Supersedes | N/A (Initial Version) |

## 2. Purpose
This policy defines the assessment, classification, treatment, documentation, and outcome monitoring standards for wound care services at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. Wound care is among the most frequently provided skilled nursing services in home health, encompassing a wide range of wound types including pressure injuries (pressure ulcers), surgical wounds, diabetic foot ulcers, venous stasis ulcers, arterial ulcers, traumatic wounds, skin tears, and ostomy site management. Wound care documentation is heavily scrutinized during CMS surveys, ADR audits, and OASIS validation reviews because wound status directly affects OASIS scoring (particularly M1311–M1350), PDGM clinical grouping and payment, and quality measure reporting. Inaccurate wound assessment, inconsistent wound staging, or incomplete documentation can result in: PDGM payment errors, OASIS accuracy deficiencies, quality measure underperformance, survey citations under 42 CFR § 484.60 and § 484.75, and patient harm from inadequate treatment. This policy ensures that all wound care is evidence-based, accurately documented, and aligned with CMS OASIS guidance.
## 3. Scope
This policy applies to all RNs and LVNs providing wound care services, the Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager, all clinicians completing OASIS wound items, and Revenue Cycle staff relying on wound documentation for coding and billing.
## 4. Policy Statement
4.1 All wound care services shall be authorized by a physician order specifying: the wound location, wound care procedure, dressing type and frequency, and any wound-related medications (e.g., topical antibiotics, enzymatic debriding agents).
4.2 At SOC and at each OASIS assessment time point, all wounds shall be assessed, classified, staged (for pressure injuries), measured, and documented using the standardized Wound Assessment Documentation Template (Appendix A) that includes all elements necessary for accurate OASIS item completion (M1311 through M1350).
4.3 Wound assessment shall include at minimum: (a) wound location (anatomical site); (b) wound etiology (pressure injury, surgical, diabetic, venous, arterial, traumatic, other); (c) wound stage/classification — using the National Pressure Injury Advisory Panel (NPIAP) staging system for pressure injuries, and the appropriate classification system for other wound types; (d) wound measurements — length x width x depth in centimeters; (e) wound bed description — percentage of granulation, epithelialization, slough, eschar, necrosis; (f) wound edge and periwound skin condition; (g) drainage — type (serous, sanguineous, serosanguineous, purulent), amount (scant, small, moderate, large); (h) signs of infection — erythema, warmth, edema, odor, increased drainage, dehiscence; (i) pain at the wound site; (j) current treatment being applied.
4.4 Wound photographs shall be obtained at SOC, at each recertification, and whenever a significant change in wound status occurs — with patient consent and in compliance with HIPAA per CO-HP-001. Photographs shall be taken with consistent technique (ruler for scale, consistent lighting, perpendicular angle) and stored in the patient's clinical record.
4.5 All wound care treatments shall follow evidence-based clinical practice guidelines (NPIAP/EPUAP/PPPIA for pressure injuries; Society for Vascular Surgery/American Venous Forum for venous ulcers; WOCN guidelines). The clinician shall document the clinical rationale for the selected treatment approach.
4.6 The assessing clinician shall ensure that OASIS wound items (M1311–M1350) are coded accurately and are consistent with the narrative wound assessment documentation in the visit note per CL-OA-007. Any discrepancy between the OASIS wound coding and the wound assessment documentation is a documentation integrity failure subject to CO-DC-001.
4.7 Wound status shall be monitored at each nursing visit, with a formal comparison to baseline status at minimum every 2 weeks. If the wound is not showing expected progress within 2–4 weeks of treatment, the RN shall: (a) reassess the treatment approach; (b) consult the Director of Nursing; (c) notify the physician with a recommendation for treatment modification; (d) consider wound care specialist referral if available.
4.8 The Director of Nursing shall ensure that all RNs and LVNs providing wound care have demonstrated competency in wound assessment, staging, measurement, treatment techniques, and OASIS wound item coding.
## 5. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Pressure Injury | Localized damage to the skin and/or underlying tissue, usually over a bony prominence or related to a medical device, resulting from sustained pressure or pressure in combination with shear. Staged per NPIAP system (Stage 1, Stage 2, Stage 3, Stage 4, Unstageable, Deep Tissue Pressure Injury). |
| NPIAP Staging | The National Pressure Injury Advisory Panel classification system for pressure injuries — the only staging system accepted by CMS for OASIS purposes. |
| Reverse Staging | The clinically incorrect practice of assigning a lower stage number to a healing pressure injury. Once a pressure injury is staged at Stage 3 or 4, it retains that stage designation forever — a healing Stage 4 is documented as "Stage 4, healing" not downstaged to Stage 3 or 2. |
| Wound Bed | The visible tissue in the base of the wound, classified as granulation tissue, epithelial tissue, slough, eschar, or necrotic tissue. |
| Undermining | Tissue destruction underlying intact skin along wound margins, measured by probing with a cotton-tipped applicator. |
| Tunneling | A channel that extends from any part of the wound through subcutaneous tissue or muscle, creating a passageway. |
| Wound Measurement | Length (longest dimension head to toe) x Width (widest dimension side to side, perpendicular to length) x Depth (deepest point from wound edge to wound base), measured in centimeters. |
| Periwound Skin | The tissue surrounding the wound, assessed for maceration, erythema, induration, and other changes. |

## 6. Procedures
### 6.1 Initial Wound Assessment at SOC

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.1.1 | Assigned RN | At the SOC visit, perform a complete skin assessment to identify all wounds — do not rely solely on the referral documentation for wound identification. Undress all dressings. Assess each wound using all elements in Section 4.3. | At the SOC visit. |
| 6.1.2 | Assigned RN | Classify and stage each wound. For pressure injuries, use the NPIAP staging system exclusively. Do not reverse-stage healing pressure injuries. For non-pressure wounds, classify by etiology (surgical, diabetic, venous, arterial, traumatic). | At the SOC visit. |
| 6.1.3 | Assigned RN | Measure each wound (L x W x D) using a disposable wound measurement tool (ruler). Note any undermining or tunneling using clock-face notation (e.g., "tunneling at 3 o'clock, 2 cm"). | At the SOC visit. |
| 6.1.4 | Assigned RN | Photograph each wound with patient consent per Section 4.4. | At the SOC visit. |
| 6.1.5 | Assigned RN | Document the wound assessment using the Wound Assessment Documentation Template (Appendix A). Ensure that the documentation supports accurate completion of OASIS items M1311 through M1350. | Within 24 hours of the SOC visit. |
| 6.1.6 | Assigned RN | Develop a wound-specific care plan including: treatment goals (e.g., wound closure, infection prevention, reduction in wound size by a defined percentage within a defined timeframe); treatment interventions; dressing change frequency; and patient/caregiver wound care education. | Within 24 hours of the SOC visit. |

### 6.2 Ongoing Wound Assessment and Treatment

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.2.1 | Assigned RN / LVN | At each wound care visit, assess the wound using all elements in Section 4.3. Compare findings to the previous visit assessment. Document all findings. | At each wound care visit. |
| 6.2.2 | Assigned RN / LVN | Perform wound care treatment per the physician order. Document the treatment performed including: wound cleansing method, debridement (if any), dressing applied, and the patient's tolerance. | At each wound care visit. |
| 6.2.3 | Assigned RN | Perform formal wound measurements (L x W x D) at minimum every 2 weeks and at each OASIS assessment time point. Document the measurements and compare to baseline. | Every 2 weeks and at OASIS time points. |
| 6.2.4 | Assigned RN | If the wound is not progressing as expected within 2–4 weeks, reassess the treatment approach per Section 4.7. | Within 2–4 weeks of treatment initiation. |
| 6.2.5 | Assigned RN | Photograph the wound at recertification, at significant change, and at discharge per Section 4.4. | At each indicated time point. |

### 6.3 OASIS Wound Item Coding Integration

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.3.1 | Assigned RN | When completing OASIS wound items (M1311–M1350), ensure that every response is supported by the narrative wound assessment documentation in the clinical record per CL-OA-007. | At each OASIS time point. |
| 6.3.2 | Assigned RN | Follow the CMS OASIS Guidance Manual for all wound item coding, including the specific look-back periods and response definitions per CL-OA-010. | At each OASIS time point. |
| 6.3.3 | Director of Nursing | Include wound documentation accuracy as a component of the monthly documentation audit. Cross-reference OASIS wound item responses against wound assessment narratives for a random sample of patients with active wounds. | Monthly. |

### 6.4 Patient and Caregiver Education

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.4.1 | Assigned RN | Provide wound care education to the patient and caregiver including: signs and symptoms of infection to report; proper dressing change technique (if the caregiver will perform between visits); pressure redistribution techniques for pressure injury patients; nutrition optimization for wound healing; and when to contact the agency or call 911. | Beginning at the SOC visit; reinforced at each wound care visit. |
| 6.4.2 | Assigned RN | Document all wound care education provided, the teaching method, and the patient's/caregiver's understanding per CL-SD-017. | At each visit where education is provided. |

### 6.5 Escalation and Exception Handling

| Condition | Escalation Path | Corrective Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Wound shows signs of clinical infection (spreading erythema, purulent drainage, fever, elevated WBC) | RN notifies physician immediately | Obtain physician orders for wound culture (if not already ordered), systemic antibiotics, and modified wound care. Increase visit frequency if ordered. | Physician notification same day; modified treatment per physician orders. |
| New pressure injury develops during the episode | Assigned RN and Director of Nursing | Conduct a root cause analysis: assess pressure redistribution, turning schedule, nutrition, and caregiver compliance. Report as an adverse event per QA-AE-001. Update the plan of care. | Root cause analysis within 48 hours; adverse event report per QA-AE-001 timeline. |
| OASIS wound coding inconsistent with wound assessment narrative | Director of Nursing identifies during audit | Correct the OASIS assessment per CL-OA-002. Provide documentation coaching to the assessing clinician. | Correction within 5 business days; coaching within 7 calendar days. |
| Wound requires advanced treatment beyond the agency's scope (e.g., surgical debridement, negative pressure wound therapy initiation) | RN recommends specialist referral to physician | Coordinate referral to wound care specialist. Continue agency wound care per physician orders pending specialist evaluation. | Referral within 48 hours. |

## 7. Documentation Requirements

| Requirement | Document / Record | Responsible Party | Location | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Initial wound assessment | Wound Assessment Documentation Template (Appendix A) for each wound | Assigned RN | EHR — visit note and wound assessment module | At SOC; within 24 hours |
| Ongoing wound assessment and treatment | Visit note documenting assessment findings, treatment, and patient response | Assigned RN / LVN | EHR — visit note | At each wound care visit; within 24 hours |
| Wound measurements | L x W x D documented in centimeters with comparison to baseline | Assigned RN | EHR — wound assessment module | Every 2 weeks and at OASIS time points |
| Wound photographs | Digital photographs with ruler for scale | Assigned RN | EHR — wound photograph module | SOC, recertification, significant change, discharge |
| OASIS wound items (M1311–M1350) | OASIS assessment consistent with wound assessment narrative | Assigned RN | EHR — OASIS module | At each OASIS time point |
| Patient/caregiver wound care education | Education documentation per CL-SD-017 | Assigned RN | EHR — visit note | At each wound care visit |
| Policy acknowledgment | Signed acknowledgment (Appendix B) | Each individual | Policy acknowledgment file | Within 14 calendar days |

## 8. Compliance & Audit Considerations
### 8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

| Compliance Indicator | Measurement Method | Acceptable Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| All wounds assessed with complete documentation at SOC | Chart audit using Wound Assessment Template | ≥95% of audited records with complete wound assessments at SOC |
| Wound measurements documented every 2 weeks | Chart audit | ≥95% |
| OASIS wound items consistent with wound assessment narrative | OASIS-to-narrative cross-reference audit | ≥95% — zero material inconsistencies |
| Wounds not progressing result in documented reassessment within 2–4 weeks | Chart review of non-healing wounds | 100% of non-progressing wounds with documented reassessment |
| Wound photographs obtained at required time points | Chart audit | ≥90% |

### 8.2 What Surveyors and Auditors Will Look For
CMS surveyors will select patients with active wounds and compare: (a) the wound assessment documentation with the OASIS wound item coding — inconsistencies are cited; (b) wound care orders with treatment provided — any deviation from the ordered treatment is a deficiency; (c) wound measurement trends to evaluate whether the wound is progressing and whether the treatment plan is responsive; (d) wound staging accuracy — reverse-staging is always cited. OASIS validation auditors will specifically target wound items because wound status directly impacts PDGM payment classification.
### 8.3 Common Failure Points

| Failure Point | Risk | Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Reverse-staging pressure injuries | OASIS accuracy deficiency; survey citation; payment error | Train all clinicians that pressure injuries never reverse-stage; include in annual wound care competency |
| Wound measurements inconsistent across visits (different clinicians measuring differently) | Quality data unreliable; OASIS accuracy issues | Standardize measurement technique (head-to-toe for length, side-to-side for width, perpendicular to surface for depth); train all clinicians |
| OASIS wound items coded without supporting narrative documentation | OASIS validation deficiency; documentation integrity failure | Monthly audit cross-referencing OASIS wound items with narrative assessments |
| Wound not progressing but treatment plan unchanged | Patient harm; survey citation for inadequate care management | 2–4 week reassessment trigger; Director of Nursing supervisory review |
| Wound photographs not obtained or not standardized | Loss of objective evidence; inconsistent trending | Standardize photography protocol; include in wound care competency evaluation |

## 10. Training & Acknowledgment Requirements
10.1 All RNs and LVNs providing wound care shall receive wound care competency training at hire and annually thereafter, including: NPIAP staging; wound measurement technique; wound photography standards; OASIS wound item coding; and evidence-based treatment protocols.
10.2 Wound care competency shall be validated through: (a) written knowledge assessment (≥80% passing score); (b) wound assessment skills demonstration (using wound models or clinical observation).
10.3 All personnel within scope shall acknowledge this policy within 14 calendar days.
## 11. Version Control
Maintained per EN-LC-001.

# CL-SD-012 — Medication Management & Administration
## 1. Policy Header

| Domain | CL — Clinical Operations |

| Classification Tier | REQUIRED |
| Status | ACTIVE |
| Review Cycle | Annual |

| Policy Owner / Steward | Director of Nursing |
| Effective Date | 2025-07-10 |

## 2. Purpose
This policy establishes the standards for medication administration, medication management, medication storage assessment, medication reconciliation, adverse drug reaction identification and reporting, and patient/caregiver medication education at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. Medication management is a core component of skilled nursing in the home health setting and is integral to virtually every patient encounter. Medication errors — including wrong dose, wrong medication, wrong route, omitted doses, drug-drug interactions, and failure to identify adverse reactions — are among the leading causes of preventable patient harm in home health. This policy ensures that all medication-related activities performed by agency staff comply with 42 CFR § 484.60 (plan of care conformance), 42 CFR § 484.75 (skilled professional services), the California Nursing Practice Act, and CMS Home Health Benefit Manual coverage requirements for skilled nursing related to medication management.
## 3. Scope
This policy applies to:
All registered nurses (RNs) providing medication administration and management services
All licensed vocational nurses (LVNs) administering medications within their California BPC § 2859 scope
Home health aides — to the extent of their observation and reporting obligations regarding medication compliance (HHAs do not administer medications)
The Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager
Physicians and allowed practitioners ordering medications
Revenue Cycle staff verifying medication-related documentation supports billed services
This policy does not govern IV medication administration (CL-SD-010), high-risk medication safety protocols (RM-PS-005), or medication reconciliation at transitions of care (CL-SD-013), though it cross-references each.
## 4. Policy Statement
4.1 All medication administration by agency staff shall be authorized by a current, valid physician order specifying: drug name, dose, route, frequency, and indication. No medication shall be administered without a physician order per CL-CP-003.
4.2 All medication administration shall follow the "Five Rights" verification protocol: right patient, right medication, right dose, right route, and right time. Additionally, the clinician shall verify the right documentation and right reason (the "Seven Rights" standard adopted by the agency).
4.3 At each skilled nursing visit, the assigned RN or LVN shall perform a comprehensive medication review including: (a) verification of the patient's actual medication-taking behavior against the prescribed regimen; (b) assessment of medication storage conditions; (c) identification of new, changed, or discontinued medications since the last visit; (d) assessment for adverse drug reactions, side effects, and drug-drug interactions; (e) assessment of the patient's and caregiver's understanding of the medication regimen; (f) documentation of all findings per Section 6.
4.4 When medication discrepancies are identified — including discrepancies between the prescribed regimen and actual patient behavior, between the agency's medication list and the pharmacy profile, or between the plan of care medication list and the current physician orders — the RN shall initiate reconciliation per CL-SD-013, notify the physician within 24 hours, and document all findings and actions.
4.5 All suspected adverse drug reactions (ADRs) shall be immediately reported to the physician, documented in the clinical record, and reported through the agency's incident reporting system per RM-ER-002. Serious ADRs that meet FDA MedWatch criteria shall be reported to the FDA.
4.6 Medication education shall be provided to the patient and caregiver at SOC and reinforced at each visit, covering: the purpose of each medication, dose and frequency, route of administration, common side effects, signs of adverse reactions to report, storage requirements, and the importance of adherence.
4.7 The agency shall not store, dispense, or pre-pour medications for patients. The agency's role is to administer medications as ordered during visits, assess the patient's medication management capability, provide education, and coordinate with the physician and pharmacy to resolve medication issues.
4.8 For patients identified as at risk for medication non-adherence (polypharmacy, cognitive impairment, complex regimens, history of non-compliance), the RN shall develop and implement a medication management plan as part of the plan of care, including interventions such as: medication organizer setup assistance, simplified regimen coordination with the physician, caregiver training, and pharmacy coordination.
## 5. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Medication Administration | The act of giving a medication to a patient by a licensed clinician — including oral, topical, injectable, inhalation, rectal, ophthalmic, otic, and transdermal routes. |
| Medication Management | The comprehensive clinical process of assessing, monitoring, educating, and coordinating the patient's medication regimen to ensure safety, efficacy, and adherence. |
| Medication Reconciliation | The process of comparing the patient's medication orders against all medications the patient is actually taking to identify and resolve discrepancies. Detailed in CL-SD-013. |
| Adverse Drug Reaction (ADR) | An undesirable response to a medication that occurs at normal doses used for prophylaxis, diagnosis, or treatment. |
| Polypharmacy | The concurrent use of five or more medications, which increases the risk of drug-drug interactions, adverse effects, and medication errors. |
| Medication Review | A systematic assessment of the patient's entire medication regimen including prescription medications, over-the-counter medications, vitamins, supplements, and herbal products. |
| Five Rights | The medication safety verification protocol: right patient, right medication, right dose, right route, right time. |
| High-Alert Medications | Medications that bear a heightened risk of causing significant patient harm when used in error, including anticoagulants, opioids, insulin, and chemotherapy agents. Governed by RM-PS-005. |
| PRN Medication | A medication ordered to be administered "as needed" based on the patient's symptoms and the clinician's clinical judgment within the parameters of the physician order. |

## 6. Procedures
### 6.1 Medication Review at Each Skilled Nursing Visit

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.1.1 | Assigned RN / LVN | At each skilled nursing visit, conduct a medication review by requesting the patient or caregiver present all medications — including prescription bottles, over-the-counter products, vitamins, supplements, and herbal products. Compare the medications on hand against the agency's current medication list and the physician-ordered medication regimen. | At each skilled nursing visit. |
| 6.1.2 | Assigned RN / LVN | Assess the patient's actual medication-taking behavior: (a) ask the patient/caregiver which medications they are taking and how they are taking them (dose, frequency, timing); (b) count pill quantities or check fill dates if non-adherence is suspected; (c) assess use of medication organizers or pill boxes; (d) observe the patient self-administering medications if indicated. Document findings per CL-OA-014. | At each visit. |
| 6.1.3 | Assigned RN / LVN | Assess medication storage: (a) verify refrigerated medications are stored at appropriate temperature; (b) verify medications are stored safely away from children; (c) verify expired medications are identified for disposal; (d) verify controlled substances are stored securely. | At each visit. |
| 6.1.4 | Assigned RN / LVN | Assess for adverse drug reactions and side effects: (a) ask the patient about new symptoms since the last visit; (b) assess vital signs for medication-related changes (orthostatic hypotension from antihypertensives, bradycardia from beta-blockers, hypoglycemia signs from insulin or oral hypoglycemics); (c) assess for signs of anticoagulant excess (bruising, bleeding); (d) assess for CNS effects (sedation, confusion, dizziness) from opioids, benzodiazepines, or anticonvulsants. | At each visit. |
| 6.1.5 | Assigned RN / LVN | If any medication discrepancy, ADR, or safety concern is identified, immediately contact the physician to report the finding and obtain guidance. Document the contact and physician response per CL-CP-003. | Within 24 hours of identification; immediately for urgent concerns. |
| 6.1.6 | Assigned RN / LVN | Document the medication review in the visit note including: (a) medications verified; (b) patient's reported adherence; (c) any discrepancies identified and actions taken; (d) any ADRs or side effects observed and actions taken; (e) medication education provided. | Within 24 hours of the visit. |

### 6.2 Medication Administration During Visits

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.2.1 | Assigned RN / LVN | Before administering any medication, perform the Seven Rights verification: (a) right patient — verify identity using two identifiers per OP-PA-002; (b) right medication — compare the medication label to the physician order; (c) right dose — verify the dose matches the order; (d) right route — verify the ordered route; (e) right time — verify the administration time is consistent with the order; (f) right documentation — ensure the order is current and documented; (g) right reason — verify the indication is consistent with the patient's diagnosis. | Before each medication administration. |
| 6.2.2 | Assigned RN / LVN | For injectable medications (subcutaneous, intramuscular): verify the injection site is appropriate; perform aseptic technique; administer the injection; observe the patient for at least 5 minutes for immediate adverse reactions; document the administration including site, medication, dose, route, time, and patient tolerance. | During the visit. |
| 6.2.3 | Assigned RN / LVN | For PRN medications: verify that the patient's current symptoms meet the criteria defined in the physician order; administer the medication; reassess the patient's response within the timeframe appropriate to the medication's expected onset of action; document the indication, administration, and patient response. | During the visit. |
| 6.2.4 | Assigned RN / LVN | For high-alert medications (anticoagulants, insulin, opioids): follow the enhanced safety protocols defined in RM-PS-005, including independent double-check verification, dose calculation verification, and specific monitoring parameters. | During the visit. |
| 6.2.5 | Assigned RN | If a medication error occurs (wrong dose, wrong medication, wrong route, wrong patient, omission): (a) assess the patient immediately for adverse effects; (b) notify the physician immediately; (c) provide any necessary clinical intervention; (d) document the error, the patient assessment, the physician notification, and all actions taken; (e) report through the incident reporting system per RM-ER-002; (f) notify the Director of Nursing within 4 hours. | Immediately upon discovery; Director of Nursing notification within 4 hours. |

### 6.3 Medication Education

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.3.1 | Assigned RN | At SOC, provide comprehensive medication education to the patient and caregiver covering: the purpose of each medication; the correct dose, frequency, and timing; the correct route and technique (especially for inhalers, injectable medications, eye drops, and topical medications); common side effects and how to manage them; signs of adverse reactions that require physician contact or emergency services; medication interactions to avoid (including food interactions); proper storage; the importance of adherence and the risks of non-adherence; the importance of not sharing medications; and how to dispose of expired or discontinued medications safely. | At the SOC visit. |
| 6.3.2 | Assigned RN / LVN | Reinforce medication education at each subsequent visit, focusing on areas where the patient has demonstrated knowledge gaps, non-adherence, or new medications have been added. | At each visit. |
| 6.3.3 | Assigned RN | Provide written medication education materials in the patient's primary language per OP-PA-003. Provide a current, written medication list to the patient and caregiver and update it at each visit when changes occur. | At SOC; updated at each medication change. |
| 6.3.4 | Assigned RN | Document all medication education provided, the teaching method used (verbal, written materials, demonstration, teach-back), and the patient's/caregiver's level of understanding per CL-SD-017. | Within 24 hours of each visit. |

### 6.4 Medication Non-Adherence Management

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.4.1 | Assigned RN | When medication non-adherence is identified, assess the root cause: (a) knowledge deficit (patient does not understand the regimen); (b) physical barrier (patient cannot open bottles, read labels, or self-administer); (c) financial barrier (patient cannot afford medications); (d) intentional non-adherence (patient chooses not to take medications); (e) cognitive impairment affecting medication management capability; (f) complex regimen (polypharmacy, multiple daily doses). | At the visit where non-adherence is identified. |
| 6.4.2 | Assigned RN | Based on the root cause assessment, implement targeted interventions: education for knowledge deficits; adaptive equipment or caregiver training for physical barriers; pharmacy assistance program referral or MSW involvement for financial barriers; motivational interviewing and physician counseling for intentional non-adherence; medication organizer setup and caregiver training for cognitive impairment; physician consultation for regimen simplification for polypharmacy. | Within 48 hours of root cause assessment. |
| 6.4.3 | Assigned RN | Document the non-adherence, root cause assessment, interventions implemented, and the patient's response. If non-adherence is persistent and poses a clinical risk, notify the physician and Director of Nursing. | Within 24 hours. |

### 6.5 Controlled Substance Documentation

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.5.1 | Assigned RN / LVN | When administering a controlled substance to a patient during a visit, document: the medication name, dose, route, time administered, the patient's pain score (or other relevant assessment) before and after administration, and the patient's response. | At the time of administration. |
| 6.5.2 | Assigned RN | If the patient's controlled substance supply appears inconsistent with expected use (excessive use suggesting diversion or misuse, or underuse suggesting non-adherence), document the finding, assess the patient, and notify the physician within 24 hours. If diversion is suspected, also notify the Director of Nursing and Compliance Officer per CO-FA-003. | Within 24 hours of identification. |

### 6.6 Escalation and Exception Handling

| Condition | Escalation Path | Corrective Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Suspected adverse drug reaction — non-emergent | RN notifies physician | Physician provides guidance; RN implements orders; documents in clinical record and incident report per RM-ER-002. | Physician notification within 24 hours; incident report within 24 hours. |
| Suspected adverse drug reaction — emergent (anaphylaxis, severe hypotension, respiratory distress) | RN calls 911; notifies physician and Director of Nursing | RN provides emergency care within scope; remains with patient until EMS arrival; documents all actions. | Immediately. |
| Medication error discovered | RN assesses patient; notifies physician immediately; notifies Director of Nursing within 4 hours | Patient assessment and intervention as needed; incident report per RM-ER-002; root cause analysis for significant errors per QA-AE-002. | Immediate assessment; incident report within 24 hours. |
| Patient refuses prescribed medication | RN documents refusal; assesses capacity; educates on risks | Notify physician within 24 hours; document refusal, education, and physician notification in visit note. | Within 24 hours. |
| Suspected controlled substance diversion | RN notifies Director of Nursing and Compliance Officer | Compliance investigation per CO-CP-007; physician notification; documentation of all findings. | Director of Nursing notification within 24 hours; Compliance Officer within 48 hours. |

| Requirement | Document / Record | Responsible Party | Location | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Medication review at each visit | Visit note documenting medication review findings per Section 6.1.6 | Assigned RN / LVN | EHR — visit note | Within 24 hours of each visit; retained minimum 7 years |
| Medication administration record | Documentation of each medication administered per Section 6.2 | Assigned RN / LVN | EHR — visit note | At each administration; within 24 hours |
| Medication education documentation | Education content, method, and patient understanding | Assigned RN / LVN | EHR — visit note | Within 24 hours per CL-SD-017 |
| Medication discrepancy documentation | Discrepancy identified, physician notification, resolution | Assigned RN | EHR — visit note and communication notes | Within 24 hours of identification |
| Adverse drug reaction documentation | ADR details, patient assessment, physician notification, interventions | Assigned RN | EHR — visit note and incident report | Within 24 hours; incident report per RM-ER-002 |
| Medication error report | Error details, patient assessment, corrective actions | Assigned RN | Incident reporting system and EHR | Within 24 hours of discovery |
| Non-adherence assessment and interventions | Root cause, interventions, patient response | Assigned RN | EHR — visit note | Within 24 hours |
| Updated medication list to patient | Written medication list | Assigned RN | Patient copy and EHR | At SOC; at each medication change |

## 8. Compliance & Audit Considerations
### 8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

| Compliance Indicator | Measurement Method | Acceptable Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Medication review documented at every skilled nursing visit | Monthly chart audit of random sample | ≥95% of audited visit notes contain medication review documentation |
| Seven Rights verification documented for all medications administered | Chart audit | ≥98% |
| Medication discrepancies result in physician notification within 24 hours | Audit of physician communication notes | ≥95% |
| All adverse drug reactions reported through incident reporting system | Cross-reference visit notes documenting ADRs with incident reports | 100% — zero unreported ADRs |
| Patient/caregiver medication education documented at SOC | SOC visit note audit | ≥95% |

### 8.2 What Surveyors and Auditors Will Look For
CMS surveyors conducting a standard survey under SOM Appendix B will specifically verify under Tag G160 and G184:
Evidence that medication management is a component of the skilled nursing visit. Surveyors will select patient records and verify that the visit note documents a medication review — not merely a notation that "meds reviewed" but a substantive assessment of the patient's medication regimen, adherence, and any identified concerns. Superficial medication documentation is a common deficiency.
Evidence that medication lists are current and consistent. Surveyors will compare the plan of care medication list, the visit note medication documentation, and the OASIS medication items. Inconsistencies across these documents are cited as documentation integrity failures.
Evidence that medication education is individualized and documented. Surveyors may interview patients about their understanding of their medications. If the patient cannot describe the purpose of their medications and the clinical record does not document education, a deficiency will be cited.
Evidence that adverse drug reactions are identified and managed. Surveyors will look for clinical records where ADR symptoms are documented in visit notes but there is no corresponding physician notification or follow-up action.
Evidence that medication errors are reported and investigated. Surveyors will review the agency's incident reporting system for medication error trends and verify that root cause analysis is conducted for significant errors.
### 8.3 Common Failure Points

| Failure Point | Risk | Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Medication review documented as "meds reviewed, no changes" without detail | Survey deficiency; inability to demonstrate skilled service | Require structured medication review section in visit note template; Director of Nursing audits monthly |
| Medication list not updated when changes occur | Documentation integrity failure; patient safety risk | EHR medication list update required before visit note can be locked |
| Medication education documented as "pt educated on meds" without specifics | Survey deficiency; unable to demonstrate individualized education | Require documentation of specific topics, teaching method, and teach-back response |
| ADRs identified in visit notes but no physician notification documented | Patient safety failure; survey citation | Train all clinicians: every ADR requires physician notification and documentation of the notification |
| Controlled substance concerns not escalated | Compliance and legal risk | Annual controlled substance awareness training; Director of Nursing reviews controlled substance documentation quarterly |

## 10. Training & Acknowledgment Requirements
10.1 All RNs and LVNs shall receive competency-validated training on medication management and administration requirements within 14 calendar days of hire and annually thereafter, including: (a) the Seven Rights protocol; (b) medication review documentation standards; (c) ADR identification and reporting; (d) high-alert medication protocols per RM-PS-005; (e) medication non-adherence assessment and intervention; (f) controlled substance documentation requirements; (g) medication education documentation standards.
10.2 All RNs and LVNs shall demonstrate competency in medication administration — including injection technique, medication verification, and ADR recognition — through skills evaluation at hire and annually.
10.3 All personnel within scope of this policy shall sign the Policy Acknowledgment Form (Appendix A) within 14 calendar days of the policy effective date, any revision, or new hire/appointment.
10.4 The Director of Nursing shall maintain training completion and competency records for all clinicians and shall report non-compliance to the Administrator within 7 calendar days of any training deadline.
## 11. Version Control
11.1 This policy is maintained under the agency's enterprise policy lifecycle management system per policy EN-LC-001.
11.2 Only the most current approved version of this policy, as reflected in the policy header, is valid for any operational, compliance, or regulatory purpose. All superseded versions must be archived and clearly marked as "SUPERSEDED — NOT FOR USE."
11.3 Any substantive revision to this policy requires: (a) review and approval by the Governing Body, documented in meeting minutes; (b) re-acknowledgment by all personnel within scope within 14 calendar days of the revised effective date; (c) update to the enterprise policy index per EN-TG-001.
11.4 Non-substantive revisions (formatting, typographical corrections, updated cross-references) may be approved by the Administrator with notification to the Governing Body at the next regular meeting.

# CL-SD-013 — Medication Reconciliation at Transitions
## 1. Policy Header

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Policy ID | CL-SD-013 |
| Policy Title | Medication Reconciliation at Transitions |
| Domain | CL — Clinical Operations |
| Subdomain | SD — Service Delivery |
| Classification Tier | REQUIRED |
| Status | ACTIVE |
| Review Cycle | Annual |
| Access Tier | Tier 2 — Restricted |
| Policy Owner / Steward | Director of Nursing |
| Effective Date | 2025-07-10 |

| Last Reviewed | 2025-07-10 |
