## 2. Purpose
This policy establishes the standards for accurate, timely, and complete OASIS data collection in compliance with CMS requirements at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. The Outcome and Assessment Information Set (OASIS) is not merely a documentation instrument — it is the financial, clinical, and regulatory backbone of the Medicare home health benefit. Every OASIS data element directly affects one or more of the following: the patient's PDGM payment group assignment (which determines how much Medicare pays the agency for the episode); the agency's publicly reported quality measures on Home Health Compare (which affect the agency's star ratings, referral relationships, and competitive standing); CMS survey compliance (inaccurate OASIS data is a direct deficiency under 42 CFR § 484.55); and the clinical validity of the agency's patient population data (which underpins every quality improvement decision the QAPI program makes).
OASIS accuracy failures are among the most consequential and most commonly cited deficiencies in home health. They occur along a spectrum: individual item errors driven by misunderstanding of CMS guidance; systematic coding patterns driven by financial pressure (upcoding to maximize payment); systematic undercoding driven by unfamiliarity with the instrument; and documentation inconsistencies where OASIS responses are not supported by the clinical narrative. All of these failure modes have regulatory, financial, and legal consequences. The False Claims Act imposes liability not only for fraudulent claims but for claims submitted with reckless disregard for their accuracy — a pattern of OASIS inaccuracy without a robust accuracy program may meet that standard.
This policy establishes the complete framework for OASIS data collection accuracy at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc., incorporating: the clinical decision rules that govern response selection; the documentation standards that must support every response; the quality review process that validates accuracy before submission; the training and authorization program that ensures only competent assessors collect OASIS data; and the audit and correction process that identifies and resolves errors after submission. This policy implements 42 CFR § 484.55(b) — which requires that the comprehensive assessment accurately reflect the patient's current health status — and CMS Conditions of Participation requirements for OASIS data integrity under 42 CFR § 484.20.
## 3. Scope
This policy applies to:
All registered nurses (RNs) authorized to conduct comprehensive assessments and collect OASIS data
The Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager responsible for OASIS quality oversight
The OASIS Quality Reviewer (a designated RN with advanced OASIS training who conducts pre-submission and post-submission OASIS audits)
OASIS submission staff responsible for transmitting data to the CMS OASIS repository
The QAPI Coordinator who uses OASIS-derived quality measures for performance improvement
Revenue Cycle staff whose payment calculations depend on accurate OASIS data
This policy does not apply to non-RN clinical staff (LVNs, therapists, HHAs), who do not collect OASIS data. It governs all OASIS time points: SOC, ROC, RECERT, FU (SCIC), TRN, and DC.
## 4. Policy Statement
4.1 All OASIS data elements shall be collected by a registered nurse who has completed the agency's OASIS Competency Program per CL-CA-001 and is listed on the current OASIS Authorized Assessor Roster. No OASIS data element shall be collected, modified, or finalized by any non-RN clinical staff member, administrative staff, revenue cycle personnel, or billing coder, regardless of the purpose of the modification.
4.2 Every OASIS response shall be selected using the current CMS OASIS-E2 Guidance Manual as the definitive authority for all coding decisions. When agency-developed coding guidance conflicts with CMS guidance, CMS guidance governs. Agency-created coding rules, internal coding conventions, or OASIS "cheat sheets" that deviate from or contradict CMS guidance are prohibited.
4.3 Every OASIS response shall be supported by documented clinical evidence in the patient's clinical record. The evidentiary hierarchy for OASIS coding shall follow CL-OA-006 (Documentation Hierarchy and Evidence Source Prioritization). An OASIS response that is not supported by documented clinical evidence is an unsupported response and constitutes a data integrity failure, regardless of whether the response happens to be clinically plausible.
4.4 OASIS data shall reflect the patient's actual clinical status at the time of the specific assessment encounter — not the patient's best possible performance, not the patient's worst-case scenario, not an average of performances across recent visits, and not an extrapolation from prior assessments. Every OASIS assessment is a contemporaneous point-in-time assessment per CL-OA-009.
4.5 The agency shall implement a multi-level OASIS quality review process: (a) a self-review by the assessing RN using the Pre-Submission Quality Review Checklist per CL-OA-019 before locking the assessment; (b) a designated OASIS Quality Reviewer review of all SOC assessments within 5 business days of locking; (c) a monthly random sample OASIS audit by the Director of Nursing covering ≥5% of all submitted assessments per CL-OA-002; (d) quarterly OASIS accuracy trending analysis presented to the QAPI Committee.
4.6 The agency shall maintain an OASIS data accuracy rate — defined as the percentage of audited OASIS items where the agency's response matches the correct response as determined by the OASIS Quality Reviewer — of ≥95% as the minimum acceptable standard. An accuracy rate below 95% on any audited item category shall trigger a Performance Improvement Project per QA-PI-001.
4.7 Any OASIS response that is identified as inaccurate, whether before or after submission, shall be corrected per the procedures established in CL-CA-003 (OASIS Transmission & Correction). All corrections shall be documented with the reason for the change and the clinical evidence supporting the corrected response.
4.8 Financial pressure, revenue targets, payment optimization goals, or any external influence on OASIS response selection are explicitly prohibited. OASIS responses shall reflect the patient's actual clinical status — the payment consequence of an accurate response is never a justification for an inaccurate one.
## 5. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| OASIS | Outcome and Assessment Information Set — the standardized data set mandated by CMS for all Medicare-certified home health agencies, currently in version OASIS-E2. |
| OASIS Item | A single data element within the OASIS data set, identified by an alphanumeric code (e.g., M1800, GG0130A). Each item has a specific definition, data collection instructions, and response options defined in the CMS OASIS-E2 Guidance Manual. |
| OASIS-E2 Guidance Manual | The CMS-published document that provides item-specific guidance for every OASIS data element, including definitions of response options, look-back periods, time points at which items are collected, and special circumstances. This is the definitive authority for all OASIS coding decisions. |
| Assessment Time Point | A specific clinical event that triggers an OASIS assessment requirement. The six time points are: SOC, ROC, RECERT, FU (Follow-Up/SCIC), TRN (Transfer), and DC (Discharge). |
| Look-Back Period | The CMS-defined timeframe prior to the assessment date during which clinical information is considered for coding a specific OASIS item. Look-back periods vary by item — some items require assessment of the past 24 hours, others 7 days, others 14 days, and some items are assessed at the moment of the visit (point-in-time). |
| OASIS Authorized Assessor | A registered nurse who has completed the agency's OASIS Competency Program and is authorized by the Director of Nursing to independently conduct comprehensive assessments and collect OASIS data. |
| OASIS Quality Reviewer | A designated RN with advanced OASIS expertise who conducts pre- and post-submission accuracy reviews of OASIS assessments. The Quality Reviewer is typically the Director of Nursing or a designee with OASIS specialist training. |
| Data Accuracy Rate | The percentage of audited OASIS item responses that match the correct response as determined by independent expert review, calculated per item category and overall. |
| Upcoding | The practice of selecting OASIS responses that reflect a higher level of functional impairment, disease severity, or resource need than the patient's actual clinical status in order to maximize payment — a False Claims Act violation. |
| Undercoding | The practice of selecting OASIS responses that reflect a lower level of functional impairment, disease severity, or clinical need than the patient's actual clinical status — a quality measure accuracy failure and a documentation integrity failure. |
| SCIC Assessment | Significant Change in Condition assessment — a Follow-Up (FU) OASIS assessment triggered when a patient experiences a major decline or improvement in health status that meets the CMS criteria for a significant change, requiring reassessment of applicable OASIS items. |

## 6. Procedures
### 6.1 OASIS Data Collection — General Requirements

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.1.1 | Assigned RN | Before conducting any OASIS assessment, verify that the current CMS OASIS-E2 Guidance Manual is available (electronic access or printed current edition). Never rely on memory, informal summaries, or prior-version guidance for item-specific coding decisions. | Before each assessment. |
| 6.1.2 | Assigned RN | Identify all OASIS items applicable to the specific assessment time point being conducted. The items collected vary by time point — not all items are collected at all time points. Use the time-point applicability table in the CMS OASIS-E2 Guidance Manual to confirm item applicability. | Before each assessment. |
| 6.1.3 | Assigned RN | For each applicable OASIS item, identify the look-back period specified in the CMS guidance. Information collected outside the look-back period shall not be used to code the item, regardless of its clinical relevance. | During data collection. |
| 6.1.4 | Assigned RN | Collect OASIS data through a combination of: (a) direct observation and physical examination of the patient during the visit; (b) structured clinical interview of the patient using validated tools where required (PHQ-2/PHQ-9, BIMS, MAHC-10); (c) structured interview of the caregiver regarding the patient's typical performance; (d) review of all available clinical documentation within the applicable look-back period. Do not select a response based on any single source alone when multiple sources are available and relevant. | During the assessment visit. |
| 6.1.5 | Assigned RN | When the patient's performance or status varies across the look-back period (some days better, some days worse), select the OASIS response that reflects the patient's usual status — the level of performance or impairment that most consistently describes the patient across the look-back period. When CMS guidance specifies a different selection rule for a specific item (e.g., worst-case selection for certain safety items), follow that item-specific rule. | During data collection. |
| 6.1.6 | Assigned RN | Document the clinical basis for every OASIS response in the assessment narrative at the time of the assessment — not after the fact. The narrative shall describe the specific observation, test result, or patient report that led to the selected response. The linkage between the narrative and the OASIS response must be traceable and unambiguous per CL-OA-007. | During and immediately after the assessment. |

### 6.2 Domain-Specific OASIS Accuracy Standards
The following domain-specific accuracy standards shall govern response selection for the highest-risk OASIS item categories. These standards supplement the CMS OASIS-E2 Guidance Manual and do not supersede it.
#### 6.2.1 Functional Status — GG Items (GG0130, GG0170)

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.2.1.1 | Assigned RN | The GG functional items assess the patient's performance of specific activities — not their capacity. Observe the patient perform each activity during the visit whenever possible. Do not select a response based solely on the patient's or caregiver's report of what the patient can or cannot do. | During the assessment visit. |
| 6.2.1.2 | Assigned RN | Use the activity-specific scoring guidance in the CMS OASIS-E2 Guidance Manual for each GG item. The response options follow a standardized functional independence scale — select the response that accurately reflects the level of assistance the patient requires, not the level the clinician believes the patient should require. | During data collection. |
| 6.2.1.3 | Assigned RN | Document the specific activity performed and observed, the level of assistance provided by the clinician or caregiver, the patient's performance quality, and any safety concerns identified. This documentation shall be specific enough that a second RN reviewing the record could independently arrive at the same GG response. | Within 24 hours of the assessment. |
| 6.2.1.4 | OASIS Quality Reviewer | Review all GG functional item responses at the SOC assessment against the narrative documentation. Flag any GG response that is not supported by a documented observation of the patient performing (or attempting to perform) the specific activity. | Within 5 business days of assessment lock. |

#### 6.2.2 Wound Assessment — M1311–M1350

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.2.2.1 | Assigned RN | At every applicable OASIS time point, undress all wound dressings and directly observe all wounds before coding any wound items. Do not code wound items based on prior documentation without direct observation. | During the assessment visit. |
| 6.2.2.2 | Assigned RN | Apply the NPIAP staging system exclusively for pressure injuries. Do not use any other staging system. Do not reverse-stage a healing pressure injury — once staged at Stage 3 or Stage 4, the wound retains that stage designation for the life of the wound regardless of healing progress. Code the wound as "Stage 3, healing" or "Stage 4, healing" rather than downstaging. | During data collection. |
| 6.2.2.3 | Assigned RN | For M1340 (Does this patient have a Surgical Wound) and M1342 (Status of Most Problematic Surgical Wound), apply the CMS-defined response options precisely per the guidance manual. Do not conflate wound types (e.g., coding a dehisced surgical wound as a pressure injury). | During data collection. |
| 6.2.2.4 | Assigned RN | Document all wound assessment findings using the Wound Assessment Documentation Template per CL-SD-011, ensuring that the documented wound status directly supports the M1311–M1350 OASIS responses. Cross-reference all wound OASIS items with the wound narrative documentation before locking the assessment. | Within 24 hours of assessment. |

#### 6.2.3 Behavioral Health — M1700–M1750

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.2.3.1 | Assigned RN | Administer the BIMS for M1700 (Cognitive Function) using the validated CMS protocol — three-word repetition, temporal orientation, and word recall. Document the item-level scores and the total score. Code M1700 using the BIMS score ranges specified in the OASIS-E2 Guidance Manual. If the patient is unable to complete the BIMS, use the Staff Assessment for Mental Status (SAMS) and code M1700 accordingly. | During the assessment. |
| 6.2.3.2 | Assigned RN | Administer the PHQ-2 (and PHQ-9 if PHQ-2 ≥3) for M1730 (Depressive Feelings) per CL-SD-022. Code M1730 using the PHQ-9 score ranges specified in the guidance. Do not code M1730 based solely on clinical impression — the validated tool administration and score are required. | During the assessment. |
| 6.2.3.3 | Assigned RN | For M1740 (Behaviors Demonstrated at Least Once a Week) and M1745 (Frequency of Disruptive/Problematic Behaviors), apply the 7-day look-back period specified in the guidance. Base coding on caregiver report and clinical observation — not exclusively on what is observed during the visit itself. | During the assessment with caregiver interview. |

#### 6.2.4 Medication Management — M2001, M2003, M2010

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.2.4.1 | Assigned RN | Code M2001 (Drug Regimen Review) based on whether a drug regimen review was completed during the assessment and whether potential clinically significant medication issues were identified. Apply the CMS-defined criteria for "potential clinically significant medication issues" (drug interactions, allergies, duplication, wrong dose, wrong drug). | During data collection. |
| 6.2.4.2 | Assigned RN | Code M2003 (Medication Follow-Up) based on whether a physician was contacted within one calendar day of completing the drug regimen review when a potential clinically significant medication issue was identified. This is a process measure — it requires physician contact, not just documentation of the issue. | Based on actions taken following the review. |
| 6.2.4.3 | Assigned RN | Code M2010 (Patient/Caregiver High-Risk Drug Education) based on whether the patient/caregiver received education specific to high-risk medications per the CMS definition. Apply the OASIS-E2 Guidance Manual's definition of "high-risk medications" — which differs from the agency's clinical high-alert medication list per RM-PS-005. | During data collection. |
| 6.2.4.4 | Assigned RN | Code medication management items per CL-OA-014 (Medication Reconciliation — Prescribed Regimen vs. Actual Patient Behavior) — distinguish between what is prescribed and what the patient is actually taking. Code the items based on the patient's actual medication-taking behavior, not the prescribed regimen alone. | During data collection. |

#### 6.2.5 Homebound Status and Eligibility

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.2.5.1 | Assigned RN | While homebound status is not a single OASIS item, it is assessed and documented as part of the comprehensive assessment and is a prerequisite for billing any Medicare home health visit. At each applicable time point, reassess and re-document homebound status with patient-specific clinical language per CL-CA-005. | At each OASIS time point. |
| 6.2.5.2 | OASIS Quality Reviewer | At each SOC review, verify that the homebound status narrative contains patient-specific functional limitations — not generic language. Flag any homebound documentation that uses template language without individualization. | Within 5 business days of assessment lock. |

### 6.3 Pre-Submission Self-Review

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.3.1 | Assigned RN | Before locking any OASIS assessment, complete the Pre-Submission Quality Review Checklist per CL-OA-019. The checklist shall verify: (a) all applicable items are completed; (b) no items are left at default or blank without clinical justification; (c) functionally related item groups are internally consistent (e.g., ambulation and locomotion items are consistent with each other and with the physical examination narrative); (d) medication items are consistent with the medication list; (e) wound items are consistent with the wound assessment narrative; (f) behavioral health items are consistent with the standardized tool scores; (g) homebound status and skilled need are documented. | Before locking each assessment. |
| 6.3.2 | Assigned RN | If the self-review identifies any inconsistency, omission, or unsupported response, correct the assessment before locking. Document the correction and the basis for the corrected response. | Before locking. |
| 6.3.3 | Assigned RN | Lock the assessment only after the self-review is complete and all identified issues are resolved. A locked assessment may not be modified without following the correction process per CL-CA-003. | After self-review completion. |

### 6.4 OASIS Quality Reviewer Review — Post-Lock, Pre-Submission

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.4.1 | OASIS Quality Reviewer | Review all SOC assessments within 5 business days of locking, using the OASIS Quality Review Tool (Appendix A). The review shall assess: accuracy of GG functional items; accuracy of wound items (M1311–M1350); accuracy of behavioral health items (M1700–M1750); accuracy of medication management items (M2001–M2010); narrative-OASIS consistency for all reviewed items; homebound documentation adequacy; skilled need documentation adequacy. | Within 5 business days of locking. |
| 6.4.2 | OASIS Quality Reviewer | Document the review findings in the OASIS Quality Review Log (Appendix B), including: the assessment date, the assessing RN, each item reviewed, the reviewer's determination (Accurate / Inaccurate — requires correction / Insufficient documentation), and any corrective action recommended. | At the time of the review. |
| 6.4.3 | OASIS Quality Reviewer | If an inaccuracy is identified, communicate the finding to the assessing RN and the Director of Nursing within 24 hours, providing the item number, the assessing RN's response, the reviewer's determination of the correct response, and the clinical evidence supporting the correction. | Within 24 hours of finding. |
| 6.4.4 | Assigned RN / Director of Nursing | If the assessing RN agrees with the reviewer's finding, initiate the OASIS correction process per CL-CA-003. If the assessing RN disagrees with the reviewer's determination, escalate to the Director of Nursing for clinical adjudication within 24 hours of the disagreement. The Director of Nursing's determination is final. | Within 24 hours of disagreement notification. |
| 6.4.5 | OASIS Quality Reviewer | Conduct quarterly ROC, RECERT, and DC assessment reviews at a minimum 10% sample rate, using the same review methodology as SOC reviews. | Quarterly. |

### 6.5 Monthly OASIS Accuracy Audit

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.5.1 | Director of Nursing | Conduct or commission a monthly OASIS accuracy audit covering ≥5% of all submitted assessments from the prior month, using the OASIS Quality Review Tool (Appendix A). The audit shall include all time points in the sample, not only SOC assessments. | Monthly. |
| 6.5.2 | Director of Nursing | Calculate the data accuracy rate for the audited sample by item category: GG functional items, wound items, behavioral health items, medication items, and overall. Document the accuracy rate in the OASIS Accuracy Dashboard (Appendix C). | Within 5 business days of audit completion. |
| 6.5.3 | Director of Nursing | Present OASIS accuracy results to the QAPI Committee quarterly. Identify any item category with an accuracy rate below 95% and initiate a Performance Improvement Project per QA-PI-001. | Quarterly QAPI meeting. |
| 6.5.4 | Director of Nursing | Provide individual clinician-level OASIS accuracy feedback to each RN assessor based on audit findings. For any RN with an accuracy rate below 85% on any item category, provide targeted retraining within 14 calendar days and schedule a follow-up audit within 30 calendar days. | Within 14 calendar days of audit completion. |

### 6.6 Escalation and Exception Handling

| Condition | Escalation Path | Corrective Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| OASIS item completed by a non-RN staff member | Director of Nursing identifies | All OASIS items completed by the non-authorized individual shall be voided and re-completed by a qualified RN. Director of Nursing assesses all visits affected for billing implications. Compliance Officer notified. | Re-assessment within 5 business days; compliance review within 14 calendar days. |
| Systematic OASIS accuracy pattern suggesting upcoding or undercoding across multiple patients | Director of Nursing identifies during audit | Director of Nursing and Compliance Officer conduct a full-scope review of all assessments submitted by the identified assessor(s) within the prior 90 days. Corrective action, retraining, and self-disclosure assessment per CO-CP-007 and FN-BC-004. | Review initiated within 5 business days; corrective action within 30 calendar days. |
| OASIS Quality Reviewer and assessing RN disagree on a response and escalation to Director of Nursing does not resolve the disagreement | Administrator and Compliance Officer | The Compliance Officer reviews the clinical record and CMS guidance independently. The Compliance Officer's determination reflects the agency's official coding position. If the Compliance Officer determines the submitted response is inaccurate and was submitted as a paid claim, initiate correction and overpayment assessment per FN-BC-004. | Resolution within 7 calendar days. |
| OASIS accuracy rate falls below 90% agency-wide in any quarter | Director of Nursing and Administrator | Agency-wide OASIS retraining initiated. External OASIS consultant engaged for review if accuracy rate does not recover above 92% within 60 calendar days. Governing Body notified at next quarterly meeting. | Retraining within 14 calendar days; consultant within 30 calendar days if needed. |

## 7. Documentation Requirements

| Requirement | Document / Record | Responsible Party | Location | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Completed OASIS data set — all applicable items | OASIS-E2 data set per applicable time point | Assigned RN | EHR — OASIS module | Within 5 calendar days of SOC; per CMS timing for other time points; retained minimum 7 years |
| Assessment narrative supporting all OASIS responses | Clinical narrative in the visit note and assessment module | Assigned RN | EHR — assessment module and visit note | Concurrent with OASIS completion |
| Standardized tool results with item-level documentation | PHQ-2/PHQ-9, BIMS, MAHC-10 scores | Assigned RN | EHR — assessment module | At applicable time points |
| Pre-submission self-review checklist | Completed Pre-Submission Quality Review Checklist per CL-OA-019 | Assigned RN | EHR — OASIS quality review module | Before each assessment lock |
| OASIS Quality Reviewer review | Completed OASIS Quality Review Tool (Appendix A) | OASIS Quality Reviewer | OASIS Quality Review Log (Appendix B) | Within 5 business days of SOC lock; quarterly for other time points |
| OASIS Accuracy Dashboard | Monthly accuracy rates by item category and by assessor | Director of Nursing | QAPI records and Director of Nursing supervisory file | Monthly; retained minimum 7 years |
| Individual clinician OASIS feedback | Written accuracy feedback per RN assessor | Director of Nursing | Personnel file and Director of Nursing supervisory file | Monthly; retained minimum 7 years |
| OASIS Authorized Assessor Roster | Current list of all RNs authorized to conduct assessments | Director of Nursing | HR file and Director of Nursing supervisory file | Updated within 5 business days of any change |
| Policy acknowledgment | Signed acknowledgment — Appendix D | Each individual; Administrator (collection) | Policy acknowledgment file | Within 14 calendar days of effective date, revision, or hire |

## 8. Compliance & Audit Considerations
### 8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

| Compliance Indicator | Measurement Method | Acceptable Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| All OASIS assessments conducted by authorized RN assessors | Authorized Assessor Roster cross-reference | 100% |
| OASIS data accuracy rate — GG functional items | Monthly audit | ≥95% |
| OASIS data accuracy rate — wound items | Monthly audit | ≥95% |
| OASIS data accuracy rate — behavioral health items | Monthly audit | ≥95% |
| OASIS data accuracy rate — medication items | Monthly audit | ≥95% |
| OASIS data accuracy rate — overall | Monthly audit | ≥95% |
| Pre-submission self-review completed before every assessment lock | OASIS module audit | ≥98% |
| OASIS Quality Reviewer review completed within 5 business days for all SOC assessments | Review log audit | ≥95% |
| Monthly OASIS accuracy audit completed | Audit log review | 100% monthly |

### 8.2 What Surveyors and Auditors Will Look For
CMS surveyors conducting an OASIS validation survey (specifically targeting OASIS accuracy under 42 CFR § 484.20 and § 484.55) will:
Select a sample of submitted OASIS assessments and independently re-assess the patients — or review the clinical record — to determine whether the submitted responses accurately reflected the patient's status at the time of the assessment. Surveyors are trained in OASIS and will identify item-specific errors.
Compare OASIS responses to narrative documentation — for every item reviewed, they will look for a narrative entry that supports the coded response. A response of "2 — Substantial/Maximal Assistance" for a GG item requires a narrative description of the patient performing the activity with that level of assistance.
Look for patterns of inaccuracy — a single item error may be cited as a standard-level deficiency; a systematic pattern of the same item being incorrectly coded across multiple patients suggests a systemic training or oversight failure and may be cited as a Condition-level deficiency.
Request the agency's OASIS quality review documentation — they will look for evidence that the agency has an active OASIS accuracy program, including Quality Reviewer documentation, accuracy audit results, and clinician feedback records.
Review the Authorized Assessor Roster — they will verify that OASIS items were completed by authorized RNs.
MAC Additional Documentation Request (ADR) auditors will specifically examine OASIS functional status items (GG section) and clinical severity items because these drive PDGM payment classification. Items coded at higher severity levels than the clinical record supports are the primary target of False Claims Act enforcement in home health.
### 8.3 Common Failure Points

| Failure Point | Risk | Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GG functional items coded based on patient report alone without observation | OASIS inaccuracy; ADR denial | Train all RNs to observe the patient perform each activity during the assessment; document the observation |
| Reverse-staging of healing pressure injuries | OASIS deficiency; quality measure distortion | Annual wound staging competency; Director of Nursing reviews all wound OASIS items monthly |
| BIMS administered incorrectly or abbreviated | M1700 inaccuracy; behavioral health item errors | Annual BIMS competency validation with observation |
| Medication OASIS items coded without completing drug regimen review | Process measure inaccuracy; False Claims Act risk | Structured medication review checklist integrated into the assessment workflow |
| OASIS Quality Reviewer role not filled or not actively reviewing | Loss of pre-submission accuracy layer | Director of Nursing designates a qualified OASIS Quality Reviewer at hire; the Reviewer is listed on the Authorized Assessor Roster with specialty designation |

## 10. Training & Acknowledgment Requirements
10.1 All RNs authorized to conduct OASIS assessments shall complete the OASIS Competency Program per CL-CA-001 before independent assessment. The program shall include OASIS-specific training covering all high-risk item categories (GG functional, wound, behavioral health, medication management) with item-level decision-rule training per the OASIS-E2 Guidance Manual.
10.2 Annual OASIS accuracy refresher training shall be provided to all authorized RN assessors, incorporating: (a) any changes to the OASIS data set or CMS guidance since the prior training; (b) the agency's OASIS accuracy audit findings from the prior year, including the most common errors and corrective guidance; (c) OASIS response selection decision-practice exercises using case scenarios.
10.3 The OASIS Quality Reviewer shall complete advanced OASIS training (OASIS specialist certification or equivalent) and shall maintain current knowledge of CMS guidance updates. The Director of Nursing shall verify the OASIS Quality Reviewer's qualifications annually.
10.4 All personnel within scope shall sign the Policy Acknowledgment Form (Appendix D) within 14 calendar days of the effective date, any revision, or hire/appointment.
## 11. Version Control
11.1 This policy is maintained under the agency's enterprise policy lifecycle management system per policy EN-LC-001.
11.2 Only the most current approved version of this policy, as reflected in the policy header, is valid for any operational, compliance, or regulatory purpose. All superseded versions must be archived and clearly marked as "SUPERSEDED — NOT FOR USE."
11.3 Any substantive revision to this policy requires: (a) review and approval by the Governing Body, documented in meeting minutes; (b) re-acknowledgment by all personnel within scope within 14 calendar days of the revised effective date; (c) update to the enterprise policy index per EN-TG-001.
11.4 Non-substantive revisions (formatting, typographical corrections, updated cross-references) may be approved by the Administrator with notification to the Governing Body at the next regular meeting.

## 2. Purpose
This policy defines the requirements and timeframes for OASIS data transmission to the CMS OASIS repository and establishes the procedures for error identification and correction at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. OASIS transmission is the formal act by which the agency discharges its CMS-mandated obligation to report patient assessment data — and its failure is an absolute regulatory deficiency. There is no clinical, operational, or financial justification that excuses non-transmission or late transmission of OASIS data. Under 42 CFR § 484.20, CMS requires that all Medicare-certified home health agencies transmit OASIS data to the national repository within defined timeframes, and CMS conditions the agency's Medicare certification on ongoing compliance with this requirement. An agency that fails to transmit OASIS data loses its ability to receive Medicare payment for the affected episodes. An agency that transmits systematically inaccurate OASIS data — and fails to correct it — is generating distorted quality measures that misrepresent the care it provides to patients, its referral sources, and the public.
This policy establishes the complete transmission workflow: who is responsible for transmission, how transmission is performed, how transmission success is confirmed, how transmission failures are identified and resolved, how post-submission corrections are made when data errors are discovered, and how the agency maintains a complete, auditable record of all OASIS submissions and corrections. This policy implements 42 CFR § 484.20 (Reporting OASIS Information) and CMS OASIS data submission technical specifications.
## 3. Scope
This policy applies to:
The designated OASIS Transmission Coordinator (the staff member responsible for managing the agency's OASIS data submission to CMS)
The Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager who provides clinical oversight of the transmission and correction process
The OASIS Quality Reviewer who identifies errors requiring correction
All authorized RN assessors whose assessments are subject to transmission and correction
IT staff supporting the EHR-to-CMS transmission infrastructure
The Compliance Officer who oversees OASIS data integrity
## 4. Policy Statement
4.1 All OASIS assessments shall be transmitted to the CMS OASIS national repository within the timeframes specified in Section 6.2. There are no exceptions to the CMS transmission deadline for Medicare-certified agencies.
4.2 The agency shall designate a qualified OASIS Transmission Coordinator who is responsible for: initiating and confirming all OASIS transmissions; monitoring the CMS response files for acceptance, rejection, and warning notifications; maintaining the agency's OASIS submission log; and escalating any transmission failure or rejection to the Director of Nursing within 24 hours.
4.3 Transmission shall be performed using the agency's certified OASIS submission software, connected to the CMS OASIS repository through the approved state data collection system or CMS direct submission pathway. The agency shall maintain current software licenses and system certifications required for OASIS transmission.
4.4 Every transmission shall be confirmed — the agency shall not assume transmission was successful without verifying the CMS acceptance response file. A transmission without a confirmed CMS acceptance is not a completed transmission regardless of whether the data was sent.
4.5 When a CMS response file identifies rejected records or warning messages, the OASIS Transmission Coordinator shall investigate and resolve every rejection within 5 business days of receipt of the response file. Rejected records shall be corrected and resubmitted within 5 business days of rejection identification.
4.6 When an error is identified in a submitted OASIS record — whether through the agency's internal audit process per CL-CA-002, through a CMS OASIS validation finding, through an ADR audit finding, or through any other means — the agency shall initiate the OASIS correction process within 5 business days of identifying the error. All corrections shall be clinically justified, documented, and processed through the CMS correction pathway.
4.7 OASIS data shall not be corrected for any reason other than to improve the accuracy of the record relative to the patient's actual clinical status at the time of the assessment. Revenue optimization, payment correction, or any other financial motivation for a correction is prohibited. All corrections shall be clinically justified in writing before processing.
4.8 The agency shall maintain a complete OASIS Submission Log documenting every transmission including: date of transmission, time point, number of records transmitted, CMS response status, any rejected records and the reason for rejection, corrections made, and resubmission dates.
## 5. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| OASIS Repository | The CMS-maintained national database that receives and stores all OASIS data submitted by Medicare-certified home health agencies. |
| CMS Response File | The electronic file returned by the CMS system after each OASIS data transmission, indicating whether each submitted record was accepted, rejected, or accepted with warnings. |
| Transmission Coordinator | The designated agency staff member responsible for managing OASIS data submissions to CMS, monitoring response files, and resolving transmission issues. |
| Rejected Record | An OASIS record that was not accepted by the CMS repository due to a data format error, missing required item, logical inconsistency, or system error. Rejected records must be corrected and resubmitted. |
| Warning Message | A CMS notification that an accepted OASIS record contains a potential data quality concern — the record was accepted but the CMS system flagged a response as potentially inconsistent. Warnings do not constitute rejections but should be investigated. |
| Correction (Inactivation) | The process of inactivating a submitted OASIS record and replacing it with a corrected version. Used when a clinical error in a submitted record is identified. |
| Inactivation | The CMS process by which a submitted OASIS record is voided from the repository. Used for records that should not have been submitted (e.g., patient was not actually admitted, wrong time point was submitted). |
| Submission Window | The CMS-defined timeframe within which OASIS data for a specific time point must be transmitted to the repository. Late submission is a compliance deficiency. |
| OASIS Submission Log | The agency's internal record of all OASIS transmissions, including transmission dates, record counts, CMS response status, rejections, corrections, and resubmissions. |

## 6. Procedures
### 6.1 OASIS Data Preparation for Transmission

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.1.1 | OASIS Transmission Coordinator | Generate a daily report from the agency's EHR listing all OASIS assessments that have been locked and approved for transmission but have not yet been transmitted to CMS. Review the report against the OASIS Submission Log to identify any records approaching their transmission deadline. | Daily by 8:00 AM. |
| 6.1.2 | OASIS Transmission Coordinator | For each assessment pending transmission, confirm: (a) the assessment has been locked by the assessing RN; (b) the OASIS Quality Reviewer review has been completed per CL-CA-002 and no outstanding corrections are pending; (c) all required data elements for the applicable time point are present and complete; (d) the assessment date and time point code are accurate. | Before each transmission batch. |
| 6.1.3 | OASIS Transmission Coordinator | If any assessment is identified as having an outstanding Quality Reviewer correction pending, do not transmit the record until the correction is completed. Notify the Director of Nursing if the pending correction will cause the assessment to approach the transmission deadline. | Before transmission; escalate to Director of Nursing if the correction will cause a deadline risk. |

### 6.2 OASIS Transmission Deadlines and Process

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.2.1 | OASIS Transmission Coordinator | Transmit all OASIS assessments to the CMS repository within the following CMS-specified deadlines: (a) SOC assessments — transmitted within 30 calendar days of the SOC date; (b) ROC assessments — transmitted within 30 calendar days of the ROC date; (c) RECERT assessments — transmitted within 30 calendar days of the recertification date; (d) FU (SCIC) assessments — transmitted within 30 calendar days of the assessment date; (e) TRN assessments — transmitted within 30 calendar days of the transfer date; (f) DC assessments — transmitted within 30 calendar days of the discharge date. Note: The 30-day CMS deadline is the regulatory maximum — the agency's operational target is transmission within 10 calendar days of the assessment date to allow time for correction and resubmission before the deadline if needed. | Per CMS deadlines; agency target is 10 calendar days. |
| 6.2.2 | OASIS Transmission Coordinator | Perform OASIS transmissions using the agency's certified OASIS submission software. Transmit records in batch submissions at minimum twice per week (Monday and Thursday), and additionally on any day when an assessment is identified as approaching the transmission deadline. | At minimum twice weekly. |
| 6.2.3 | OASIS Transmission Coordinator | For each transmission batch: (a) document the transmission in the OASIS Submission Log (Appendix A) including: date and time of transmission, number of records transmitted, assessment time points included, and the name of the staff member initiating the transmission; (b) retain the electronic export file and the submission confirmation from the agency's EHR or OASIS submission software; (c) await the CMS response file. | At each transmission; documented in the Submission Log. |

### 6.3 CMS Response File Processing

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.3.1 | OASIS Transmission Coordinator | Retrieve and review the CMS response file within 2 business days of transmission. The response file will identify each submitted record as: accepted, accepted with warnings, or rejected. | Within 2 business days of transmission. |
| 6.3.2 | OASIS Transmission Coordinator | For each accepted record without warnings: update the OASIS Submission Log to reflect the CMS acceptance. No further action required for accepted records. | At the time of response file review. |
| 6.3.3 | OASIS Transmission Coordinator | For each record accepted with warnings: document the warning code and message in the OASIS Submission Log. Notify the Director of Nursing of all warnings within 24 hours of receipt. The Director of Nursing shall assess whether the warning indicates a clinical data quality concern requiring investigation. If the warning indicates a potential accuracy issue, initiate the correction assessment per Section 6.4. | Within 24 hours of response file receipt. |
| 6.3.4 | OASIS Transmission Coordinator | For each rejected record: document the rejection code and reason in the OASIS Submission Log. Notify the Director of Nursing within 24 hours. Investigate the rejection reason — which may be a data format error, a missing required element, a logical inconsistency, or a system error. Resolve the rejection cause and resubmit within 5 business days of rejection identification. | Within 24 hours of rejection; resubmission within 5 business days. |
| 6.3.5 | Director of Nursing | For rejections that cannot be resolved within 5 business days due to clinical complexity, notify the Administrator and contact the CMS OASIS Help Desk or the state OASIS coordinator for guidance. Document all contacts and the agency's efforts to resolve the rejection. | By Day 5 if not resolved; escalation immediately. |

### 6.4 OASIS Correction Process

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.4.1 | Director of Nursing / OASIS Quality Reviewer | When an error in a submitted OASIS record is identified through any means (internal audit per CL-CA-002, CMS response file warning, ADR audit finding, OASIS validation finding, self-identification by the assessing RN), document the identified error in the Correction Assessment Form (Appendix B) including: the specific item(s) in error, the submitted response, the correct response supported by clinical evidence, the reason the original response was inaccurate, and the clinical documentation that supports the correction. | Within 5 business days of error identification. |
| 6.4.2 | Director of Nursing | Review and approve the Correction Assessment Form before initiating any OASIS correction in the EHR or CMS system. The Director of Nursing's signature on the form confirms: (a) the correction is clinically justified; (b) the corrected response is supported by documented clinical evidence; (c) the correction is being made to improve accuracy — not for financial or revenue purposes. | Before initiating the correction. |
| 6.4.3 | Assigned RN / Director of Nursing | Process the OASIS correction in the agency's EHR using the correction/inactivation function. If the correction involves a response change (not a full record inactivation), the EHR shall generate a corrected OASIS record that retains the original assessment date. If the entire record should not have been submitted (e.g., wrong time point, patient was not actually admitted), initiate the inactivation process rather than a correction. | Within 5 business days of Director of Nursing approval. |
| 6.4.4 | OASIS Transmission Coordinator | Transmit the corrected OASIS record to the CMS repository as a correction transmission. Document the correction transmission in the OASIS Submission Log including: the original assessment date, the time point, the items corrected, the correction date, and the CMS confirmation of the correction acceptance. | Within 2 business days of correction processing. |
| 6.4.5 | Compliance Officer | Review all corrections where the corrected OASIS response results in a payment change — either an increase or a decrease in the PDGM payment group. If the correction results in a decrease in payment (i.e., the original OASIS response led to overpayment), assess whether a Medicare overpayment exists and initiate the repayment process per FN-BC-004 within the 60-day CMS repayment requirement. | Within 14 calendar days of correction transmission for payment-affecting corrections. |
| 6.4.6 | Director of Nursing | Document all corrections in the Correction Log (Appendix C) and report a summary of all corrections made in the prior quarter to the QAPI Committee at each quarterly meeting, including: the number of corrections, the reason categories, and any accuracy improvement actions taken. | Quarterly QAPI reporting. |

### 6.5 Transmission Failure Response

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.5.1 | OASIS Transmission Coordinator | If a technical transmission failure occurs (submission software error, internet connectivity failure, CMS system unavailability), document the failure in the OASIS Submission Log with the date, time, error description, and immediate troubleshooting actions taken. | At the time of the failure. |
| 6.5.2 | OASIS Transmission Coordinator | Notify the Director of Nursing and IT staff of the transmission failure within 4 hours. Attempt to resolve the technical issue and retransmit within 24 hours. | Within 4 hours; retransmission attempted within 24 hours. |
| 6.5.3 | Director of Nursing | If the transmission failure cannot be resolved within 24 hours, contact the CMS OASIS Help Desk to document the agency's transmission attempts and request guidance. Document the contact and the CMS guidance received. | After 24 hours without resolution. |
| 6.5.4 | Director of Nursing | Assess whether the transmission failure will cause any assessment to exceed the CMS submission deadline. If a deadline will be missed due to a documented technical failure beyond the agency's control, document all efforts to transmit and maintain the documentation for potential CMS review. | Continuously during the failure period. |

### 6.6 Escalation and Exception Handling

| Condition | Escalation Path | Corrective Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Assessment not transmitted within 10-calendar-day agency operational target | OASIS Transmission Coordinator alerts Director of Nursing | Director of Nursing assesses the reason. If the delay is due to a pending Quality Reviewer correction, expedite the correction. If due to operational failure, transmit immediately. | Transmission within 24 hours of identification. |
| CMS rejection rate exceeds 5% in any transmission batch | Director of Nursing and IT | Investigate systemic cause — may indicate EHR configuration error or OASIS software issue. IT reviews the submission file format. Director of Nursing reviews all rejected records for clinical data quality issues. | Investigation within 5 business days. |
| A correction is requested by Revenue Cycle without a clinical basis | Compliance Officer | Reject the correction request. The Compliance Officer confirms that corrections may only be made for clinical accuracy reasons and shall document the Revenue Cycle request and the rejection. | Immediately upon identification. |
| CMS notifies the agency of an OASIS data quality concern through the CMS Quality Improvement Organization or state survey agency | Director of Nursing and Compliance Officer | Conduct a full-scope review of the identified data quality concern. Develop a corrective action plan. Implement corrections for all affected records. Report to the Governing Body at the next quarterly meeting. | Corrective action plan within 14 calendar days; Governing Body report at next quarterly meeting. |

## 8. Compliance & Audit Considerations
### 8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

| Compliance Indicator | Measurement Method | Acceptable Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| All OASIS assessments transmitted within the 30-day CMS deadline | Submission Log audit vs. assessment dates | 100% — zero late transmissions |
| Agency operational transmission target — 10 calendar days | Submission Log audit | ≥95% transmitted within 10 calendar days |
| CMS response file reviewed within 2 business days | Submission Log review dates | ≥98% |
| Rejected records resolved and resubmitted within 5 business days | Rejection resolution log | ≥95% |
| All corrections clinically justified with documented basis | Correction Assessment Form audit | 100% |
| OASIS Submission Log maintained and current | Log completeness audit | 100% — current log with no missing entries |

### 8.2 What Surveyors and Auditors Will Look For
CMS surveyors will request the agency's OASIS Submission Log and verify that all assessments for the survey look-back period were transmitted within the 30-day deadline. They will also verify that the agency has a CMS response file review process and that rejections were resolved. Surveyors will specifically look for evidence of correction requests that appear financially motivated — corrections that always result in higher payment groups are a red flag for upcoding.
### 8.3 Common Failure Points

| Failure Point | Risk | Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Assessments transmitted but CMS response file not reviewed | Undetected rejections; assessments not in the CMS database | Mandatory 2-business-day response file review; Transmission Coordinator daily report |
| Corrections made without clinical justification documented | False Claims Act risk | Correction Assessment Form required before any correction; Director of Nursing sign-off mandatory |
| OASIS software not updated after CMS data set changes | Rejected records due to format errors | IT monitors CMS updates; software update within 30 calendar days of any CMS data set change |

# CL-CA-004 — Recertification Assessment & Process
## 1. Policy Header

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Policy ID | CL-CA-004 |
| Policy Title | Recertification Assessment & Process |
| Domain | CL — Clinical Operations |
| Subdomain | CA — Clinical Assessment |
| Classification Tier | REQUIRED |
| Status | ACTIVE |
| Review Cycle | Annual |
| Access Tier | Tier 2 — Restricted |
| Policy Owner / Steward | Director of Nursing |
| Effective Date | 2025-07-10 |
| Version | 1.0 |
| Approved By | Governing Body Chair — Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. |
| Last Reviewed | 2025-07-10 |
| Next Review Date | 2026-07-10 |
| Supersedes | N/A (Initial Version) |

## 2. Purpose
This policy defines the assessment, documentation, and physician approval process for recertification of home health eligibility at each 60-day certification period at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. Recertification is simultaneously the most critically time-constrained clinical process in home health and the most consequential for both the patient and the agency's revenue integrity. A recertification that is not completed within the Day 56–60 window is a CMS compliance failure. A recertification that is completed but not supported by documented clinical findings of continued eligibility is a billing compliance failure. A recertification that is completed on time and documented but for which the physician signature is not obtained before the next episode's claims are submitted is a False Claims Act exposure.
The recertification assessment is not merely an administrative exercise — it is a genuine, comprehensive clinical assessment of the patient's current status, the legitimacy of their continued home health eligibility, and the appropriateness of the proposed plan for the next certification period. Every recertification must answer three questions with documented clinical evidence: (1) Does this patient continue to meet the Medicare homebound criteria? (2) Does this patient continue to require skilled services? (3) Is the proposed plan of care for the next period clinically appropriate and achievable? If any of these three questions cannot be answered affirmatively with documented clinical evidence, the patient shall not be recertified. This policy implements 42 CFR § 424.22(b) (recertification requirements for Medicare home health) and CMS recertification standards in the Home Health Benefit Manual, Chapter 7, § 30.2.
## 3. Scope
This policy applies to:
All registered nurses conducting recertification assessments
The Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager responsible for recertification oversight
Clinical Coordinators managing the recertification tracking schedule per CL-CP-008
Physicians and allowed practitioners who certify continued eligibility
Medical Records staff managing recertification documentation
Revenue Cycle staff whose billing depends on completed recertifications
## 4. Policy Statement
4.1 Every active home health patient receiving Medicare home health services shall be formally recertified for each subsequent 60-day certification period. There is no mechanism by which a patient may continue to receive Medicare home health services — and the agency may continue to bill for those services — without a completed, physician-signed recertification.
4.2 The recertification assessment — including all applicable OASIS data elements for the RECERT time point — shall be completed by a qualified RN within the Day 56–60 window of the current certification period. This 5-day window is defined by CMS and is non-negotiable: an assessment completed before Day 56 or after Day 60 is not a valid RECERT assessment.
4.3 The recertification assessment shall be a genuine, comprehensive re-evaluation of the patient's current clinical status — not a copy-forward or update of the SOC assessment, and not a perfunctory documentation exercise. Every RECERT OASIS item shall reflect the patient's actual status at the time of the RECERT assessment.
4.4 The recertification shall document, with patient-specific clinical evidence: (a) the patient's continued homebound status and the specific functional limitations that support the homebound determination; (b) the continued need for skilled services and why those services remain medically necessary; (c) the patient's progress (or lack thereof) during the current certification period; (d) the proposed plan of care for the next certification period including updated diagnoses, services, goals, and physician orders; (e) the clinical rationale for the proposed visit frequency in the next period.
4.5 If the recertification assessment reveals that the patient no longer meets the Medicare homebound criteria or no longer requires skilled services, the patient shall not be recertified. The clinician shall document the findings, notify the physician, and initiate discharge planning per CL-CP-006.
4.6 The recertification plan of care shall be transmitted to the certifying physician for signature no later than the last day of the current certification period. Physician signature tracking shall be maintained per CL-CP-008 and CL-CP-009. No Medicare claim for the new certification period shall be submitted without a physician-signed recertification on file.
4.7 Recertification assessments shall not be conducted more than 5 days before the start of the assessment window (Day 56) or at any time after the current certification period has expired (after Day 60). An assessment conducted outside the Day 56–60 window is not a valid RECERT assessment and must be submitted as a different time point or corrected per CL-CA-003.
## 5. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Recertification | The formal process by which a physician re-certifies that a patient continues to meet the Medicare criteria for home health services for a subsequent 60-day certification period. |
| Certification Period | A period of not more than 60 calendar days during which the physician certifies (or recertifies) that the patient is eligible for Medicare home health services. The first certification period begins with the SOC date. |
| Day 56–60 Window | The five-calendar-day window within which the OASIS RECERT assessment must be conducted. Day 1 is the SOC date or the first day of the current certification period. Day 56 is 55 days after Day 1; Day 60 is 59 days after Day 1. |
| RECERT Time Point | The CMS-defined OASIS assessment time point corresponding to the recertification of a patient for a subsequent certification period. |
| Recertification Narrative | The clinical summary that is a required component of the recertification plan of care, documenting the patient's current diagnoses, functional status, homebound status, continued need for skilled services, and proposed services for the next period. |
| Copy-Forward | The practice of carrying forward data from a prior assessment into the current assessment without re-evaluation — prohibited for OASIS assessments, which must reflect the patient's current status at the time of the specific assessment. |
| Continued Eligibility | The determination that a patient continues to meet all Medicare home health benefit criteria: homebound status, need for skilled services, services are reasonable and necessary, and a physician-approved plan of care is in place. |

## 6. Procedures
### 6.1 Recertification Scheduling and Tracking

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.1.1 | Clinical Coordinator | Using the Recertification Tracking System per CL-CP-008, identify all patients whose Day 56 falls within the next 20 calendar days. Generate and distribute the Recertification Due Report to the Director of Nursing and all assigned RNs. | No later than Day 40 of each certification period. |
| 6.1.2 | Clinical Coordinator | Schedule the recertification assessment visit within the Day 56–60 window for every patient on the report. Confirm the scheduled date with the assigned RN and the patient/caregiver. Document the scheduled date in the Recertification Tracking System. | No later than Day 50. |
| 6.1.3 | Director of Nursing | Verify by Day 50 that a recertification assessment is scheduled for every patient approaching Day 56. For any patient without a scheduled assessment, escalate immediately to the Director of Nursing for same-day scheduling. | Day 50 verification. |
| 6.1.4 | Clinical Coordinator | If a scheduled recertification assessment cannot occur on the planned date within the Day 56–60 window (patient hospitalized, patient unavailable), notify the Director of Nursing immediately. The Director of Nursing shall assess whether the window can still be met and shall coordinate an alternate visit. | Immediately upon identifying a scheduling conflict within the window. |

### 6.2 Recertification Assessment — Content and Conduct

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.2.1 | Assigned RN | Before the recertification visit, review: the patient's SOC assessment; all visit notes from the current certification period; the current plan of care; the physician's most recent orders; any hospitalization or significant changes during the period; and the current medication list. Prepare the recertification plan of care draft based on the review, to be finalized after the assessment visit. | Before the recertification visit. |
| 6.2.2 | Assigned RN | At the recertification visit, conduct a comprehensive assessment of the patient's current status using all applicable OASIS RECERT time point items. The assessment shall be conducted as a fresh, contemporaneous evaluation of the patient's current status — not a comparison exercise against the prior assessment. Every OASIS item shall reflect what the patient's status is at this moment of assessment, using the applicable look-back periods specified in the CMS OASIS-E2 Guidance Manual. | During the Day 56–60 window visit. |
| 6.2.3 | Assigned RN | At the recertification visit, specifically assess and document: (a) the patient's current homebound status — what specific functional limitations currently prevent the patient from leaving home without considerable effort? These shall be patient-specific, current limitations — not a restatement of the SOC homebound documentation; (b) the continued need for skilled services — specifically, what services are still required and why they are still medically necessary? This documentation shall address both continuity (the original skilled need persists) and currency (the skilled need is assessed based on the patient's current status); (c) the patient's progress toward goals — which goals have been met, which remain in progress, which have been modified, and which have not been achieved with explanation; (d) the appropriate visit frequency for the next certification period — based on current clinical status, not maintained from the prior period by default. | During the recertification visit. |
| 6.2.4 | Assigned RN | Develop the recertification plan of care for the subsequent certification period, incorporating: (a) all diagnoses, updated to reflect current conditions; (b) current and accurate medication list; (c) services and visit frequencies appropriate to current clinical needs; (d) updated, measurable goals for the next period; (e) any new safety measures; (f) the recertification narrative per Section 6.3. | Within 24 hours of the recertification visit. |
| 6.2.5 | Assigned RN | Complete and lock all applicable OASIS RECERT items in the EHR within 5 calendar days of the recertification visit, after completing the pre-submission self-review per CL-CA-002 and CL-OA-019. | Within 5 calendar days of the recertification visit. |

### 6.3 Recertification Narrative Requirements
The recertification narrative is a required component of the recertification plan of care and shall contain the following elements, each documented with patient-specific clinical content:

| Narrative Element | Required Content |
| --- | --- |
| Current primary and secondary diagnoses | Updated ICD-10 diagnoses reflecting the patient's current conditions — including any new diagnoses identified during the episode and any diagnoses that have resolved |
| Homebound status | Patient-specific functional limitations that prevent the patient from leaving home without considerable and taxing effort — must be current and specific (e.g., "Patient requires assistance of two to transfer from bed to chair and ambulates ≤15 feet before requiring rest due to severe dyspnea; SOB at rest on 2L NC" not "patient has difficulty ambulating") |
| Continued skilled need | Identification of each skilled discipline ordered for the next period with the clinical reason each is still medically necessary |
| Functional progress during the current period | Measurable description of the patient's progress toward goals — what improved, what remained stable, what declined, and the clinical explanation |
| Prognosis for the next period | The clinician's assessment of the patient's potential for continued benefit from home health services in the next 60-day period |
| Proposed plan for the next period | A clear description of the services, frequency, and goals proposed for the next certification period |

### 6.4 Non-Recertification — When Recertification Is Not Appropriate

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.4.1 | Assigned RN | At every recertification assessment, evaluate the patient's continued eligibility using the three eligibility questions in Section 2 (homebound? skilled need? clinically appropriate plan?). If any question cannot be answered affirmatively with documented clinical evidence, do not proceed with recertification. | During the recertification assessment. |
| 6.4.2 | Assigned RN | If the patient no longer meets recertification criteria, document the clinical findings supporting the non-recertification determination: the specific evidence that the patient no longer requires skilled services, is no longer homebound, or whose continued treatment would not result in meaningful clinical progress. | Within 24 hours of the recertification assessment. |
| 6.4.3 | Assigned RN | Notify the physician within 24 hours of the non-recertification determination, providing the clinical summary and requesting a physician discharge order. Initiate discharge planning per CL-CP-006. | Within 24 hours. |
| 6.4.4 | Assigned RN | Do not schedule or deliver skilled visits after the expiration of the current certification period if the patient is not being recertified. Services delivered after the certification period expiration without a new physician-signed recertification are not billable under Medicare. | Immediately upon non-recertification determination. |

### 6.5 Escalation and Exception Handling

| Condition | Escalation Path | Corrective Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Recertification assessment is not completed within the Day 56–60 window | Director of Nursing identifies | Director of Nursing assesses the reason and determines whether services may continue. If the window is narrowly missed (Day 61–62) and the patient continues to require skilled services, consult the Compliance Officer regarding billing implications. Complete the assessment as soon as possible. Do not bill for services after Day 60 without a valid recertification. | Assessment completed immediately; Compliance Officer consultation within 24 hours. |
| Patient is hospitalized during the Day 56–60 window | Director of Nursing | A recertification assessment cannot be conducted during an inpatient stay. If the patient returns home before Day 60, attempt to complete the recertification visit. If the certification period expires while the patient is hospitalized, a new SOC assessment is required upon the patient's return. | Immediate assessment upon patient's return from hospitalization if within window. |
| Physician refuses to recertify despite the patient meeting eligibility criteria | Director of Nursing and Administrator | Director of Nursing engages the physician to discuss the clinical basis for the refusal. If the disagreement is substantive, consult the Compliance Officer. Services cannot continue without a physician-signed recertification regardless of the clinical team's assessment of the patient's eligibility. | Resolution within 7 calendar days. |
| Recertification assessment reveals clinical findings inconsistent with prior documentation | Director of Nursing and OASIS Quality Reviewer | Review the entire episode record for documentation integrity concerns. If the inconsistency suggests prior visit documentation does not accurately reflect the patient's clinical status, notify the Compliance Officer. Assess for potential OASIS correction needs per CL-CA-003. | Compliance Officer notification within 48 hours. |

## 7. Documentation Requirements

| Requirement | Document / Record | Responsible Party | Location | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| RECERT OASIS assessment | All applicable OASIS RECERT time point items | Assigned RN | EHR — OASIS module | Within 5 calendar days of RECERT visit; retained minimum 7 years |
| Recertification assessment narrative | Comprehensive narrative per Section 6.2.3 | Assigned RN | EHR — assessment module | Within 24 hours of RECERT visit |
| Recertification plan of care | Updated POC with recertification narrative per Section 6.3 | Assigned RN | EHR — plan of care | Within 24 hours of RECERT visit |
| Physician recertification signature | Physician-signed recertification document | Certifying physician / Medical Records | EHR — clinical record | Before claim submission for new certification period; retained minimum 7 years |
| Recertification Tracking System entry | Updated tracking data per CL-CP-008 | Clinical Coordinator | Recertification Tracking System | At each milestone per CL-CP-008 |
| Non-recertification documentation | Clinical findings and physician notification for non-recertified patients | Assigned RN | EHR — clinical record | Within 24 hours of non-recertification determination |
| Policy acknowledgment | Signed acknowledgment — Appendix A | Each individual; Administrator (collection) | Policy acknowledgment file | Within 14 calendar days |

## 8. Compliance & Audit Considerations
### 8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

| Compliance Indicator | Measurement Method | Acceptable Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| RECERT assessments completed within Day 56–60 window | OASIS date audit vs. certification period dates | ≥98% within the 5-day window |
| RECERT narrative contains all required elements per Section 6.3 | Chart audit | ≥95% |
| Homebound status documented with patient-specific current limitations | Chart audit | ≥95% |
| Physician-signed recertification on file before claim submission | Revenue Cycle pre-bill verification | 100% |
| RECERT OASIS accurate and consistent with narrative | OASIS Quality Reviewer review | ≥95% |

### 8.2 What Surveyors and Auditors Will Look For
Surveyors will request all RECERT assessments for the look-back period and verify: the assessment date falls within the Day 56–60 window; the homebound and skilled need documentation is patient-specific and current; the recertification plan reflects the patient's actual current status; and the physician-signed recertification is on file. ADR auditors will cross-reference the RECERT OASIS responses against the visit note narratives from the last 30 days of the current period to verify that the RECERT accurately reflects the patient's trajectory.
### 8.3 Common Failure Points

| Failure Point | Risk | Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| RECERT conducted on Day 55 or Day 61 | CMS compliance deficiency; invalid RECERT | Day 40 alert in Recertification Tracking System; Day 50 Director of Nursing verification |
| Homebound and skilled need documentation copied from SOC | Survey citation; billing vulnerability | Train RNs to write current, patient-specific RECERT narratives; Director of Nursing audit |
| Services delivered after Day 60 without signed recertification | False Claims Act risk | Revenue Cycle billing hold; Recertification Tracking System alert |

# CL-CA-005 — Homebound Status Determination & Documentation
## 1. Policy Header

| Policy Title | Homebound Status Determination & Documentation |
| Domain | CL — Clinical Operations |

| Review Cycle | Annual |

| Effective Date | 2025-07-10 |
