## 2. Purpose
This policy establishes the criteria and documentation requirements for determining and verifying patient homebound status per CMS guidelines at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. Homebound status is the gating criterion for Medicare home health eligibility — a patient who is not homebound is categorically ineligible for the Medicare home health benefit, regardless of how much skilled care they need or how medically complex they are. If a patient is not homebound and the agency bills Medicare for home health services, the claim is false. There is no amount of skilled need, physician documentation, or clinical good faith that makes a non-homebound patient billable.
Yet homebound determination is also one of the most consistently misunderstood, inconsistently documented, and frequently litigated aspects of home health compliance. ADR auditors deny claims for homebound documentation failures more frequently than for almost any other reason. The most common failures are: homebound documentation that is generic and not patient-specific; homebound documentation that is copied forward from the SOC without re-evaluation; homebound documentation that fails to address the "considerable and taxing effort" standard; and homebound documentation that focuses on the patient's diagnosis rather than their specific functional limitations. This policy establishes a clear, operationally precise framework for homebound determination and documentation that eliminates these failure modes. It implements 42 CFR § 409.42(a) (homebound criteria), the CMS Home Health Benefit Manual Chapter 7, § 30.1, and the CMS OASIS-E2 Guidance Manual homebound documentation requirements.
## 3. Scope
This policy applies to:
All registered nurses conducting comprehensive assessments, recertification assessments, and all OASIS time point assessments
The Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager responsible for homebound documentation quality
The OASIS Quality Reviewer who validates homebound documentation at each assessment review
Revenue Cycle staff relying on homebound documentation to support billing
The Compliance Officer who oversees homebound documentation integrity
## 4. Policy Statement
4.1 A patient is homebound for purposes of Medicare home health eligibility if and only if both of the following criteria are met simultaneously: (a) Criterion 1 — Condition-Based Normal Inability to Leave Home: Due to illness or injury, the patient has a condition that restricts their ability to leave the home. This means the patient has a medical condition that would normally cause an individual to be confined to the home. A person who is not confined, or is confined only for non-medical reasons (e.g., lack of transportation, personal preference, caregiver unavailability), does not meet the homebound criteria. (b) Criterion 2 — Considerable and Taxing Effort: Leaving the home requires a considerable and taxing effort by the patient. The effort required must be caused by the patient's medical condition — not merely inconvenient or uncomfortable, but genuinely demanding due to the patient's illness or injury.
4.2 Both criteria must be met and both must be documented with patient-specific clinical language at every applicable assessment time point. Documentation that satisfies Criterion 1 but not Criterion 2, or Criterion 2 but not Criterion 1, is insufficient homebound documentation.
4.3 Homebound status does not mean the patient may never leave the home. A patient may leave the home for medical appointments, adult day care, religious services, or for other infrequent reasons and remain homebound — provided that leaving the home requires a considerable and taxing effort due to their medical condition.
4.4 Homebound status shall be assessed and documented at SOC, at each RECERT, and at any OASIS time point where homebound status is applicable. A homebound determination made at SOC does not automatically remain valid for subsequent periods — each period requires an independent homebound assessment.
4.5 Homebound documentation shall be written in patient-specific, functional, clinical language that describes: (a) the specific medical condition causing the normal inability to leave home; (b) the specific functional limitations that make leaving home require considerable and taxing effort; (c) the patient's current level of functional performance that supports the homebound determination. Generic, diagnosis-only, or template-driven homebound documentation is not sufficient.
4.6 The following factors are acceptable bases for homebound status when they create the conditions defined in Section 4.1: inability to ambulate without assistance of another person or an assistive device; dyspnea severe enough to restrict activity to short distances within the home; severe weakness, fatigue, or exercise intolerance; pain that significantly limits the patient's ability to leave the home; cognitive impairment that prevents safe unsupervised community mobility; paralysis or severe neurological deficits; post-surgical restrictions limiting mobility; psychiatric conditions that prevent leaving the home safely.
4.7 The following circumstances, standing alone, do not support homebound status: patient preference to remain at home; lack of transportation; caregiver unavailability; a diagnosis that sounds severe but does not functionally restrict the patient's ability to leave home; advanced age without functional limitation.
## 5. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Homebound Status | The CMS-defined patient characteristic required for Medicare home health eligibility: the patient has a condition due to illness or injury that restricts their ability to leave home, and leaving home requires considerable and taxing effort, as defined in 42 CFR § 409.42(a). |
| Normal Inability to Leave Home | The condition of a patient whose medical condition would normally keep them confined to the home — i.e., most patients with the same diagnosis and functional status would be unable to leave home freely. |
| Considerable and Taxing Effort | The degree of effort required for a homebound patient to leave the home — it must be genuinely demanding due to the medical condition, not merely inconvenient. Factors include: significant exertion required for the patient to prepare and exit the home; need for assistance of another person; need for medical equipment for transport; and significant symptomatic worsening from the effort. |
| Patient-Specific Documentation | Homebound documentation that describes the individual patient's specific diagnoses, functional limitations, and current performance — not generic or template language applied uniformly to all patients. |
| Generic Homebound Language | Homebound documentation that consists of diagnosis codes, medical terminology without functional context, or template language that does not describe this specific patient's current functional limitations — insufficient for Medicare billing purposes. |
| Taxing Effort Indicators | Observable or patient-reported findings that demonstrate leaving home requires considerable and taxing effort: post-exertion dyspnea, post-exertion fatigue, post-exertion pain exacerbation, requirement for multiple rest periods to prepare to leave, requirement for significant caregiver assistance, requirement for special transportation, or extended recovery period following a community excursion. |

## 6. Procedures
### 6.1 Homebound Determination at SOC

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.1.1 | Assigned RN | At the SOC visit, conduct a specific, focused homebound assessment that addresses both CMS criteria independently. Do not assume homebound status based on the patient's diagnosis or prior documentation from another setting. The homebound determination is made by the assessing RN based on direct clinical assessment at the time of the visit. | During the SOC visit. |
| 6.1.2 | Assigned RN | To assess Criterion 1 (condition-based normal inability to leave home), evaluate: what medical condition is restricting the patient's ability to leave the home? Is the restriction due to the illness or injury, or due to non-medical factors? What is the current severity of the condition and how does it functionally restrict the patient? | During the SOC visit. |
| 6.1.3 | Assigned RN | To assess Criterion 2 (considerable and taxing effort), evaluate: what would the patient have to do physically to leave the home? Does the patient require assistance of another person to exit? Does the patient require an assistive device? Would the effort of leaving worsen the patient's symptoms? Does the patient report being significantly taxed by the rare occasions they do leave home? Observe the patient's functional capacity during the visit and use this as clinical evidence. | During the SOC visit. |
| 6.1.4 | Assigned RN | Document the homebound status determination using the Homebound Documentation Standards defined in Section 6.3. Write the homebound narrative in the patient's assessment module and/or plan of care before or at the time of locking the OASIS. | Within 24 hours of the SOC visit. |

### 6.2 Homebound Assessment at Subsequent Time Points

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.2.1 | Assigned RN | At each RECERT assessment, independently reassess the patient's homebound status. A patient who met homebound criteria at SOC may or may not continue to meet criteria at RECERT — functional improvement may make leaving home less taxing, or functional decline may strengthen the homebound determination. Each RECERT homebound narrative shall be freshly written based on the patient's current status. | During each RECERT visit. |
| 6.2.2 | Assigned RN | At each OASIS time point, verify that homebound status has been re-assessed and that the homebound documentation reflects the patient's current functional limitations — not prior documentation. If the patient's functional status has changed since the prior assessment, the homebound documentation shall reflect the current status. | At each OASIS time point. |
| 6.2.3 | Assigned RN | At each skilled visit throughout the certification period (not only at OASIS time points), monitor the patient for functional changes that may affect homebound status. If the patient's functional status has improved to the point where leaving home no longer requires considerable and taxing effort, notify the Director of Nursing and the physician. The patient may no longer be homebound and continuation of services may require discharge or non-recertification. | At each skilled visit. |

### 6.3 Homebound Documentation Standards
All homebound documentation shall include the following elements, written with patient-specific clinical content:

| Documentation Element | Required Content | Example of Adequate Documentation | Example of Inadequate Documentation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Medical condition causing inability to leave home | The specific medical diagnosis or condition that restricts the patient from leaving home — not merely the diagnosis code | "Patient has severe biventricular heart failure (NYHA Class III) with persistent lower extremity edema 3+ bilateral and dyspnea at rest on 2L nasal cannula" | "Patient has CHF" or "Patient has cardiac condition" |
| Specific functional limitations | The precise functional impairments that result from the medical condition and make leaving home require considerable effort | "Patient is unable to ambulate more than 15 feet before requiring rest due to dyspnea; requires assistance of one person for transfers; cannot negotiate the three exterior steps without rest and standby assist of two" | "Patient has difficulty ambulating" or "patient is weak" |
| Evidence of considerable and taxing effort | Observable or patient-reported evidence that leaving home genuinely demands considerable physical effort | "Patient reports that on the one occasion she left home for a cardiac appointment in the prior month, she required 30 minutes to prepare and dress with caregiver assistance, rode in a wheelchair to the vehicle, required supplemental oxygen during transport, and required one hour of rest upon return before resuming normal home activities" | "Patient only leaves home for medical appointments" |
| Assistive device or assistance requirements | The level of human assistance and/or assistive device required for any community mobility | "Requires rolling walker for all ambulation and assistance of one person for stair negotiation; cannot independently access the vehicle due to inability to perform step transfers" | "Uses walker" |
| Frequency and circumstances of leaving home | How often and under what circumstances the patient leaves the home, demonstrating that community mobility is genuinely exceptional and taxing | "Patient leaves home approximately once per month for physician appointments only; transport is via medical transport van with wheelchair lift" | "Patient rarely leaves home" |

### 6.4 Homebound Status Monitoring During the Episode

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.4.1 | Assigned RN | At every skilled visit, document objective clinical indicators relevant to homebound status as part of the visit note: vital signs before and after any observed exertion; ambulation distance and quality; transfer assistance required; dyspnea assessment before and after activity. These routine visit note entries constitute the clinical evidentiary record that supports continued homebound status between OASIS assessments. | At each skilled visit. |
| 6.4.2 | Assigned RN | If the patient reports or demonstrates a significant improvement in functional status suggesting they may no longer be homebound — such as returning to driving, ambulating independently in the community, or working — document the finding and notify the Director of Nursing within 24 hours. | Within 24 hours of identification. |
| 6.4.3 | Director of Nursing | Upon notification of potential homebound status loss, conduct a clinical review within 48 hours and determine whether the patient continues to meet homebound criteria. If homebound criteria are no longer met, notify the physician and initiate discharge per CL-CP-006. | Within 48 hours of notification. |

### 6.5 Escalation and Exception Handling

| Condition | Escalation Path | Corrective Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| SOC or RECERT homebound documentation is generic and does not meet the standards in Section 6.3 | OASIS Quality Reviewer identifies during review | OASIS Quality Reviewer returns documentation to the assessing RN for specific rewrite before locking. The patient shall not be billed for the episode until adequate homebound documentation is on file. Director of Nursing provides coaching. | Documentation corrected before locking; coaching within 7 calendar days. |
| Evidence identified during the episode that the patient was not homebound at the time of the SOC | Director of Nursing and Compliance Officer | Compliance Officer conducts a billing review for the affected episode. If homebound criteria were not met at SOC, the episode may constitute a false claim. Self-disclosure may be required per OIG self-disclosure protocols. | Compliance Officer review within 5 business days; legal consultation as warranted. |
| Visit note documents the patient drove independently to the pharmacy — casting doubt on homebound status | Assigned RN notifies Director of Nursing | Director of Nursing assesses whether the patient continues to meet homebound criteria. If driving independently suggests homebound criteria are not met, initiate discharge planning and notify the physician. Document all findings. | Director of Nursing assessment within 48 hours. |
| A pattern of homebound documentation inconsistency across multiple RNs | Director of Nursing identifies during monthly audit | Agency-wide homebound documentation training. Director of Nursing provides written feedback to all RNs with specific examples of adequate vs. inadequate documentation. Re-audit within 30 calendar days. | Training within 14 calendar days; re-audit within 30 calendar days. |

## 7. Documentation Requirements

| Requirement | Document / Record | Responsible Party | Location | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Homebound status narrative at SOC | Patient-specific homebound documentation per Section 6.3 | Assigned RN | EHR — assessment module and plan of care | Within 24 hours of SOC visit; retained minimum 7 years |
| Homebound status narrative at RECERT | Freshly written, current homebound documentation | Assigned RN | EHR — assessment module and plan of care | Within 24 hours of RECERT visit |
| Visit note homebound-relevant clinical observations | Functional performance indicators documenting continued homebound status | Assigned RN | EHR — visit notes | At each skilled visit; within 24 hours |
| Director of Nursing homebound status loss review | Clinical review documentation | Director of Nursing | EHR — supervisory notes | Within 48 hours of notification |
| OASIS Quality Reviewer homebound documentation review | Review findings in the OASIS Quality Review Log | OASIS Quality Reviewer | OASIS Quality Review Log | At each applicable assessment review |
| Policy acknowledgment | Signed acknowledgment — Appendix A | Each individual; Administrator (collection) | Policy acknowledgment file | Within 14 calendar days |

## 8. Compliance & Audit Considerations
### 8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

| Compliance Indicator | Measurement Method | Acceptable Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| All SOC assessments contain patient-specific homebound documentation meeting the standards in Section 6.3 | OASIS Quality Reviewer review and Director of Nursing monthly audit | ≥95% |
| All RECERT assessments contain freshly written homebound documentation | Chart audit cross-referencing RECERT homebound narrative against SOC narrative | ≥95% non-copy-forward |
| Visit notes document homebound-relevant functional observations | Monthly chart audit | ≥90% |
| Patients identified as potentially non-homebound are assessed within 48 hours | Director of Nursing supervisory review | 100% |

### 8.2 What Surveyors and Auditors Will Look For
ADR auditors examining homebound documentation will look for: patient-specific language describing both CMS criteria; evidence that the documentation was freshly assessed at each time point; visit note entries that corroborate the homebound determination (e.g., visit notes describing the patient's functional limitations during visits are evidence of homebound status; visit notes describing the patient as "doing well" without any functional limitation documentation undermine it). Surveyors conducting standard CMS surveys will interview patients about their community mobility patterns and compare the patient's description to the homebound documentation in the clinical record.
### 8.3 Common Failure Points

| Failure Point | Risk | Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Homebound documentation consists only of diagnosis codes | ADR denial; not specific enough to support billing | Require narrative description of functional limitations in homebound section of EHR template |
| RECERT homebound documentation is a copy of SOC documentation | Survey deficiency; ADR denial | EHR configuration prevents copy-forward of homebound narrative field; Director of Nursing audits RECERT records monthly |
| Visit notes describe patient improvements without noting continued homebound indicators | Undermines homebound documentation | Train all RNs to include homebound-relevant functional observations in every visit note |

# CL-CA-006 — Face-to-Face Encounter Compliance
## 1. Policy Header

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Policy ID | CL-CA-006 |
| Policy Title | Face-to-Face Encounter Compliance |
| Domain | CL — Clinical Operations |
| Subdomain | CA — Clinical Assessment |
| Classification Tier | REQUIRED |
| Status | ACTIVE |
| Review Cycle | Annual |
| Access Tier | Tier 2 — Restricted |
| Policy Owner / Steward | Director of Nursing |
| Effective Date | 2025-07-10 |
| Version | 1.0 |
| Approved By | Governing Body Chair — Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. |
| Last Reviewed | 2025-07-10 |
| Next Review Date | 2026-07-10 |
| Supersedes | N/A (Initial Version) |

## 2. Purpose
This policy defines the requirements for physician or allowed practitioner face-to-face (F2F) encounters for home health patients at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc., per 42 CFR § 424.22. The face-to-face encounter requirement was established by the Affordable Care Act and implemented by CMS to reinforce physician oversight of home health services and to ensure that the certifying physician has directly assessed the patient within a defined timeframe of the home health episode's initiation. The F2F requirement is a threshold condition for Medicare home health billing: if the required F2F encounter is not present, properly documented, and appropriately timed, the agency's claims for that episode are not payable — regardless of the clinical validity of the care delivered.
The F2F requirement creates three distinct compliance obligations: (1) the encounter itself must have occurred within the required timeframe; (2) the encounter must have been conducted by a qualifying practitioner; and (3) the documentation of the encounter must meet the CMS content requirements. Failure in any one of these three dimensions is sufficient to render the episode's claims non-payable. This policy addresses all three dimensions with operational precision, establishing clear accountability for each element of the F2F compliance process, integrating F2F tracking into the agency's clinical workflow, and defining the escalation process when the F2F requirement is at risk of not being met. This policy implements 42 CFR § 424.22(a)(1)(iv) and CMS Home Health Benefit Manual, Chapter 7, § 30.5.
## 3. Scope
This policy applies to:
All registered nurses conducting SOC assessments who are responsible for verifying F2F compliance at the initiation of each episode
Clinical Coordinators responsible for F2F tracking per CL-CA-007
The Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager responsible for F2F compliance oversight
Physicians and allowed practitioners who conduct F2F encounters and provide required documentation
Revenue Cycle staff who must verify F2F compliance before claim submission
Medical Records staff who obtain and file F2F documentation
## 4. Policy Statement
4.1 Every patient admitted to Medicare home health services at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall have a qualifying face-to-face encounter documented and on file before the agency submits a final claim for the episode. The F2F encounter is a condition of Medicare payment — not a documentation preference.
4.2 The F2F encounter must have occurred within the following CMS-defined timeframe: no more than 90 calendar days before the SOC date, or no more than 30 calendar days after the SOC date. An encounter outside this window does not satisfy the F2F requirement, regardless of its clinical content.
4.3 The F2F encounter must be conducted by a qualifying practitioner — a physician (MD or DO), nurse practitioner (NP), clinical nurse specialist (CNS), or physician assistant (PA) working in collaboration with a physician. The encounter must have occurred in a context where the practitioner directly evaluated the patient — a telephone consultation is not a qualifying F2F encounter.
4.4 The certifying physician must review and sign the certification statement that includes the F2F encounter attestation. The certifying physician may not be the same individual who owns or directly supervises the home health agency (Stark Law prohibition).
4.5 The F2F encounter documentation must include: the date of the encounter; the practitioner's clinical findings that support the home health plan of care; and attestation that the encounter occurred and was related to the reason the patient requires home health care. The documentation must be authored by the practitioner who conducted the encounter — the agency's clinical notes cannot substitute for the practitioner's own documentation.
4.6 The agency shall not coach, instruct, or pressure physicians or their staff to write specific language in F2F documentation. The agency may provide educational materials explaining the CMS content requirements to physicians as a general resource, but shall not draft F2F documentation on behalf of physicians or request language that is not supported by the physician's independent clinical assessment.
4.7 The agency shall track F2F compliance for every active episode using the F2F Tracking System per CL-CA-007. No final claim shall be submitted for any episode without confirmed, compliant F2F documentation on file.
## 5. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Face-to-Face Encounter | A direct, in-person clinical evaluation of the patient conducted by a qualifying practitioner (physician, NP, CNS, or PA) that occurs within the CMS-defined timeframe relative to the SOC date. Telehealth encounters conducted using interactive audio-video technology may qualify as F2F encounters under current CMS rules — see Section 6.5. |
| Qualifying Practitioner | A physician (MD or DO), nurse practitioner (NP), clinical nurse specialist (CNS), or physician assistant (PA) working in collaboration with a physician, who is legally authorized to practice medicine and who conducted a direct patient evaluation. The certifying physician is typically the qualifying practitioner, but another practitioner who conducted the F2F may provide the encounter documentation to the certifying physician for review. |
| F2F Window | The CMS-defined timeframe within which the F2F encounter must have occurred: no more than 90 calendar days before the SOC date, or no more than 30 calendar days after the SOC date. |
| Attestation | The certifying physician's statement that the F2F encounter occurred, was conducted by the identified practitioner, and was related to the primary reason the patient requires home health services. |
| Episode | A 60-day certification period of Medicare home health services. Each episode requires a qualifying F2F encounter. |
| Certifying Physician | The physician who signs the certification (and recertification) of the patient's eligibility for home health services. This physician is responsible for reviewing the F2F encounter documentation and attesting to the encounter. |

## 6. Procedures
### 6.1 F2F Identification at Intake

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.1.1 | Intake / Clinical Coordinator | At the time of referral receipt, identify the patient's most recent encounter with a qualifying practitioner and whether that encounter falls within the F2F window relative to the anticipated SOC date. Document the encounter date, the practitioner's name and credentials, and the encounter setting (office, hospital, SNF, telehealth) in the intake record. | At referral receipt. |
| 6.1.2 | Intake / Clinical Coordinator | If no encounter within the F2F window is identified at intake, immediately notify the Director of Nursing and the referring physician. Assess whether a qualifying encounter can occur before or promptly after the SOC date. | At referral receipt if no qualifying encounter is identified. |
| 6.1.3 | Assigned RN | At the SOC visit, verify the F2F encounter status: confirm that the patient had a qualifying encounter within the F2F window, ask the patient and caregiver about recent physician visits or hospitalizations, and review any documentation from the referring encounter that was transmitted with the referral. | At the SOC visit. |

### 6.2 F2F Documentation Acquisition

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.2.1 | Clinical Coordinator / Medical Records | Within 5 business days of the SOC date, contact the qualifying practitioner's office to obtain the F2F encounter documentation. The request shall specify: the patient's name and date of birth; the date of the encounter; and the CMS content requirements for the documentation (date of encounter, clinical findings supporting home health, and attestation language). | Within 5 business days of SOC. |
| 6.2.2 | Medical Records | Acceptable F2F documentation includes: hospital discharge summary containing the encounter date, clinical findings, and physician signature; office visit notes from the qualifying practitioner; specialist consultation notes; or a CMS-compliant F2F encounter form completed and signed by the qualifying practitioner. A certification statement alone (without encounter documentation) is not sufficient. | At the time of documentation receipt. |
| 6.2.3 | Medical Records | Upon receipt of F2F documentation, verify that it meets all CMS content requirements per Section 4.5. If the documentation is incomplete — missing the encounter date, missing clinical findings, or lacking attestation — return it to the practitioner's office for completion before filing. Document all contacts with the practitioner's office in the F2F tracking system per CL-CA-007. | Within 3 business days of receipt. |
| 6.2.4 | Medical Records | File the complete, compliant F2F documentation in the patient's clinical record. Update the F2F Tracking System per CL-CA-007 to reflect receipt and verification. | Within 3 business days of receipt. |

### 6.3 F2F for Post-SOC Encounters (Encounter After SOC Date)

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.3.1 | Clinical Coordinator | If the F2F encounter occurs after the SOC date (within the 30-day post-SOC window), track the encounter date and monitor its occurrence through the F2F Tracking System per CL-CA-007. | From SOC date until the post-SOC encounter is documented. |
| 6.3.2 | Clinical Coordinator | If the 30-day post-SOC window is approaching without a qualifying encounter having occurred, notify the Director of Nursing at Day 20 post-SOC. The Director of Nursing shall contact the certifying physician to ensure a qualifying encounter is scheduled before Day 30. | Day 20 post-SOC if no qualifying encounter has occurred. |
| 6.3.3 | Director of Nursing | If no qualifying F2F encounter occurs within 30 days of the SOC and the F2F window closes without compliance, notify the Compliance Officer. The episode's claims may not be submitted until the F2F requirement is satisfied. If the window has closed without a qualifying encounter, consult the Compliance Officer regarding the disposition of any claims submitted for the episode. | Day 30 post-SOC if no qualifying encounter; Compliance Officer immediately. |

### 6.4 F2F Compliance Verification Before Claim Submission

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.4.1 | Revenue Cycle | Before submitting any final claim for a home health episode, verify that the F2F Tracking System shows compliant F2F documentation on file: the encounter is within the F2F window, the practitioner is a qualifying practitioner, and the documentation meets all CMS content requirements. | Before each final claim submission. |
| 6.4.2 | Revenue Cycle | If compliant F2F documentation is not on file at the time of claim submission preparation, place the episode on billing hold and notify the Director of Nursing and Medical Records immediately. Do not submit the claim without compliant F2F documentation. | At claim preparation; billing hold immediately if F2F is not compliant. |
| 6.4.3 | Director of Nursing | Upon notification of a billing hold for F2F non-compliance, assess whether the F2F requirement can still be satisfied (e.g., the encounter occurred but documentation has not been obtained) and coordinate immediate documentation acquisition. If the F2F window has closed and no qualifying encounter occurred, consult the Compliance Officer regarding the billing disposition. | Within 24 hours of billing hold notification. |

### 6.5 Telehealth F2F Encounters

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.5.1 | Clinical Coordinator / Medical Records | CMS has authorized certain telehealth encounters conducted using interactive audio-video technology as qualifying F2F encounters. When a patient's qualifying encounter was conducted via telehealth, verify: (a) the encounter used interactive, two-way audio-video communication (not telephone only); (b) the encounter was conducted by a qualifying practitioner; (c) the encounter falls within the F2F window; (d) the telehealth encounter is permitted under current CMS guidance for home health F2F purposes (CMS guidance on telehealth F2F may be updated — verify against the current CMS Home Health Benefit Manual). | At the time of F2F documentation acquisition. |
| 6.5.2 | Medical Records | Document the telehealth encounter type in the F2F Tracking System. Obtain documentation from the practitioner confirming the interactive audio-video nature of the encounter along with the standard F2F content requirements. | Per standard F2F documentation acquisition process. |

### 6.6 Escalation and Exception Handling

| Condition | Escalation Path | Corrective Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Patient was discharged from the hospital and no discharge summary with a qualifying encounter date is available within 5 business days | Medical Records and Director of Nursing | Request the discharge summary from the hospital records department. If unavailable within 14 calendar days of SOC, the Director of Nursing contacts the hospital's medical records department in writing. Consider requesting an office visit F2F encounter from the certifying physician within the 30-day post-SOC window as an alternative. | Escalation at Day 5; alternative encounter arranged by Day 20 if hospital records unavailable. |
| F2F documentation is received but is authored by a non-qualifying practitioner (e.g., a registered nurse, a social worker) | Medical Records returns the documentation | Request documentation authored or co-signed by a qualifying practitioner (MD, DO, NP, CNS, or PA). The agency shall not accept F2F documentation not authored by a qualifying practitioner. | Return and re-request within 24 hours of identification. |
| Certifying physician is the same individual who holds an ownership interest in the agency | Compliance Officer and Director of Nursing | The Stark Law prohibits the certifying physician from having a prohibited financial relationship with the home health agency. If such a relationship is identified, the Director of Nursing must identify an alternative certifying physician. Do not bill with a certifying physician in a prohibited financial relationship. | Immediate identification and resolution before billing. |
| Claims submitted without F2F documentation are identified through an ADR or audit | Revenue Cycle and Compliance Officer | Do not contest the denial if the F2F requirement was genuinely not met. Assess for overpayment and refund per FN-BC-004. Conduct a retrospective review of all episodes submitted without verified F2F documentation. | Overpayment assessment within 14 calendar days; refund within CMS 60-day timeline. |

## 7. Documentation Requirements

| Requirement | Document / Record | Responsible Party | Location | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| F2F encounter documentation | Hospital discharge summary, office visit note, consultation note, or CMS-compliant F2F form authored by qualifying practitioner | Certifying practitioner; Medical Records (filing) | EHR — clinical record | Obtained within 30 calendar days of SOC; on file before claim submission; retained minimum 7 years |
| F2F Tracking System entry | F2F encounter date, practitioner name/credentials, documentation status, compliance verification | Clinical Coordinator | CL-CA-007 F2F Tracking System | From SOC through documentation receipt |
| Revenue Cycle F2F verification | Pre-bill verification that F2F documentation is compliant and on file | Revenue Cycle | Revenue Cycle records | Before each final claim submission |
| Billing hold documentation | Record of billing hold and Director of Nursing/Compliance Officer notification | Revenue Cycle | Revenue Cycle records | At each hold event; retained minimum 7 years |
| Policy acknowledgment | Signed acknowledgment — Appendix A | Each individual; Administrator (collection) | Policy acknowledgment file | Within 14 calendar days |

## 8. Compliance & Audit Considerations
### 8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

| Compliance Indicator | Measurement Method | Acceptable Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Compliant F2F documentation on file before claim submission | Revenue Cycle pre-bill verification | 100% — zero claims submitted without compliant F2F |
| F2F documentation received within 30 calendar days of SOC | F2F Tracking System audit | ≥95% received within 30 calendar days |
| F2F documentation meets all CMS content requirements | Medical Records verification review | 100% of filed F2F documentation meets content requirements |
| F2F within the allowable window for all episodes | F2F Tracking System audit | 100% |

### 8.2 What Surveyors and Auditors Will Look For
ADR auditors examining F2F compliance will: verify that F2F documentation exists for the episode; verify the encounter date falls within the F2F window; verify the practitioner is a qualifying practitioner; and verify the documentation contains the required clinical findings and attestation. The absence of a qualifying practitioner's note — and substitution of the agency's clinical documentation — is an immediate denial. Surveyors will also verify that the certifying physician does not have a prohibited financial relationship with the agency.
### 8.3 Common Failure Points

| Failure Point | Risk | Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| F2F documentation is a certification statement alone without encounter documentation | ADR denial; episode not payable | Train medical records staff to obtain practitioner encounter notes, not just certification forms |
| F2F encounter conducted by an NP but certifying physician is different — no attestation that physician reviewed | Incomplete F2F compliance | Obtain physician attestation of review on all F2F documents authored by non-physician practitioners |
| F2F window missed because no encounter occurred within 30 days post-SOC | Episode not payable | Day 20 alert in F2F Tracking System; Director of Nursing arranges encounter before Day 30 |

## 2. Purpose
This policy defines the operational tracking system for face-to-face (F2F) encounter documentation at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc., including status dashboards, expiration alerts, escalation timelines, and accountability for preventing lapses that result in claim denials. The clinical requirements for F2F compliance are defined in CL-CA-006. This policy provides the operational infrastructure that makes those requirements executable — the tracking system that ensures no F2F deadline is missed, no compliant documentation requirement slips through without verification, and no claim is submitted without the billing team having confirmed F2F compliance on a patient-by-patient, episode-by-episode basis.
Without a systematic F2F tracking program, F2F compliance depends on the individual memory and diligence of intake staff, medical records coordinators, and revenue cycle staff — an inherently unreliable system that scales poorly as the agency's patient census grows. The F2F tracking system described in this policy replaces individual reliance with a structured, automated, status-visible workflow that generates alerts at defined milestones, assigns accountability at each stage, and creates an auditable record of every F2F compliance action taken for every episode.
## 3. Scope
This policy applies to:
Clinical Coordinators who manage the F2F Tracking System daily
Medical Records staff who obtain and verify F2F documentation
The Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager who reviews F2F compliance status weekly
Revenue Cycle staff who perform pre-bill F2F verification
The Compliance Officer who oversees F2F compliance integrity
## 4. Policy Statement
4.1 The agency shall maintain a centralized F2F Tracking System (electronic, within the EHR or a dedicated tracking tool) that captures and displays the F2F compliance status of every active home health episode in real time.
4.2 Every new episode shall be entered into the F2F Tracking System within 24 hours of the SOC date, with all required data fields per Section 6.1. No episode shall be excluded from the tracking system.
4.3 The F2F Tracking System shall generate automated alerts at the following milestones: (a) Day 20 post-SOC — if F2F documentation has not been received and a post-SOC encounter is being relied upon to satisfy the requirement; (b) Day 25 post-SOC — escalation alert to Director of Nursing if F2F documentation is still not received; (c) Day 28 post-SOC — Administrator escalation if F2F documentation is still not received; (d) 5 business days after any SOC — alert if F2F documentation request has not been initiated.
4.4 The F2F Tracking System shall maintain a clear, real-time status display for every episode, categorized as: (a) F2F Compliant — qualifying encounter confirmed within window; compliant documentation received and filed; (b) F2F Pending — qualifying encounter identified; documentation requested but not yet received; (c) F2F At Risk — Day 20+ post-SOC; post-SOC encounter not yet occurred or documentation not received; (d) F2F Non-Compliant — window has closed without a qualifying encounter; claims for this episode shall not be submitted.
4.5 The Director of Nursing shall review the F2F Tracking System dashboard at minimum weekly and shall report F2F compliance status to the Administrator monthly and to the Governing Body quarterly.
4.6 Revenue Cycle shall not submit any claim for any episode that is not in F2F Compliant status in the tracking system. The F2F Tracking System status shall be a mandatory field in the pre-bill checklist.
## 5. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| F2F Tracking System | The agency's centralized electronic system for monitoring F2F compliance status for every active episode, generating milestone alerts, and maintaining an auditable record of all F2F actions. |
| F2F Compliant Status | The episode status indicating that a qualifying F2F encounter has occurred within the CMS window, compliant documentation has been received and verified, and the episode is cleared for billing. |
| F2F Pending Status | The episode status indicating that a qualifying F2F encounter has been identified but documentation has not yet been received. Active follow-up is in progress. |
| F2F At Risk Status | The episode status indicating that Day 20 post-SOC has passed without receipt of compliant F2F documentation, or that no qualifying encounter has been confirmed, triggering escalated follow-up. |
| F2F Non-Compliant Status | The episode status indicating that the F2F window has closed without a qualifying encounter occurring or compliant documentation being obtained. The episode's claims are not payable under Medicare. |
| Milestone Alert | An automated notification generated by the F2F Tracking System at a defined date that triggers a specific accountability action. |
| Pre-Bill F2F Verification | The mandatory check performed by Revenue Cycle before each claim submission confirming that the episode is in F2F Compliant status in the tracking system. |

## 6. Procedures
### 6.1 F2F Tracking System — New Episode Entry

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.1.1 | Clinical Coordinator | Within 24 hours of every SOC, create a new episode entry in the F2F Tracking System with the following required data fields: (a) patient name and MR#; (b) SOC date; (c) certifying physician name and NPI; (d) F2F window start date (90 days before SOC) and end date (30 days after SOC); (e) qualifying encounter date (if known at intake); (f) encounter practitioner name and credentials; (g) encounter type (hospital discharge, office visit, SNF visit, telehealth); (h) documentation request date; (i) documentation receipt date; (j) documentation compliance verification status; (k) current episode F2F status (Pending, Compliant, At Risk, Non-Compliant). | Within 24 hours of SOC. |
| 6.1.2 | Clinical Coordinator | If the qualifying encounter has already been identified at intake (e.g., patient was recently discharged from the hospital and the discharge summary is available), enter the encounter date and set the status to "F2F Pending — Documentation Requested" immediately. Initiate documentation acquisition per CL-CA-006 Section 6.2. | Within 24 hours of SOC. |
| 6.1.3 | Clinical Coordinator | If no qualifying encounter has been identified at intake, set the status to "F2F At Risk" immediately. Notify the Director of Nursing and initiate the post-SOC encounter coordination process per CL-CA-006 Section 6.3. | Within 24 hours of SOC if no encounter identified. |

### 6.2 F2F Tracking System — Daily Management

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.2.1 | Clinical Coordinator | Review the F2F Tracking System dashboard daily to identify: (a) new milestone alerts triggered (Day 20, Day 25, Day 28); (b) episodes that have changed status (new documentation received, window closing); (c) any episode that should have moved to F2F Compliant but has not been updated. | Daily by 9:00 AM. |
| 6.2.2 | Clinical Coordinator | For all episodes in F2F Pending status, confirm the documentation request is active. If a documentation request has been outstanding for more than 10 business days without receipt, initiate a follow-up contact with the practitioner's office. Document the follow-up in the tracking system. | Daily review; follow-up at 10 business days. |
| 6.2.3 | Clinical Coordinator | For all episodes in F2F At Risk status, verify that escalation steps per Section 6.3 are active and documented. If an At Risk episode reaches Day 28 without resolution, confirm that the Administrator escalation has occurred. | Daily for all At Risk episodes. |
| 6.2.4 | Medical Records | Upon receipt of F2F documentation for any episode, immediately update the F2F Tracking System with the receipt date and initiate the documentation compliance verification. If the documentation passes verification, update the status to F2F Compliant. If it does not pass verification, retain the Pending or At Risk status and document the deficiency. | Within 24 hours of documentation receipt. |

### 6.3 Milestone Alert Management and Escalation

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.3.1 | Clinical Coordinator | Day 5 Post-SOC Alert — if F2F documentation has not been requested by Day 5, initiate the documentation acquisition request per CL-CA-006 Section 6.2. Document the request in the tracking system. | Day 5 post-SOC. |
| 6.3.2 | Clinical Coordinator | Day 20 Post-SOC Alert — if F2F documentation has not been received and the qualifying encounter was intended to occur post-SOC, contact the certifying physician's office by telephone to verify: (a) the patient has or will have a qualifying encounter before Day 30; (b) the encounter documentation will be transmitted to the agency before Day 30. Document the contact, the physician's confirmation, and the scheduled encounter date if provided. | Day 20 post-SOC. |
| 6.3.3 | Director of Nursing | Day 25 Post-SOC Alert — the Director of Nursing is automatically notified of all episodes reaching Day 25 without F2F Compliant status. The Director of Nursing shall directly contact the certifying physician to confirm the qualifying encounter will occur and documentation will be transmitted before Day 30. Document all communications. | Day 25 post-SOC. |
| 6.3.4 | Administrator | Day 28 Post-SOC Alert — if F2F documentation is still not received by Day 28, the Administrator is notified. The Administrator contacts the physician practice administration to expedite. The Administrator and Director of Nursing assess whether services should continue past Day 30 given the F2F non-compliance risk. The Compliance Officer is notified. | Day 28 post-SOC. |
| 6.3.5 | Compliance Officer | Day 30 Post-SOC — if no qualifying encounter has occurred and the F2F window closes, the Compliance Officer confirms the episode is marked Non-Compliant in the tracking system. Revenue Cycle is notified that no claim may be submitted for this episode. The Compliance Officer assesses whether any claims already submitted for the episode require refund per FN-BC-004. | Day 30 post-SOC if no qualifying encounter. |

### 6.4 Documentation Compliance Verification

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.4.1 | Medical Records | Upon receipt of any F2F documentation, complete the F2F Documentation Verification Checklist (Appendix A): (a) ☐ Documentation is authored or co-signed by a qualifying practitioner (MD, DO, NP, CNS, or PA); (b) ☐ The encounter date is documented; (c) ☐ The encounter date falls within the F2F window (90 days pre-SOC or 30 days post-SOC); (d) ☐ Clinical findings relevant to the home health plan of care are documented; (e) ☐ Attestation that the encounter occurred and was related to the home health diagnosis is present or is contained in the physician certification; (f) ☐ The documentation is not an agency-authored note substituting for the practitioner's own documentation. | Within 24 hours of documentation receipt. |
| 6.4.2 | Medical Records | If the documentation passes all checklist items, mark the episode as F2F Compliant in the tracking system. File the documentation in the clinical record. Notify Revenue Cycle that the episode is cleared for billing. | Within 24 hours of verification. |
| 6.4.3 | Medical Records | If the documentation fails any checklist item, document the specific deficiency, retain the episode status as Pending or At Risk, and return the documentation to the practitioner's office with a specific request for correction or completion. Document the return and the specific requested corrections. | Within 24 hours of identification of deficiency. |

### 6.5 Weekly Director of Nursing Review

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.5.1 | Director of Nursing | Each week, review the complete F2F Tracking System dashboard and generate the Weekly F2F Status Report (Appendix B). The report shall display: (a) total active episodes by F2F status category; (b) all episodes in At Risk or Non-Compliant status with individual escalation plans; (c) all milestone alerts triggered in the prior week and actions taken; (d) documentation received in the prior week and compliance verification status. | Weekly; report generated by end of business each Monday. |
| 6.5.2 | Director of Nursing | For every episode in At Risk or Non-Compliant status, document the specific action being taken and the expected resolution date. | At weekly review. |
| 6.5.3 | Director of Nursing | Report a summary of F2F compliance status — total active episodes, F2F Compliant percentage, Non-Compliant episodes and their billing status — to the Administrator monthly. Include in the monthly report any episodes for which claims were placed on billing hold due to F2F non-compliance and the financial impact. | Monthly. |

### 6.6 Pre-Bill F2F Verification Integration

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.6.1 | Revenue Cycle | For every episode being prepared for final claim submission, access the F2F Tracking System and confirm the episode status is F2F Compliant. This verification shall be documented in the Revenue Cycle pre-bill checklist per FN-BC-001. | Before each final claim submission. |
| 6.6.2 | Revenue Cycle | If the episode status in the F2F Tracking System is not F2F Compliant, immediately place the episode on billing hold and notify the Clinical Coordinator and Director of Nursing. Do not submit the claim and do not assume the status will be resolved without active follow-up. | At claim preparation; billing hold immediately. |
| 6.6.3 | Revenue Cycle | Maintain a Billing Hold Log documenting every episode placed on billing hold for F2F non-compliance, including: the episode dates, the reason for the hold, the resolution actions taken, and the claim submission date once F2F compliance is achieved. | Updated at each billing hold event; retained minimum 7 years. |

### 6.7 Escalation and Exception Handling

| Condition | Escalation Path | Corrective Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| F2F Tracking System data entry error — wrong SOC date or wrong encounter date entered | Clinical Coordinator identifies; corrects and notifies Director of Nursing | Correct the tracking system entry immediately. Assess whether the error affected any billing hold decisions. If a claim was submitted during a period of inaccurate tracking data, review with Compliance Officer. | Correction within 24 hours; Compliance Officer review within 48 hours if billing was affected. |
| Multiple episodes approaching Non-Compliant status simultaneously — volume surge | Director of Nursing and Administrator | Administrator authorizes temporary additional administrative support for F2F documentation acquisition. Director of Nursing prioritizes episodes by SOC date proximity to the F2F window deadline. | Resource assessment within 24 hours of identification. |
| Physician's office refuses to provide F2F documentation | Director of Nursing and Administrator | Administrator contacts the physician practice administration in writing, explaining the CMS requirement and the consequence to the patient's episode. If the refusal persists, consult Legal Counsel. The episode shall not be billed without compliant documentation. | Written contact within 5 business days of refusal. |
| Claims submitted for Non-Compliant episodes are identified through an audit | Compliance Officer and Revenue Cycle | Immediate halt of further billing for the affected episodes. Compliance Officer assesses for overpayment per FN-BC-004. Voluntary refund within the 60-day CMS timeline if overpayment is confirmed. | Immediate halt; overpayment assessment within 14 calendar days. |

| Requirement | Document / Record | Responsible Party | Location | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| F2F Tracking System — episode entries | Complete entry for every active episode with all required data fields | Clinical Coordinator | F2F Tracking System | Within 24 hours of SOC; updated continuously |
| F2F Documentation Verification Checklist | Completed checklist for every F2F document received | Medical Records | F2F Tracking System and clinical record | Within 24 hours of documentation receipt; retained minimum 7 years |
| Milestone alert responses | Documentation of actions taken at each alert milestone | Clinical Coordinator / Director of Nursing / Administrator | F2F Tracking System | At each milestone; retained minimum 7 years |
| Weekly F2F Status Report | Director of Nursing weekly compliance review | Director of Nursing | Director of Nursing supervisory file | Weekly; retained minimum 7 years |
| Revenue Cycle Billing Hold Log | Record of every episode on F2F billing hold | Revenue Cycle | Revenue Cycle records | At each hold event; retained minimum 7 years |
| Monthly F2F compliance report to Administrator | Summary of F2F status, Non-Compliant episodes, financial impact | Director of Nursing | Administrator file | Monthly |
| Policy acknowledgment | Signed acknowledgment — Appendix C | Each individual; Administrator (collection) | Policy acknowledgment file | Within 14 calendar days |

## 8. Compliance & Audit Considerations
### 8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

| Compliance Indicator | Measurement Method | Acceptable Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| All episodes entered in F2F Tracking System within 24 hours of SOC | Tracking System audit vs. SOC dates | 100% |
| F2F Compliant status achieved before claim submission for all episodes | Pre-bill verification audit | 100% — zero claims submitted for Non-Compliant episodes |
| Milestone alerts actioned within the required timeframe | Tracking System milestone log audit | ≥95% |
| F2F documentation verification completed within 24 hours of receipt | Tracking System receipt-to-verification timestamps | ≥95% |
| Weekly Director of Nursing F2F review completed | Review log audit | 100% weekly |

### 8.2 What Surveyors and Auditors Will Look For
ADR auditors will request the agency's F2F documentation for each episode under review. A robust, auditable F2F Tracking System demonstrates to auditors that the agency has an active F2F compliance program — not that the agency simply got lucky finding documentation when asked. Surveyors will also verify that the pre-bill verification process is active and documented.
### 8.3 Common Failure Points

| Failure Point | Risk | Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No centralized tracking — F2F status managed by individual staff memory | High-volume environments produce F2F failures at scale | Mandatory centralized tracking system; daily review; automated alerts |
| Milestone alerts generated but not actioned | Alerts without accountability are meaningless | Each alert assigned a specific responsible party with documented response requirement |
| Revenue Cycle submits claims without verifying F2F Tracking System status | Non-compliant claims submitted | F2F Tracking System status is a mandatory field in the pre-bill checklist; supervisor approval required to bypass |

# CL-CD-001 — Clinical Documentation Standards
## 1. Policy Header

| Field | Value |

| Domain | CL — Clinical Operations |
| Subdomain | CD — Clinical Documentation |
| Classification Tier | REQUIRED |
| Status | ACTIVE |
| Review Cycle | Annual |
| Access Tier | Tier 2 — Restricted |
| Policy Owner / Steward | Director of Nursing |
| Effective Date | 2025-07-10 |

| Last Reviewed | 2025-07-10 |
| Next Review Date | 2026-07-10 |
| Supersedes | N/A (Initial Version) |

## 2. Purpose
This policy establishes the minimum standards for clinical documentation content, timeliness, accuracy, and authentication for all clinical records at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. Clinical documentation is not administrative paperwork — it is the legal, clinical, and financial record of every professional act performed for every patient on every visit. It is simultaneously: the clinical record that governs the next clinician's decisions; the legal record that defines the agency's liability in litigation; the regulatory record that determines whether a CMS surveyor finds compliance or a deficiency; the billing record that justifies every Medicare payment; and the quality record that drives every QAPI improvement decision.
Documentation failures in home health are the single most consequential category of compliance failure. An undocumented clinical finding might as well not have occurred — legally and regulatorily, it did not. A visit note that does not demonstrate the skilled nature of the services provided is not a billable visit under Medicare, regardless of what the clinician actually did. A plan of care modification that is not reflected in the clinical record may be a billing compliance failure. Documentation that is not authenticated within required timeframes is not a completed record. Documentation that is altered without proper notation is a falsification. Documentation that contradicts itself across the record undermines the entire episode's clinical and billing integrity.
This policy establishes the universal clinical documentation standards that govern every clinical record entry at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc., regardless of the discipline creating the entry, the type of visit, or the service delivered. Discipline-specific documentation requirements that supplement these universal standards are addressed in the respective discipline policies (CL-SD-001 through CL-SD-025) and the OASIS-specific documentation requirements are addressed in CL-OA-001 through CL-OA-019. This policy implements 42 CFR § 484.110 (Condition of Participation: Clinical Records) and CMS documentation standards established in the Home Health Benefit Manual and State Operations Manual.
## 3. Scope
This policy applies to:
All registered nurses (RNs) creating clinical record entries
All licensed vocational nurses (LVNs) creating clinical record entries
All physical therapists (PTs) and physical therapist assistants (PTAs) creating clinical record entries
All occupational therapists (OTs) and certified occupational therapy assistants (COTAs) creating clinical record entries
All speech-language pathologists (SLPs) creating clinical record entries
All medical social workers (MSWs) creating clinical record entries
All home health aides (HHAs) creating visit documentation
The Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager responsible for documentation quality oversight
Medical Records staff responsible for clinical record management
The Compliance Officer responsible for documentation integrity oversight
This policy governs all entries in the patient's clinical record — visit notes, assessment documents, care coordination notes, physician communication notes, OASIS assessments, plan of care documents, and any other record that becomes part of the patient's permanent clinical record.
## 4. Policy Statement
4.1 Every entry in a patient's clinical record shall be: accurate — reflecting what was actually observed, assessed, performed, and communicated; complete — containing all required elements for the type of entry; timely — created within the timeframe specified for the entry type; legible — clearly readable in the format used (electronic or written); authenticated — identified with the author's name, credential, date, and time; and consistent — aligned with all related entries in the clinical record.
4.2 Every clinical record entry shall be individualized to the specific patient, the specific visit, and the specific clinical situation. Template-driven documentation that does not reflect the actual clinical encounter is prohibited. Copy-forward of prior entries without independent verification and documentation of the current status is prohibited, except as specifically authorized by the EHR workflow and where the copied content is explicitly verified as current at the time of copying.
4.3 Every visit note shall demonstrate the skilled nature of the service provided — specifically documenting why the service required the training, skill, and judgment of a licensed clinician. Visit notes that describe only routine observations, vital signs, or equipment checks without demonstrating clinical reasoning, skilled assessment, or skilled intervention do not support Medicare billing for skilled services.
4.4 Clinical record entries shall be made promptly after the visit or clinical event — the agency's maximum timeframe for visit note completion and locking is 24 hours after the visit, as defined in CL-CD-004. Notes made significantly after the clinical event are subject to the late entry standards defined in CO-DC-003.
4.5 All clinical record entries shall be authenticated by the clinician who performed the service. Authentication means the clinician signs the entry (physically or electronically) with their full name and credential (e.g., Jane Smith, RN), and the date and time of the entry are documented. Unsigned entries are not valid record entries.
4.6 Corrections to clinical record entries shall be made using the standards defined in CO-DC-003 (Late Entry, Correction & Amendment Standards). No entry shall be obliterated, deleted, or altered in a manner that conceals the original content. Electronic record alterations shall maintain an audit trail showing the original content, the change, the date, time, and identity of the person making the change.
4.7 The clinical record is the agency's primary tool for demonstrating the medical necessity, skilled nature, and appropriateness of all services billed to Medicare. Revenue Cycle shall not submit a claim for any visit or service that is not supported by a completed, authenticated, and medically necessary visit note in the patient's clinical record.
4.8 All clinical record entries shall respect patient privacy and confidentiality per HIPAA requirements and agency policy CO-HP-001. Entries shall not contain information about other patients, providers, or third parties that is not directly relevant to the patient's care.
## 5. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Clinical Record | The complete, permanent collection of all clinical documentation for a patient — encompassing assessments, visit notes, care coordination records, physician orders, OASIS data, plan of care documents, and all other records created in connection with the patient's home health episode. |
| Visit Note | The clinical documentation entry created by a clinician for each patient visit, documenting the patient's status, the clinical services provided, the patient's response, education delivered, and the plan for follow-up. |
| Authentication | The process by which an entry in the clinical record is identified as the work of a specific clinician, accomplished by the clinician's signature (electronic or physical) including their name, credential, and the date and time of entry. |
| Timeliness | The requirement that clinical record entries be completed within a defined timeframe after the clinical event — the agency's standard is 24 hours for visit notes, per CL-CD-004. |
| Skilled Documentation | Documentation that demonstrates why the services provided required the training, skill, and professional judgment of a licensed clinician — the clinical reasoning and professional judgment that distinguishes skilled care from maintenance or custodial care. |
| Medical Necessity | The clinical justification for a service — documentation that the service was reasonable and necessary for the treatment of the patient's illness or injury, consistent with generally accepted medical practice. |
| Copy-Forward | The practice of duplicating content from a prior clinical record entry into a current entry. Prohibited unless the clinician independently verifies the copied content as accurate at the time of the current entry. |
| Electronic Health Record (EHR) | The agency's certified electronic clinical record system used to create, store, authenticate, and retrieve all patient clinical records. |
| Audit Trail | The electronic log maintained by the EHR system that records all access to and changes in patient clinical records, including the identity of the accessor or author, the date and time of access, and the content of any change made. |
| Legibility | The quality of documentation that makes it readable and understandable by any qualified clinician who reviews the record — in electronic records, this refers to entries that are clearly written, free from undefined abbreviations, and logically organized. |

## 6. Procedures
### 6.1 General Clinical Documentation Requirements — All Disciplines

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.1.1 | All Clinicians | Every visit note and clinical record entry shall be individualized to the specific patient and the specific visit. Before beginning a visit note, do not copy forward any prior note. Start from the current clinical encounter and document what was observed, assessed, and done at this visit, for this patient, today. | At each visit. |
| 6.1.2 | All Clinicians | Every visit note shall be written in specific, clinical, observation-based language. Avoid vague terms that do not communicate meaningful clinical information: "patient doing well," "no changes noted," "patient tolerates," "stable," "routine visit," "nursing visit." These phrases, without specific clinical context, do not demonstrate skilled care. | At each visit. |
| 6.1.3 | All Clinicians | Every visit note shall include the following universal required elements: (a) date and time of the visit; (b) the specific clinical purpose of the visit — why this visit was necessary today; (c) subjective data — what the patient and caregiver reported since the last visit; (d) objective data — specific clinical findings from the assessment, including all relevant measurements and observations; (e) assessment — the clinician's professional judgment and clinical reasoning about the patient's current status, response to treatment, and trajectory; (f) plan — interventions provided, education delivered, coordination actions taken, and the plan for the next visit; (g) goal progress — specific, measurable notation of progress toward each active plan of care goal (progressing, plateaued, regressed, goal met); (h) authentication — clinician's full name, credential, and the date and time of entry. | In every visit note. |
| 6.1.4 | All Clinicians | Document goal progress using the same measurement units and methods established at SOC. If the goal was "patient will ambulate 50 feet without rest," document the actual distance ambulated and the level of assistance — not "patient is improving with ambulation." Measurable progress documentation enables objective evaluation of the patient's trajectory and the effectiveness of the care plan. | In every visit note. |
| 6.1.5 | All Clinicians | Document all clinical communications relevant to the visit: physician contacts (including the specific information communicated and the physician's response); contacts with other disciplines; contacts with the caregiver; and any referrals initiated. These communications are part of the clinical record and may not be omitted from the visit note. | In the visit note for the day of the communication. |
| 6.1.6 | All Clinicians | Use only approved abbreviations in clinical record entries. The agency shall maintain an Approved Abbreviation List (Appendix A) — abbreviations not on the approved list shall not be used. Undefined abbreviations that could be misread (e.g., "qd" interpreted as either "every day" or "4 times a day") are prohibited. | At all times. |

### 6.2 Demonstrating Skilled Care in Documentation
This section provides the agency's standards for documentation that demonstrates the skilled nature of clinical services. These standards supplement the discipline-specific documentation requirements in CL-SD-001 through CL-SD-025.

| Documentation Element | Standard for Skilled Documentation | Example of Skilled Documentation | Example of Non-Skilled Documentation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Assessment findings | Document specific clinical findings with quantitative measurements or standardized scale scores | "BP 168/94 sitting; HR 88 irregular; SpO2 88% on 2L NC; bilateral LE edema 3+ to mid-calf; lung auscultation — bibasilar crackles; weight 184.6 lbs, up 3.2 lbs from 3 days prior" | "VS stable; lungs clear; patient OK" |
| Clinical reasoning | Document the clinician's professional interpretation of findings and their significance | "Weight gain of 3.2 lbs in 3 days combined with increased LE edema and bibasilar crackles represents early decompensation pattern consistent with CHF exacerbation; physician notification required per the care plan parameters" | "Weight gained, noted edema" |
| Intervention justification | Document why the specific intervention required the skills of a licensed clinician | "Complex wound care performed to the left heel Stage 3 pressure injury: sharp debridement of 1.5 cm × 0.8 cm area of adherent slough using sterile forceps and scissors; wound irrigated with NS; Medihoney antimicrobial gel applied; DSD applied; wound dimensions now 3.2 × 2.4 × 0.6 cm — decreased from 3.5 × 2.8 × 0.8 cm at last visit, representing measurable wound healing" | "Wound care done per orders; wound looks better" |
| Patient response | Document the patient's actual response to interventions with measurable outcomes | "Patient tolerated wound care procedure with pain rated 4/10 at initiation, decreasing to 2/10 at procedure end; no bleeding; no adverse reactions; patient verbally reported less pain than prior wound care visit" | "Patient tolerated procedure well" |
| Education delivery | Document specific topic, method, content taught, and teach-back result | "Educated patient on signs of CHF decompensation using teach-back: asked patient to name 3 warning signs requiring agency notification — patient correctly identified weight gain >2 lbs, increased ankle swelling, and increased shortness of breath. Also reviewed sodium restriction — patient correctly stated daily limit of 2,000 mg and identified 3 high-sodium foods to avoid" | "Patient educated on CHF management; patient verbalized understanding" |

### 6.3 Documentation Integrity Standards

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.3.1 | All Clinicians | Never document care that was not provided. Never document observations that were not made. Clinical record entries must reflect what actually occurred at the visit — not what was planned, not what is typically done, and not what would look better. False documentation is fraud regardless of clinical intent. | At all times. |
| 6.3.2 | All Clinicians | Never falsify, backdate, or pre-date clinical entries. The date and time of every entry shall reflect the actual date and time the entry was created. If a note is created after the visit date, it shall be documented as a late entry per CO-DC-003 — including the date of the actual visit, the reason for the late entry, and the date the entry was created. | At all times. |
| 6.3.3 | All Clinicians | Never alter a previously authenticated entry to change its clinical meaning without using the late entry/correction process per CO-DC-003. The audit trail in the EHR must be preserved — any change to an authenticated entry must maintain the original content and document the change, the reason for the change, and the identity and date of the person making the change. | At all times. |
| 6.3.4 | All Clinicians | Documentation shall be internally consistent — within a single visit note and across the full clinical record. A visit note that documents the patient as "independent in ambulation" while the assessment recorded "patient required standby assist for ambulation" is internally inconsistent and constitutes a documentation integrity failure. Clinicians shall review their entries for internal consistency before authenticating. | Before authentication of each entry. |

### 6.4 Visit Note Authentication

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.4.1 | All Clinicians | Authenticate every visit note and clinical record entry by applying the electronic signature in the EHR. Authentication includes: (a) the clinician's full legal name; (b) professional credential (RN, LVN, PT, OT, SLP, MSW, HHA); (c) the date and time of authentication. | Before or at the time of entry submission in the EHR. |
| 6.4.2 | All Clinicians | Review the complete visit note for accuracy, completeness, and internal consistency before authenticating. Once authenticated, the note is a permanent part of the clinical record. Authentication without review is an attestation that an unreviewed note is accurate — do not authenticate without reviewing. | Before each authentication. |
| 6.4.3 | Supervising RN (for LVN and HHA entries) | Co-signature by a supervising RN is required for certain LVN and HHA documentation per the respective scope of practice standards and agency supervision policies (CL-SD-001 for LVNs, CL-SD-006 for HHAs). The co-signature shall be applied within 14 calendar days of the entry date. | Within 14 calendar days of the entry date for required co-signatures. |

### 6.5 Director of Nursing Documentation Quality Oversight

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.5.1 | Director of Nursing | Conduct a monthly clinical documentation audit per CO-DC-002 covering a random sample of ≥5% of all visit notes from the prior month. The audit shall assess: (a) presence of all required universal elements per Section 6.1.3; (b) individualization — no copy-forward or template language; (c) skilled documentation — clear demonstration of skilled care and medical necessity; (d) goal progress documentation — specific and measurable; (e) authentication completeness; (f) consistency with related clinical record entries; (g) timeliness per CL-CD-004 standards. | Monthly. |
| 6.5.2 | Director of Nursing | Document audit findings in the Documentation Quality Dashboard (Appendix B) by discipline and by individual clinician. Identify documentation deficiencies by category and frequency. | Within 5 business days of audit completion. |
| 6.5.3 | Director of Nursing | Provide individual written feedback to each clinician with identified documentation deficiencies, including specific examples from the audited records, the applicable standard, and the required correction. | Within 14 calendar days of audit completion. |
| 6.5.4 | Director of Nursing | For any clinician with a documentation quality score below 80% on any category in any month, initiate targeted documentation retraining within 14 calendar days and schedule a follow-up audit within 30 calendar days. | Within 14 calendar days of audit completion. |
| 6.5.5 | Director of Nursing | Present documentation quality audit results to the QAPI Committee quarterly, identifying trends, systemic issues, and improvement actions. | Quarterly QAPI meeting. |

### 6.6 Escalation and Exception Handling

| Condition | Escalation Path | Corrective Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A visit note is identified as documenting care that the clinician could not have provided (e.g., visit note completed when the patient reports no visit occurred; visit note completed from the office without the visit having occurred) | Director of Nursing and Compliance Officer | Compliance Officer initiates a compliance investigation per CO-CP-007. Do not alter or delete the documentation pending investigation. Document all facts as discovered. If billing has occurred for the falsified visit, assess for overpayment and potential self-disclosure. | Investigation initiated within 24 hours. |
| Copy-forward documentation identified — visit notes for multiple consecutive visits are identical | Director of Nursing identifies during audit | Director of Nursing directs the clinician to amend all copy-forward notes using the late entry/correction process per CO-DC-003. Provides corrective training. Reports pattern to Compliance Officer if billing has been submitted. | Amendment within 14 calendar days; Compliance Officer notification if billing affected. |
| Visit note does not support the skilled nature of the service — may not be billable | Director of Nursing identifies during audit | Director of Nursing and Revenue Cycle assess whether the visit can be supported as skilled based on the available clinical record. If the visit cannot be supported, do not bill for it or retract the claim if already submitted. Provide documentation coaching to the clinician. | Assessment within 5 business days; billing decision within 10 business days. |
| Clinician refuses to authenticate a note | Director of Nursing | Director of Nursing investigates the reason. If the clinician refuses because the note is inaccurate, the note must be corrected before authentication per CO-DC-003. If the clinician refuses for other reasons, document the refusal and initiate HR action per HR-ER-002. | Investigation within 24 hours; HR referral if refusal persists. |
